units.tr: The relative αὐτός is placed after every person: ἐμοῦ αὐτὸς ἀκούω, "I hear myself" (memet audio); σοῦ αὐτὸς ἀκούω, "I hear you yourself"; ἐκεῖνος αὐτὸς λέγει, "he himself says." In Luke 2: "σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τῆς ψυχῆς διελεύσεται ῥομφαία" ["but a sword will pierce through your very soul, or your own soul"].

units.la: Genitiuus pluralis αὐτῶν postponi-tur frequenter huic nomini ἰδίου, ἰδίοις αὐτῶν ἀγαθοῖς, suis propriis bonis. Quomodo etiam dixerūt ueteres Latini, suo sibi gladio hunc iugulo.
units.tr: The genitive plural αὐτῶν is often placed after the noun ἴδιος: ἰδίοις αὐτῶν ἀγαθοῖς, "with their own proper goods." In the same way the older Latins said suo sibi gladio hunc iugulo, "I cut this man's throat with his own sword."

units.la: Et ponitur αὐτὸς quandoque loco reciproci, Grego. ὁρῶν ἐν τλῷ τῇ δήμῳ κίνη- σιν ἐπ' αὐτὸν, Vídens igitur in se motum populi ἐπ' αὐτὸν, posuit pro ἐφ' ἑαυτόν.
units.tr: Sometimes αὐτός is used in place of the reflexive. Gregory: "ὁρῶν ἐν τῷ τότε τῇ δήμῳ κίνησιν ἐπ' αὐτόν" ["seeing then the movement of the people against himself"], where ἐπ' αὐτόν stands for ἐπ' ἑαυτόν.

units.la: Et contra reciprocum pro relatiuo, ὡς ὅπου ἂν ἐξὸν ἑαυτῷ ποιεῖν, tanquam ipsi quicquid libet liceat. Vbi ἑαυτῷ, pro αὐτῷ ponitur.
units.tr: Conversely, the reflexive is used for the relative: "ὡς ὅπου ἂν ἐξῇ ἑαυτῷ ποιεῖν" ["as if it were allowed to him to do whatever he likes"], where ἑαυτῷ is put for αὐτῷ.

units.la: Sic ὅς, ἕ, οἵ, ἑ, modo reciproce, modo non reciproce accipiuntur. Reciproce, τοιαῦτα οἱ συνειδὼς ἄλλοις ἑαυτῷ talium sibi conscius est malorū. Non reciproce, Greg. ἐπειδὴ οἱ φανλῶν πλῆθος πολύ, Postquā ingens uisa est ei multitudo.
units.tr: So ὅς, ἥ, οἵ, αἳ are sometimes taken reflexively and sometimes not. Reflexively: "τοιαῦτα οἱ συνειδὼς ἄλλοις ἑαυτῷ" ["conscious to himself of such evils"]. Non-reflexively, Gregory: "ἐπειδὴ οἱ φανῆναι πλῆθος πολύ" ["after a great multitude appeared to him"].

units.la: Sic σφὰς pro seipsos, uel pro eos ponunt: σφισὶν, pro sibīpsīs, uel pro ipsīs.
units.tr: Likewise σφᾶς is used for themselves or for them, and σφισίν for to themselves or to them.

units.la: Compositá.
units.tr: Compounds.

units.la: Pronomina composita possunt diuisim construi, in prima quidem persona & secunda singulariter tantum, & in tertia pluraliter tantum. Verū dum cōposite dicuntur, capiuntur absolute. Dí-uisim uero dicuntur discretionis aut em phasis causa, διδάσκω ἐμαυτὸν ὑόν, uel διδάσκω ἐμὲ αὐτοῦ υἱόν, Doceo filium meum uel meipsius, σαυτῷ φίλῳ, uel σοὶ αὐτῷ φίλῳ, Tibiipsi amicus: ita & in aliis casi-bus. In tertia persona diuisim dicimus, σφῶν αὐτῶν, σφίσιν αὐτοῖς, σφὰς αὑτούς. Et cō-iunctim ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, ἑαυτούς.
units.tr: Compound pronouns may be construed separately: in the first and second persons only in the singular, and in the third person only in the plural. When they are used compounded, they are taken as absolute. They are used separately for the sake of distinction or emphasis: διδάσκω ἐμαυτὸν υἱόν or διδάσκω ἐμὲ αὐτοῦ υἱόν, "I teach my son, or my own son"; σαυτῷ φίλῳ or σοὶ αὐτῷ φίλῳ, "a friend to yourself"; and so in the other cases. In the third person we say separately σφῶν αὐτῶν, σφίσιν αὐτοῖς, σφὰς αὑτούς, and jointly ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, ἑαυτούς.

units.la: Verum quia composita primæ & se-cundæ personæ proferuntur duntaxat singulariter, ideo tā in duali quàm plu-rali ponunt simplicia cum relatiuis. In duali, νῶι αὐτὼ ὠφελοῦμεν, nosipsos iuua-mus. νῶιν αὐτοῖν ἀπόμεθα, nobisipsis iun-gimur. In plurali, ut ἡμεῖς αὐτῶν, ἡμῖν αὐ-τοῖς, ἡμᾶς αὐτὰς, nostrorumipsorum, no-bisipsis, nosipsos.
units.tr: But because compounds of the first and second persons are used only in the singular, they use the simple forms with the relative in both the dual and the plural. Dual: νῶι αὐτὼ ὠφελοῦμεν, "the two of us help ourselves"; νῶιν αὐτοῖν ἁπτόμεθα, "we are joined to ourselves." Plural: ἡμεῖς αὐτῶν, ἡμῖν αὐτοῖς, ἡμᾶς αὐτάς, "of ourselves, to ourselves, ourselves."

units.la: Vtūtur Græci hoc pronomine ἑαυτῶ in omni persona. ἑαυτὸς ὠφελῶμεν, ὠφελῆτε, ὠφελῶσι, nosipsos iuuamus, uosip-sos iuuatis, feipsos iuuant. Et id nō mo-do in plurali, uerum etiam in singulari.
units.tr: The Greeks use this pronoun ἑαυτῶν in every person: ἑαυτοὺς ὠφελῶμεν, ὠφελῆτε, ὠφελῶσι, "we help ourselves, you help yourselves, they help themselves." And they do this not only in the plural but also in the singular.

units.la: Xenophon. 2. Οἰκονομικῶν. ἐπὶ δὲ παιδεύεως τῆς τὰς ἑαυτῆς φίλους, Sic enim tuos instituis amicos. Verba sunt uirtutis ad uoluptatem. Ioan. 18. σὺ ἀφ' ἑαυτῶ τῶτο λέγεις, ἢ ἄλλω σοι εἶπε ὡς εἰ ἐμῶ; Lucía. in Apol. ταῦτα μὴν ὡς ἐς ἑαυτ̓, ὡς τὸ εἰκῶ, λέλεκταί σοι. ἑαυτ̓ dixít, pro σαυτόν. cum Latíni solum in tertia persona feruent hanc constructionem, id est, sui, sibi, se, à se: quod sicut caret nominatiuo, ita & Græca reciproca compósita.
units.tr: Xenophon, Oeconomicus 2: "ἐπὶ δὲ παιδεύσει τὰς ἑαυτῆς φίλους" ["for thus you train your own friends"]. These are words of virtue set against pleasure. John 18: "σὺ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ τοῦτο λέγεις, ἢ ἄλλοι σοι εἶπον περὶ ἐμοῦ;" ["do you say this of yourself, or did others tell you about me?"]. Lucian, in the Apology: "ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ὡς ἐς ἑαυτόν, ὡς τὸ εἰκός, λέλεκταί σοι" ["these things, then, as is likely, have been said to you concerning yourself"]. He wrote ἑαυτ' for σαυτόν. The Latins keep this construction only in the third person, namely sui, sibi, se, a se; and just as this lacks a nominative, so do the Greek reflexive compounds.

units.la: Caret etiam nominatiuo hoc nomē ἀλλήλων, ἀλλήλοις, ἀλλήλας, & similē habet cum pronominibus constructionē, in omni persona, eo modo quo Latinis inuicem, siue inter, cum accusatiuo φιλεῖν ἀλλήλας, inuicem amare, uel inter se amare. ἀλλήλας ἐλεῶμεν, nos nostri inuicē miseremur, nos nostri inter nos miseremur. ἀλλήλας χαρίζεσθε, inuicē uo bis indulgetis. ἀλλήλας ὑπολαμβάνουσι, inuicem se potiuntur.
units.tr: The word ἀλλήλων, ἀλλήλοις, ἀλλήλας also lacks a nominative, and it takes a construction with the pronouns in every person, in the way the Latins use inuicem or inter: with the accusative, φιλεῖν ἀλλήλας, "to love one another," or "to love among themselves." ἀλλήλας ἐλεῶμεν, "we pity one another," "we pity among ourselves." ἀλλήλας χαρίζεσθε, "you grant favours to one another." ἀλλήλας ὑπολαμβάνουσι, "they lay hold of one another."

units.la: Si uero componatur cum præpositione, habebit nominatiuum, ἐπαλλήλα, ἀμφαλλήλα: uerum tunc non recípit constructionem reciprocam.
units.tr: But if it is compounded with a preposition, it will have a nominative, as in ἐπαλλήλα, ἀμφαλλήλα; but then it does not take the reciprocal construction.

units.la: Appendix.
units.tr: Appendix.

units.la: Mutatio personarum fit, σφέτεςον ωα τέρ ὑμνείουσαι, pro ὑμέτεςον. τὶς ἀρ σφως, pro αὐτω.
units.tr: A change of persons occurs, as in σφέτερον, used for ὑμέτερον in the sense of "your," as in the verb ὑμνεῖουσαι; and τίς ἄρ' σφως, used for αὐτῷ.

units.la: Item numeri, ἀξεἱδλη νυῶ ἀμμε παλιμ πλαγχθέντας οἵω; pro ἡμᾶς. Et apud Pindarum uerbum duale χαρύετον, pro plurali χηρύσσι.
units.tr: Likewise a change of number, as in the Greek ἀξεῖδλη νῶ ἄμμε παλιμ πλαγχθέντας οἵω, used for ἡμᾶς ("us"). And in Pindar the dual verb χαρύετον is used for the plural χηρύσσι.

units.la: Appendix secunda.
units.tr: Second appendix.

units.la: Constrvuntur etiam Pronomina adverbiorum loco, ταῦτά τοι, ταῦτ' ἀρα, ταῦτα δ' ἐ, ταῦτα δ' ἡ, id est, proinde, ad hæc, præterea. In omnibus his subauditur præpositio διὰ ταύτη, hoc pacto, hac ratione, hac de causa, ideo. ταύτη τοι, itaque, propter hoc. ταύτῃ, ὅπερ, ubi simul ponuntur, ualent, οὕτως, ὅπως. ἕςω ταύτῃ, ὅπῃ ὑπολαμβάνεται, Sic fit, ut creditur.
units.tr: Pronouns are also construed in place of adverbs: ταῦτά τοι, ταῦτ' ἄρα, ταῦτα δ' ἔπειτα, ταῦτα δ' ἠδέ, that is, "accordingly, therefore, moreover." In all of these the preposition διά is understood before ταύτῃ, meaning "in this way, by this reasoning, for this cause, therefore." ταύτῃ τοι means "accordingly, for this reason." When ταύτῃ and ὅπερ are placed together, they mean οὕτως, ὅπως, "in such a way as": ἔστω ταύτῃ, ὅπῃ ὑπολαμβάνεται, "so it is, as it is believed."

units.la: DE CONSTRVCTIONE VERBORUM.
units.tr: On the Construction of Verbs.

units.la: VERBA sensuum significatiua iunguntur genitiuo, ἀκούω τῆς φωνῆς, αἰσθάνομαι, ἀπτομαι, γεύομαι, ὀσφραίνομαι, ἐρἀω, ἐπιθυμῶ. Exceptis uisum significantibus, quae accusatiuo iunguntur, ὁρῶ τὴν πόλιν. Verum Attici omnia sentiendi uerba construunt cum accusatiuo.
units.tr: Verbs of sensation that signify take the genitive: I hear the voice [ἀκούω τῆς φωνῆς], I perceive [αἰσθάνομαι], I touch [ἅπτομαι], I taste [γεύομαι], I smell [ὀσφραίνομαι], I love [ἐράω], I desire [ἐπιθυμῶ]. The exception is verbs signifying sight, which take the accusative: I see the city [ὁρῶ τὴν πόλιν]. But the Attic writers construe all verbs of sensation with the accusative.

units.la: αἰσθάνομαι.
units.tr: aisthanomai [αἰσθάνομαι].

units.la: Caeterum uerbum αἰσθάνομαι quandoque significat intelligo, & tum si referatur ad eandem personam, construitur cum participio nominatiui casus. αἰσθάνομαι καλῶς ποιῶν, Intelligo quod bene faciam. αἰσθάνῃ καλῶς ἀναγινώσκων, Intelligis te recte legere.
units.tr: Moreover, the verb aisthanomai sometimes means "I understand." When it refers to the same person, it is construed with a participle in the nominative case: I understand that I am doing well [αἰσθάνομαι καλῶς ποιῶν]; you understand that you are reading well [αἰσθάνῃ καλῶς ἀναγινώσκων].

units.la: Sin uero ad aliam personam, construitur accusatiuo. αἰσθάνομαί σε ποιοῦντα τό, Intelligo te hoc facere.
units.tr: But if it refers to another person, it takes the accusative: I understand you to be doing this [αἰσθάνομαί σε ποιοῦντα τό].

units.la: Item ἀκούω capitur nonnunquam pro uocor, & tunc habet utrinque nominatiuum, more uocatiuorū uerborum. Sic Gregrius de Seruatore ait, σαμαρεί της ἀνθρ ωπ εί, uocatur Samaritanus.
units.tr: Likewise akouō is sometimes used for "I am called," and then it has a nominative on both sides, after the manner of verbs of calling. Thus Gregory says of the Saviour: "You are called a Samaritan" [σαμαρεί της ἀνθρ ωπ εί].

units.la: Construuntur quoq; genitiuo uerba dominandi, uel imperandi, curandi, assequendi, separandi, priuandi, participandi, erroris, concedendi, prohibendi, ad hæc plenitudinis, copiæ, aut inopiæ. Κυριεύω, κρατῶ σου, ἀρχῳ μὴ δενός, nulli impero. μεμνημαι, φεγγίζω, ἐπιμελομαί σου τέτου ἐτυχον. δάφιω, χωρῶ ζομαι, σεεομαι τέτων. κοινωνῶ σοι τῆς δόξης. ἀμβρτανάς τῆς ὁδὸς. συγχωρῶ, ὑπείκω, καλύω, γυμνῶ σε ἀγαθῶν. κενῶ σε φεαλμάτων. πληρῶ σε ἀγαθῶν. Matth. 22. ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων.
units.tr: Verbs of ruling, commanding, caring for, attaining, separating, depriving, sharing, erring, yielding, forbidding, and, in addition, those of fullness, abundance or want also take the genitive. I am lord of you [κυριεύω, κρατῶ σου]; I rule over no one [ἄρχω μηδενός]; I remember [μέμνημαι]; I give light [φεγγίζω]; I take care of you [ἐπιμελοῦμαί σου]; I obtained this [τούτου ἔτυχον]; I need these things [δέομαι τούτων]; I share the glory with you [κοινωνῶ σοι τῆς δόξης]; I miss the way [ἁμαρτάνω τῆς ὁδοῦ]; I grant, I yield [συγχωρῶ, ὑπείκω]; I strip you of goods [γυμνῶ σε ἀγαθῶν]; I empty you of sight [κενῶ σε ὀφθαλμῶν]; I fill you with good things [πληρῶ σε ἀγαθῶν]. Matt. 22: "the wedding was filled with guests reclining" [ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων].

units.la: Ne mireris si prædicta uerba interdū datiuo uel accusatiuo constructa inueniās apud poetas, ἀγλαΐας ἅπομαι. λαχόντες ἐν ὀλίγῳ δόσιν, Pindarus.
units.tr: Do not be surprised if you find the verbs just mentioned sometimes construed with the dative or accusative in the poets: I lay hold of splendour [ἀγλαΐας ἅπτομαι]; having received a gift in small measure [λαχόντες ἐν ὀλίγῳ δόσιν], Pindar.

units.la: Appretiatiua uerba.
units.tr: Verbs of Valuing.

units.la: Appretiatiua uerba admittunt genitiuum significatem pretium, ὠνησάμην τῶν ἀρχῶν. πολλῶ πωλεῖς, magno uēdis. δέκα ταλάντων τιμᾶσαι. τιμωμαί μοι Θανάτῳ, Meipsum morte dignū censeo.
units.tr: Verbs of valuing admit a genitive signifying the price: I bought it for the magistracies [ὠνησάμην τῶν ἀρχῶν]; you sell at a high price [πολλοῦ πωλεῖς], that is, sell dearly; to value at ten talents [δέκα ταλάντων τιμᾶσαι]; I deem myself worthy of death [τιμῶμαί μοι θανάτου].

units.la: Quod etiā quandoque dicitur praecedente præpositione πρὸς uel αντὶ, aut si mili. τὸν βίον πρὸς μικρὰ κέρδη καταλλά- τλουταὶ, Modicis lucris uitam comutat. αντὶ ζωῆς σώματος ἀθανάτον δόξαν αὐτῆ καταλλάξασθαι, pro morti obnoxio corpore gloriam comutare immortalem.
units.tr: This is also sometimes said with the preceding preposition πρός or ἀντί, or with an accusative. They exchange their life for small gains [τὸν βίον πρὸς μικρὰ κέρδη καταλλάττονται]. In exchange for a body subject to death, to barter immortal glory [ἀντὶ ζωῆς σώματος ἀθανάτον δόξαν αὐτῆ καταλλάξασθαι].

units.la: ἐκλείψεως σύνταγμα uel præpositionis.
units.tr: Ellipsis of the construction (syntagma) or of the preposition.

units.la: Crebro regunt uerba genitiuum ἐλλλείπεως, deficiente σύνταγμα, ut ἀπὸ ἔχομαί σε τῆς αἱρέσεως, hoc est, σύνταγμα τῆς αἱρέσεως, suscipio siue approbo te, quod ad uoluntatē attinet. Δαιμονίζω σε τῆς Τύχης, hoc est, σύνταγμα τῆς τύχης. Huius schematis est etiam quod dicitur, εὖ ἥκει φρενῶν, pro φρενιμός ὄξιν. εὖ ἥκει παιδείας, eruditus est. Quem morem Latini imitantur nonunquam in huiusmodi orationibus, Populi seruandi laborat, Reipublicæ defendendæ periclitatur, in quibus deest causa.
units.tr: Verbs often govern the genitive through ellipsis of the construction [σύνταγμα]. Thus "I hold you of the sect" [ἔχομαί σε τῆς αἱρέσεως] stands for "the construction of the sect," that is, I accept or approve you, so far as the will is concerned. "I make you possessed of fortune" [δαιμονίζω σε τῆς τύχης] stands for "the construction of fortune." To this figure also belongs the expression "he is well of mind" [εὖ ἥκει φρενῶν], for "being of sound mind"; "he is well of learning" [εὖ ἥκει παιδείας], that is, he is learned. The Latins sometimes imitate this usage in such expressions as "he labours of saving the people," "he is in danger of defending the commonwealth," where the word causa is omitted.

units.la: Quandoque deficiente alía quauis præpositione, quę postulat genitiuum, λύω σε τῆς δεσμάτων, pro ἀπὸ τ δεσμάτων. διώκω σε τῆς οἰκίας, pro ςὴ τῆς οἰκίας. παύω σε τῆ̣ν κακῶν, παύω σε τὸ παύζειν. κουφίζω σε τῆς χέιρες, pro ἀπὸ τῆς χείρες, ἀρπάζω σε τ' πνεῦς, pro ςὴ πνεῦς.
units.tr: Sometimes the genitive is used when some other preposition that requires it is omitted: I release you from the chains [λύω σε τῆς δεσμῶν], for ἀπὸ τῶν δεσμῶν. I drive you out of the house [διώκω σε τῆς οἰκίας], for ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας. I stop you from [παύω σε τῶν κακῶν], I stop you from playing [παύω σε τοῦ παίζειν]. I lift you from the hand [κουφίζω σε τῆς χειρός], for ἀπὸ τῆς χειρός. I snatch you from the breath [ἁρπάζω σε τῆς πνοῆς], for ἐκ τῆς πνοῆς.

units.la: Verba accusandi, &c.
units.tr: Verbs of Accusing, etc.

units.la: Verba accusandi, damnandi, absoluendi, & confimilia, genitiuum adscifcunt, qui significet crimen: quod nonnūquam etiam effertur per accusatiuū. Per genitiuum quidem, ut διώκω σε φόνυ. Accuso te cædis. αἰτιῶμαί σε τῆδε, criminose hoc tibi obiicio. ἀλίσκω σε τούτυ τ' ἀδικήματος, conuinco te huius iniuriae. ἐάλω κλοπῆς, damnatus est furti.
units.tr: Verbs of accusing, condemning, acquitting and the like take a genitive signifying the crime, which is sometimes also expressed by the accusative. With the genitive: I accuse you of murder [διώκω σε φόνου]; I charge you with this [αἰτιῶμαί σε τῆδε], that is, I bring this charge against you; I convict you of this injury [ἁλίσκω σε τούτου τοῦ ἀδικήματος]; he was condemned for theft [ἐάλω κλοπῆς].

units.la: Quod etiam licet sic dicere, ἐάλω κλέπτων. vel sic, ἐάλω ὅτι κλοπῆ: & ita in aliis similib. διώκω σε πληγῶν, ἐγκαλῶ σοι πληγῶν, Ago tecum iniuriarum ob uerbera. φεύγω δ' ἐλείας, causam dico super status controuerfia. φεύγων φόνυ, postulatus cædis. φεύγων ὕβρεως, postulatus iniurię. φεύγων ἀνθρωποφονίας, reus homicidij, καταγινώσκω σε φόνυ, damno te cædis.
units.tr: It is also permissible to say it thus: he was condemned for stealing [ἐάλω κλέπτων], or thus: he was condemned because of theft [ἐάλω ὅτι κλοπῆ]; and so in other similar cases: I sue you for blows [διώκω σε πληγῶν]; I bring a charge against you for blows [ἐγκαλῶ σοι πληγῶν], I bring suit against you for injuries on account of blows. I plead my case on a question of status [φεύγω δ' ἐλείας]. Being accused of murder [φεύγων φόνου]; accused of insult [φεύγων ὕβρεως]; a defendant on a charge of homicide [φεύγων ἀνθρωποφονίας]; I condemn you of murder [καταγινώσκω σε φόνου].

units.la: Per accusatiuum, καταγινώσκω σε τῶδε, hoc de te iudico & æstimo. καταγινώσκω σῦ σὲ ἀμαθίαν, Iudico te imperitum.
units.tr: With the accusative: I judge and reckon this of you [καταγινώσκω σε τῶδε]. I judge you ignorant [καταγινώσκω σὲ ἀμαθίαν].

units.la: Verba Passiua.
units.tr: Passive Verbs.

units.la: Verba passiua exigunt genitiuū mediante præpositione ὑπό uel παρά, aut si ὑπò uel mili: sicut Latinis ablatiuum mediante præpositione à uel ab. τύπτομαι ὑπὸ σοῦ. μόνον Loco cuius quandoque ponunt datiuū, ἐπείπονταί μοι, pro ὑπὸ ἐμοῦ. λέλεκταί σοι, pro ὑπὸ σοῦ. διδάσκομαί σοι ῥητορικὴν, pro διδάσκομαι ὑπὸ σοῦ.
units.tr: Passive verbs require a genitive with the preposition ὑπό or παρά, or if ὑπό or μετά, just as Latins use the ablative with the preposition a or ab. I am struck by you [τύπτομαι ὑπὸ σοῦ]. Instead of this they sometimes put the dative: I am followed by me [ἐπείπονταί μοι], for by me [ὑπὸ ἐμοῦ]; it has been said by you [λέλεκταί σοι], for by you [ὑπὸ σοῦ]; I am taught rhetoric by you [διδάσκομαί σοι ῥητορικὴν], for I am taught by you [διδάσκομαι ὑπὸ σοῦ].

units.la: Quædam uerba regunt genitiuum, quia resoluuntur in nomen, cui iungitur genitiuus. ἀξιῶ σε πιμῆς, pro ἡξίωμαί σε ἄξιον τῆς τιμῆς. γυμνῶ σε ἐνδυμάτων, pro γυμνῶ σε γυμνὸν τῆς ἐνδυμάτων. Ad Heb.3. πλείονος δόξης ἔτιμ παρὰ Μωϋσῆ ἠξιώθη, ampliori gloria præ Moyse dignus habitus est.
units.tr: Some verbs govern the genitive because they are resolved into a noun to which the genitive is joined. I think you worthy of honour [ἀξιῶ σε τιμῆς], for I have deemed you worthy of the honour [ἠξίωμαί σε ἄξιον τῆς τιμῆς]. I strip you of garments [γυμνῶ σε ἐνδυμάτων], for I strip you naked of the garments [γυμνῶ σε γυμνὸν τῆς ἐνδυμάτων]. Heb. 3: "He has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses" [πλείονος δόξης παρὰ Μωϋσῆ ἠξιώθη], that is, he was judged worthy of greater glory before Moses.

units.la: Verbum Substantiuum.
units.tr: The Substantive Verb.

units.la: Verbum substantiuum adsciscit non nunquam genitiuū. τούτων ἐστιν ὁ πλάτων, horum, aut de numero horū est Plato. Quod uerbum quandoque omittitur, ἐκ τῆς ἀδικούντων ἐγώ, Neque ego sum de numero nocentium.
units.tr: The substantive verb sometimes takes a genitive: Plato is of these, or is one of their number [τούτων ἐστιν ὁ Πλάτων]. This verb is sometimes omitted: I am not one of the wrongdoers [ἐκ τῆς ἀδικούντων ἐγώ].

units.la: Idem cum articulo.
units.tr: The same with the article.

units.la: Construitur etiam quādoc̨ uerbum substantiuum ἐσὶ cum articulo subiun-ctiuo, & in recto & in obliquo, tam sin-gularis quàm pluralis numeri, hoc mo-do: ἐσὶν οἱ τινες, hoc est aliqui. οὐκ ἐσὶν οἱ π-νες τρέχουσι, nulli currūt. ἐσὶν οἷς, pro qui bufdam. φωνῆς ἐσὶν οἷς ἀξηκέεἶο, uox quę dam quibufdam exaudiebatur. ἐσὶν οὓς, aliquos: ut ἰδὼν πολλὰς μὴ ἐν μάχης φεύ-γοντας, ἐσὶ δὲ ἐς εἰς θανατον ἀσπιτούλας, Vidi multos e conflictu fugientes, & aliquos in morte prostratos: pro quo etiam dicunt, ἐσὶν ἐς τινας. ἐσὶν ὦν, quorun-dam. ἐσὶν ὅς, quídam. ἐσὶν ἕ, cuiusdam. Et sic de alijs casibus.
units.tr: The substantive verb ἐστί is also sometimes constructed with the relative article, in the nominative and the oblique cases, in both singular and plural, as follows: ἔστιν οἱ τινες [ἔστιν οἱ τινες], that is, some. οὐκ εἰσὶν οἱ τρέχουσι [οὐκ εἰσὶν οἱ τρέχοντες], none are running. ἔστιν οἷς [ἔστιν οἷς], for certain people: φωνὴ ἔστιν οἷς ἠκούετο [φωνὴ ἔστιν οἷς ἠκούετο], a voice was heard by certain people. ἔστιν οὓς [ἔστιν οὓς], some (acc.), as in ἰδὼν πολλὰς μὲν ἐν μάχῃ φεύγοντας, ἔστι δὲ οὓς εἰς θάνατον ἀσπίδας [ἰδὼν πολλοὺς μὲν ἐν μάχῃ φεύγοντας, ἔστι δὲ οὓς εἰς θάνατον ...]: I saw many fleeing from the battle, and some stretched out in death. In place of this they also say ἔστιν ἑς τινας [ἔστιν εἴς τινας]. ἔστιν ὧν [ἔστιν ὧν], of certain people. ἔστιν ὅς [ἔστιν ὅς], a certain person. ἔστιν οὗ [ἔστιν οὗ], of a certain person. And so with the other cases.

units.la: Quodlibet uerbum genítiuo cõstrui tur significanti tempus, aut partem, aut materiam. νυκτὸς ἡ ἡμέρας ἐργάζεται σἰρῳ μάξῃ τῇ ἀσοδός. πίνω τῆς ὕδατος, bibo de aqua, πίνω τὸ ὕδωρ, bibo aquā. ἐποίησε λί-θῳ, fecit e lapide.
units.tr: Any verb is constructed with the genitive when it signifies time, a part, or material: νυκτὸς ἢ ἡμέρας ἐργάζεται [νυκτὸς ἢ ἡμέρας ἐργάζεται], he works by night or by day; σίτου ... [σίτου ...] ... ; πίνω τοῦ ὕδατος [πίνω τοῦ ὕδατος], I drink of the water, πίνω τὸ ὕδωρ [πίνω τὸ ὕδωρ], I drink the water; ἐποίησε λίθου [ἐποίησε λίθου], he made it out of stone.

units.la: Item datiuo designanti instrumētum uel causam, ἐδ' ἔξατο χεὶ κύπελλον, φθό-νῳ ταῦτα ἐποίησε.
units.tr: Likewise the dative is used to denote the instrument or the cause: ἐδέξατο χειρὶ κύπελλον [ἐδέξατο χειρὶ κύπελλον], he received the cup in his hand; φθόνῳ ταῦτα ἐποίησε [φθόνῳ ταῦτα ἐποίησε], he did these things out of envy.

units.la: Datiuo iunguntur uerba sequendi, ἑπομαι, ἀκολουθῶ σοι. Dicis congrue, ἀφαιρῶ σε χρυσίον, χρυσίῳ, uel χρυσίῳ, ἀφαιρῶ σε uel σοι χρυσίον.
units.tr: Verbs of following take the dative: ἕπομαι, ἀκολουθῶ σοι [ἕπομαι, ἀκολουθῶ σοι], I follow you. One says correctly ἀφαιρῶ σε χρυσίον, or χρυσίῳ, or χρυσίῳ ἀφαιρῶ σε, or σοι χρυσίον [ἀφαιρῶ σε χρυσίον], I deprive you of gold.

units.la: Verba certandi.
units.tr: Verbs of contending.

units.la: Similiter uerba certādi, μάχομαι νυσὶ ἐν φρέατι, In puteo cum canibus pugna= re, τοῖς θεοῖς μάχεσθαι. φιλονεικῶ σοι, cōten do aduersum te. πάλαιῶ τοῖς πολλοῖς, lu- ctor aduersus multos, πυνεγτέρεῖς πολε- μεῖν, aduersus pauciores belligerare.
units.tr: Similarly verbs of contending: μάχομαι κυσὶν ἐν φρέατι [μάχομαι κυσὶν ἐν φρέατι], to fight with dogs in a well; τοῖς θεοῖς μάχεσθαι [τοῖς θεοῖς μάχεσθαι], to fight against the gods; φιλονεικῶ σοι, I contend against you; πάλαιω τοῖς πολλοῖς, I wrestle against many; πλειόνων ἐστὶ πολεμεῖν [πλειόνων ἐστὶ πολεμεῖν]... fewer things to be waged in war against the more numerous, that is, to make war against fewer.

units.la: Sic Vergilius, Placidone etiam pugnabis amori?
units.tr: So Virgil: "Placidone etiam pugnabis amori?" Will you even fight against a gentle love?

units.la: Nonnunquam & pretiū ponitur in datiuo. Chryfoft. ἱδ᾽ ἵσῳ θανάτῳ τὸ ποίμνιον ᾠριάμψω, propria morte gregē emens.
units.tr: Sometimes the price too is put in the dative. Chrysostom: ἰδίῳ ἵσῳ θανάτῳ τὸ ποίμνιον ἐξηγόρασεν [ἰδίῳ ἵσῳ θανάτῳ τὸ ποίμνιον ἐξηγόρασεν], having bought the flock with his own death as the price.

units.la: Verba significatiua motus.
units.tr: Verbs signifying motion.

units.la: Verba significantibus motum ad lo= cum, additur sæpe datiuus loco accusati ui, cum præpositione, ut ὁρμᾷ δι᾽ ἀέρος τῇ πόλει, pro εἰς πόλιν.
units.tr: Verbs signifying motion towards a place are often joined with a dative in place of the accusative with a preposition, as ὁρμᾷ διὰ ἀέρος τῇ πόλει [ὁρμᾷ διὰ ἀέρος τῇ πόλει], he rushes through the air to the city, in place of εἰς πόλιν [εἰς πόλιν].

units.la: Cum uerba regunt datiuum prono= minis αὐτὸς, sæpenumero intelligitur prepositio σὺν, ut ἀπολέμῳ αὐταῖς ὡλέναις τὰ πλεῖα, hoc est, σὺν αὐταῖς ὡλεναῖς, αὐ= Τῆς ὄπλοις ἔλαβεν ἀνδρας, hoc est; σὺν αὐτῆς ὄπλοις, Vna cum armis accepit uiros. Esᴉ pro habeo, gaudet datiuo, sicut apud Latinos, ὧν ἔσι μοι ἀργύριον.
units.tr: When verbs govern the dative of the pronoun αὐτός, the preposition σύν is often understood, as ἀπολέμῳ αὐταῖς χερσὶν τὰ πλεῖα [ἀπολέμῳ αὐταῖς χερσὶν τὰ πλεῖα], that is, σὺν αὐταῖς χερσίν, with their own hands; αὐτῇ σὺν ὅπλοις ἔλαβεν ἄνδρας [αὐτῇ σὺν ὅπλοις ἔλαβεν ἄνδρας], that is, σὺν αὐτῇ ὅπλοις, she took men along with her arms. ἔστι, meaning "I have," takes the dative, as in Latin: ὧν ἔστι μοι ἀργύριον [ὧν ἔστι μοι ἀργύριον], I have money of these things.

units.la: χεῶμαι & χεῆσθαι, & similia construuntur datiuo. χεῶμαι τοῖς φίλοις, καλῶς ἑαυτῷ χεῆσθαι, honeste se habere.
units.tr: χρῶμαι and χρῆσθαι, and similar verbs, are constructed with the dative: χρῶμαι τοῖς φίλοις [χρῶμαι τοῖς φίλοις], I use my friends; καλῶς ἑαυτῷ χρῆσθαι [καλῶς ἑαυτῷ χρῆσθαι], to conduct oneself well, to behave honourably.

units.la: Haec autem genitiuo & datiuo, φθονῶ μετέχω, κοινωνῶ, συγγινώσκω. ut φθονῶ σοι τῆς σαλήτης. μετέχω σοι τούτου, Huius rei tecum particeps sum.
units.tr: But these verbs take the genitive and dative: φθονῶ, μετέχω, κοινωνῶ, συγγινώσκω, as φθονῶ σοι τῆς σωτηρίας [φθονῶ σοι τῆς σωτηρίας], I envy you your salvation; μετέχω σοι τούτου [μετέχω σοι τούτου], I share with you in this matter.

units.la: Impersonalia.
units.tr: Impersonal verbs.

units.la: Item haec impersonalia, δεῖ μέτεσι, μέλει, μεταμέλει, διαφέρει, ἀρέσκει. ut μέλει μοι τοῦτο, uel ἀρεῖ τοῦτο, Huius mihi cura est. διαφέρει μοι τούτου, uel ἀρεῖ τούτου, huius mea refert. ἀρέσκει μοι τούτου, uel πρέπει τούτου, huius me decet. δεῖ μοι τούτου, Opus est mihi hac re.
units.tr: Likewise these impersonal verbs: δεῖ, μέτεστι, μέλει, μεταμέλει, διαφέρει, ἀρέσκει. For example μέλει μοι τούτου, or ἀρέσκει τούτου [μέλει μοι τούτου], this is a care to me, I am concerned with this. διαφέρει μοι τούτου, or ἀρέσκει τούτου, this matters to me. ἀρέσκει μοι τούτου, or πρέπει τούτου, this suits me. δεῖ μοι τούτου, I have need of this thing.

units.la: Ἀμελῶ ομαι, πιμωρῶ, ἐκδικῶ σοι, uel ὑπὲρ σε, Vlcisci iniuriam tibi illatam. Cũ ac cusatiuo uero significant haec uerba, crucio, uindico, ἑαυτὸν τιμωρέμενος. ἀμύνομαι uel ἐκδικῶ σε, uindico te.
units.tr: ἀμύνομαι, τιμωρῶ, ἐκδικῶ σοι, or ὑπὲρ σε, to avenge a wrong done to you. But with the accusative these verbs mean to torment, to avenge oneself, as ἑαυτὸν τιμωρούμενος [ἑαυτὸν τιμωρούμενος], avenging oneself. ἀμύνομαι or ἐκδικῶ σε, I avenge you.

units.la: Attici plerunque casum uerbi praecedentis dentis sequenti cōstruunt, licet ab eo sit alienus, χρῶμαι οἷς ἔχω βιβλίοις, pro ἃ ἔχω. Ἀπολαύω ὧν ἔχω ἀγαθῶν.
units.tr: The Attics commonly construe the case of the preceding verb with the following one, even though it is foreign to it: χρῶμαι οἷς ἔχω βιβλίοις [χρῶμαι οἷς ἔχω βιβλίοις], for ἃ ἔχω, I use the books I have. ἀπολαύω ὧν ἔχω ἀγαθῶν [ἀπολαύω ὧν ἔχω ἀγαθῶν], I enjoy the goods I have.

units.la: Vtūtur item accusatiuo pro datiuo, ἀρέσκει σε, pro σοι, οἷά με ποιεῖς, pro μοι. Theo, Idyl. 2. Et uerbis actiuis pro passi uis, & ediuerso, γράφειν pro γράφεσθαι.
units.tr: They also use the accusative for the dative: ἀρέσκει σε, for σοι, and οἷά με ποιεῖς, for μοι. Theocritus, Idyll 2. And they use active verbs for passive, and conversely, γράφειν for γράφεσθαι.

units.la: Quędam uerba propter uaria significata uariīs casibus iungūtur, κυριεύω σε, dominor tui, κυριεύω σε, dominum te facio, &c.
units.tr: Certain verbs, because of their various meanings, are joined with various cases: κυριεύω σε, I am lord of you; κυριεύω σε, I make you lord, etc.

units.la: Enallage modorum.
units.tr: Interchange of moods.

units.la: Accipitur modus pro modo, ut ἐὰν ἐλθῇς, pro ἐλθῇς. τέμνειν pro τέμνε, πεποίη- ται, pro πεποίηκε.
units.tr: One mood is used for another, as ἐὰν ἔλθῃς, for ἔλθῃς [ἐὰν ἔλθῃς]; τέμνειν for τέμνε [τέμνειν]; πεποίηται for πεποίηκε [πεποίηται].

units.la: Indicatiuo utuntur nōnunquam loco optatiui. Greg. ἄδηλον ὃν, εἰ ἀφεσήσει, Incertum erat, si admissurus erat. ἀφεσῆ σεῖαι dixit pro ἀφεσήσοιτο.
units.tr: The indicative is sometimes used in place of the optative. Gregory: ἄδηλον ἦν, εἰ ἀφεσήσει [ἄδηλον ἦν, εἰ ἀφεσήσει], it was uncertain whether he would be willing to forgive. He said ἀφεθῆ εἴη [ἀφεθῇ εἴη] for ἀφεθήσοιτο.

units.la: Per Indicatiuum etiā multa dicunt, quæ Latini efferunt per coniunctiuum. οὐτ' ἐποίησα ἀδελφὸν, ἐφ' ᾧ ἠχωΐθη, Neque feci quicquā, ob quod erubuerit, uel erubescere debuerit. χρῆσαι ἀδελφῶν ἐστιν, ὅσις μὴ ἐβαπτίσθη. Quod etiam per Optatiuū dici poteft,addito ἂν ἀληθινῶς, hoc modo, χρίσαιντῶν ἐδέις ἔσῃ,ὅσις μὴ βαπτιθείη ἂν
units.tr: Through the indicative they also express many things which the Latins render by the subjunctive: οὐδὲν ἐποίησα ἀδελφόν, ἐφ' ᾧ ἠρυθρίασεν [οὐδὲν ἐποίησα ἀδελφόν, ἐφ' ᾧ ἠρυθρίασεν], I did nothing, on account of which he blushed or ought to blush. χρῖσαι ἀδελφῶν ἐστιν, ὅστις μὴ ἐβαπτίσθη [χρῖσαι ἀδελφῶν ἐστιν, ὅστις μὴ ἐβαπτίσθη], he is one of the brethren who has not been baptised. This can also be said by the optative, with ἂν ἀληθινῶς added, in this way, χρίσαιντῶν ἐδέις ἔσῃ,ὅσις μὴ βαπτιθείη ἂν [χρίσαι τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἔσῃ, ὅστις μὴ βαπτισθείη ἂν]: truly one of the brethren you would be, who had not been baptised.

units.la: Plerūque etiam uerbum Optatiuum cōstructum cum particula potentiali ἂν, habet sensum futuri, ὅτι ἂν ποιήσειε, quod facere possit, uel poterit. Sine ἂν uero quandoque capitur pro praeterito, ἃ ἔδει, quæ opportuna erant.
units.tr: Often also an optative verb construed with the potential particle ἂν has the sense of a future, ὅτι ἂν ποιήσειε [ὅτι ἂν ποιήσειε], what he could do, or will be able to do. Without ἂν, however, it is sometimes taken for the past, ἃ ἔδει [ἃ ἔδει], things which were fitting.

units.la: Optatiuus praeterea sæpe ponitur pro Indicatiuo. Plato in Protag. ἔλεγες γὰρ, ὅτι ὁ Ζεὺς, τῷ Ληκγοσυλῳ, καὶ τῷ αἰδοῖ πέμψειε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις. ἔπεμψε dixit, pro ἔπεμψε.
units.tr: The optative is also often put for the indicative. Plato in the Protagoras: ἔλεγες γὰρ, ὅτι ὁ Ζεὺς, τῷ Ληκγοσυλῳ, καὶ τῷ αἰδοῖ πέμψειε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις. ἔπεμψε [ἔλεγες γὰρ, ὅτι ὁ Ζεὺς ... τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ... ἔπεμψε]: for you said that Zeus sent to men, by Hermes, justice and reverence; ἔπεμψε [ἔπεμψε] for the indicative, he sent.

units.la: Modus coniunctiuus sæpe accommodatur futuro, etiam in uoce præsenti, ὁπόσα βούλῃ, quęcunque uolueris. οὓς ἂν ἐθέλῃς, quoscunque uolueris. ὅσῳ ἂν πλεονάκις εἰσίῃς εἰς ἐμὲ, id est, ingressus fueris, uel adieris.
units.tr: The subjunctive is often used for the future, even in the present voice: ὁπόσα βούλῃ [ὁπόσα βούλῃ], as many as you wish. οὓς ἂν ἐθέλῃς [οὓς ἂν ἐθέλῃς], whomever you wish. ὅσῳ ἂν πλεονάκις εἰσίῃς εἰς ἐμέ [ὅσῳ ἂν πλεονάκις εἰσίῃς εἰς ἐμέ], that is, as often as you shall have entered or approached me.

units.la: Infinitiuus cum aduerbijs, πρὶν, ἕως, μὴ, ὡς, sæpe pro Indicatiuo, Optatiuo, uel Subiunctiuo, prout sententiæ conciniit, accipitur, πρὶν εἰπεῖν, pro εἶπον ἐς, ἐς, ὁμῶς, ἐτε. uel εἴπω, ἠς, ἡ, &c. ἕως ἀμβλεῖναι, pro ἀμβλέιναι, ἡς, ἡ, μὴ γνῶναι, pro μὴ ἴνοῖν ἠς. ης, η. γνῶ γνῶς ῶ, &c. ὡς εἰπεῖν, ut ita dicam, sic dicere licet. Græcis frequens usus est, ἀορίστων infinitiuorum, quādo per ἵνα in Subiunctiuum possunt conuerti, ἐτέλει γεάψαι. ἐτέλει ἵνα γεάφῃ. κελεύει διδάσκειν, κελεύει ἵνα διδάσκῃ, &c.
units.tr: The infinitive with the adverbs πρίν, ἕως, μή, ὡς is often taken for the indicative, optative or subjunctive, as the sense requires: πρὶν εἰπεῖν [πρὶν εἰπεῖν], for εἶπον, εἶπες, εἶπε, etc., or εἴπω, εἴπης, εἴπῃ, etc.; ἕως ἀμβλεῖναι [ἕως ἀμβλύνειν], for ἀμβλύνειν, ἀμβλύνῃς, ἀμβλύνῃ; μὴ γνῶναι [μὴ γνῶναι], for μὴ γνῶ, γνῷς, γνῷ, etc.; ὡς εἰπεῖν [ὡς εἰπεῖν], as I may say, so to speak, it is permitted to say so. It is a frequent Greek usage that aorist infinitives, when they can be turned into the subjunctive by ἵνα, are so turned: ἐτέλει γράψαι [ἐτέλει γράψαι], ἐτέλει ἵνα γράψῃ [ἐτέλει ἵνα γράψῃ]; κελεύει διδάσκειν [κελεύει διδάσκειν], κελεύει ἵνα διδάσκῃ [κελεύει ἵνα διδάσκῃ], etc.

units.la: In uerbis coniunctiuis sæpe subaudiitur ἵνα, uel aliud quippiam simile. Chrysostom. Concione secunda de fato: ἑτέρως λυμαίνεται τὸ πείθειν ἐπιχειρῶν, ut alio pacto noceat, persuadere conatur.
units.tr: In subjunctive verbs ἵνα, or some other similar word, is often understood. Chrysostom, in the second sermon on fate: ἑτέρως λυμαίνεται τὸ πείθειν ἐπιχειρῶν [ἑτέρως λυμαίνεται τὸ πείθειν ἐπιχειρῶν], he tries to persuade so as to harm in another way.

units.la: Coniunctiuis construuntur interrogatiua dubitatiue accepta, ποτέρων σιωπῶ; an sileam; τί λέγω;
units.tr: Deliberative interrogatives are construed with the subjunctive: ποτέρως σιωπῶ; [ποτέρως σιωπῶ]; shall I be silent? τί λέγω; [τί λέγω]; what am I to say?

units.la: Impersonalia.
units.tr: Impersonal verbs.

units.la: Impersonalia construuntur infinitiuis praesentibus, uel praeteritis, sed nunquam futuris, etiam si de futuro fiat sermo, ut δεῖ φαναι. χρὴ λαβεῖν. ἐνδέχεται εἶναι, licet esse. φιλεῖ γίγνεσθαι, solet fieri.
units.tr: Impersonal verbs are construed with the present or past infinitive, but never with the future, even when the sense concerns the future: δεῖ φαναι [it is necessary to say], χρὴ λαβεῖν [one must take], ἐνδέχεται εἶναι [it is possible to be], licet esse, φιλεῖ γίγνεσθαι [it is customary to become], solet fieri.

units.la: Infinitiui construction. Primo cum μέλλω.
units.tr: Construction of the infinitive. First, with μέλλω.

units.la: Verbum μέλλω construitur etiam in finitiuis praesentibus, & futuris, μέλλω ζῆν, uel μέλλω δράσειν, sum facturus. Interdum etiam cū Aorifto μέλλω γενέσθαι.
units.tr: The verb μέλλω [to be about to] is construed with the present and future infinitives: μέλλω ζῆν [I am about to live], or μέλλω δράσειν [I am going to act], sum facturus. Sometimes it is also construed with the aorist: μέλλω γενέσθαι [I am about to become].

units.la: Sic. ero. Sed cum perfecto nunquam.
units.tr: So too with the future of "to be", ero. But never with the perfect.

units.la: Cum uerbis motus ad locum.
units.tr: With verbs of motion to a place.

units.la: Infinitiuus construitur uerbis motus ad locum. Matth.5. ἐκ ἤλθον καταλύσαι, ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι τὸν νόμον. Ioan.14. πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι ὑμῖν τόπον. Cui quandoque additur praepositio εἰς, cum articulo neutro, ἔρχομαι εἰς τὸ προσκαλεῖν, Vado oratum.
units.tr: The infinitive is construed with verbs of motion towards a place. Matt. 5: "I came not to destroy but to fulfil the law" [οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι, ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι τὸν νόμον]. John 14: "I go to prepare a place for you" [πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι ὑμῖν τόπον]. To this the preposition εἰς is sometimes added, with the neuter article: ἔρχομαι εἰς τὸ προσκαλεῖν [I come to summon], "I go to beg".

units.la: Cum altero Infinitiuo.
units.tr: With another infinitive.

units.la: Construitur etiā Infinitiuus cum alte ro infinitiuo. ὁρῶ σε μελλητὴν ἀναγινώσκειν, Video te meditari ut legas.
units.tr: The infinitive is also construed with another infinitive: ὁρῶ σε μελλητὴν ἀναγινώσκειν [I see you hesitating to read], "I see you preparing to read".

units.la: Cum relatiuis nominibus.
units.tr: With relative nouns.

units.la: Nomina relatiua iunguntur Infiniti- uis, οἷον εὐφραίνειν, pro οἷον διφραίνειν, uel οἳ οὐ εὐφρανεῖν δλωσαι ἂν, quale possit affi- cere gaudio. οἱ θεοὶ εἰσὶν οἷοι μὴ μεταβάλ- λειν. Dij sunt qui non mutentur. τοιοῦτός ἐστιν, οἷος μὴ ἥδεσθαι, talis est, ut non delectetur. οἷος καθεύδειν, Pronus ad dormiendum. οἷος ποιεῖν, Potens ad faciendū. ᾧ οἷον παθεῖν, Nihil uetat quo minus addamus. ὅσα χάριν ὁρᾶν, Quantum ego cernere queam.
units.tr: Relative nouns are joined to infinitives: οἷον εὐφραίνειν [such as to gladden], or οἳ οὐ εὐφρανεῖν δλωσαι ἂν [such as could bring joy], "of such a kind as to affect with joy". οἱ θεοὶ εἰσὶν οἷοι μὴ μεταβάλλειν ["the gods are such as not to change"]: "Gods are those who do not change." τοιοῦτός ἐστιν, οἷος μὴ ἥδεσθαι ["he is such as not to rejoice"]: "he is such that he does not take delight." οἷος καθεύδειν: "prone to sleep." οἷος ποιεῖν: "able to do." ᾧ οἷον παθεῖν: "nothing forbids us from adding." ὅσα χάριν ὁρᾶν: "as much as I am able to see."

units.la: Cum adiectiuis.
units.tr: With adjectives.

units.la: Et nomina adiectiua {Greek} pulcher uisu. {Greek} fortis ad pugnā. Luci, in luctu. {Greek} id est, profundior quàm ut pedibus transiri possit.
units.tr: Adjectival nouns are likewise so construed: "pleasant to look upon" (pulcher uisu); "strong for fighting" (fortis ad pugnam); "mournful in grief" (Luci, in luctu); and {Greek}, that is, "deeper than it can be crossed on foot".

units.la: Sic Virgilius,
units.tr: So Virgil:

units.la: Cur nō Mopse boni, quoniā cōuenimus ambo, Tu calamos inflare leues, ego dicere uersus.
units.tr: Why not, good Mopsus, since we have met together, you blow the light reeds and I sing verses?

units.la: Accusatiuus quando præcedat Infinitiuū.
units.tr: When the accusative precedes the infinitive.

units.la: Quando infinitiuus & uerbum præcedens pertinent ad diuersas personas, opus est accusatiuo ante infinitiuum. {Greek} id est, dico te scire hæc.
units.tr: When the infinitive and the verb preceding it refer to different persons, an accusative is required before the infinitive: "I say that you know these things."

units.la: Sin autem pertineat ad eandem personam, nō est opus accusatiuo, {Greek} dixit facturum, nempe se.
units.tr: But if it refers to the same person, no accusative is needed: "he said that he would act," namely, himself.

units.la: Quandoque nominatiuus præcedit Infinit.
units.tr: Sometimes the nominative precedes the infinitive.

units.la: Infinitiuus non tam accusatiuum habet ante se, quàm nominatiuum. {Greek} dicit se authore fuisse, {Greek} Tam alienus est ab arrogantia, ut cum omnia norit,
units.tr: The infinitive has before it not so much an accusative as a nominative: "he says that he himself was the author"; "he is so far from arrogance that, although he knows everything, he thinks he knows nothing."

units.la: t tamen se nihil scire putet. Id autem fit, si casus uerbi finiti praecedens trahat ad se casum infinitiui.
units.tr: This happens when the case of the preceding finite verb draws to itself the case of the infinitive.

units.la: Accusatiuus post Infinitiuum.
units.tr: Accusative after the infinitive.

units.la: Plerūque etiam postponunt Infiniti-uorum accusatiuum, qui tamen a parte anteriori regitur. χρὴ μὴ σφόδρα μελλῆσαι τῆς δυσσεβείας, ἐν ὑμμέροις ὅπως αὐ ζῆτελθεν. Oportet eos nō negligere pietatem, qui animo reuoluunt quomodo perficiant.
units.tr: Often they also place the accusative of the infinitive after it, although it is governed from the front: χρὴ μὴ σφόδρα μελλῆσαι τῆς δυσσεβείας, ἐν ὑμμέροις ὅπως αὐ ζῆτελθεν: "those who turn over in their minds how they may accomplish it ought not to neglect piety."

units.la: ἐν καλῷ & similes phrases cum Infinitiuo.
units.tr: ἐν καλῷ and similar phrases with the infinitive.

units.la: His orationibus, ἐν καλῷ, id est, bonum, commodum. ἐν καλλίςῳ, honestissimum, commodissimum, recte additur Infinitiuus, mediante articulo genitiuo τῶ. ἐν καλῷ τῶ ποιεῖν, commode ad faciendum. ἐν καλλίςῳ τῶ ποιεῖν, commodissime ad faciendum.
units.tr: In these expressions, ἐν καλῷ, that is, "well, conveniently"; ἐν καλλίστῳ, "most honourably, most conveniently": the infinitive is rightly added, with the genitive article τῷ intervening: ἐν καλῷ τῷ ποιεῖν, "conveniently for doing"; ἐν καλλίστῳ τῷ ποιεῖν, "most conveniently for doing."

units.la: Infinitiuus per figuram.
units.tr: The infinitive used figuratively.

units.la: Vtuntur & figurate Infinitiuo, ὡς ἰδεῖν τὸν ἀνθρωπον, pro ὡς ἰδὲν ὁ ἀνθρωπος. ὡς ἀκοῦσαι τὰς παιδίας, pro ὡς ἤκουσαν οἱ παῖδες. ἐπειδὴ ἀκοῦσαι τὸν, pro ἐπειδὴ ἤκουσεν ἐκ. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἠγέσθαι, pro ἐπειδὴ ἠγέσατο. In quibus ἐπειδὴ tantum ualet, quam
units.tr: They also use the infinitive figuratively: ὡς ἰδεῖν τὸν ἀνθρωπον for ὡς ἰδὼν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ["as the man saw"]; ὡς ἀκοῦσαι τὰς παιδίας for ὡς ἤκουσαν οἱ παῖδες ["as the boys heard"]; ἐπειδὴ ἀκοῦσαι τὸν for ἐπειδὴ ἤκουσεν ["after he heard"]; ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἠγέσθαι for ἐπειδὴ ἠγέσατο ["but after he led"]. In these, ἐπειδὴ has only as much force as μετὰ τὸ, so that the sense is μετὰ τὸ γε νέεσθαι ["after the going"].

units.la: {Infinitiuus per figuram}Inf.p fig. quantum μετὰ τὸ: ut sit sensus, μετὰ τὸ γε νέεσθαι.
units.tr: The infinitive used figuratively, continued: ἐπειδὴ has the same force as μετὰ τὸ, so that the sense is "after going" (μετὰ τὸ γε νέεσθαι).

units.la: Infinitiuus loco participiorum impersonalium.
units.tr: The infinitive in place of impersonal participles.

units.la: Ponitur etiam Infinitiuus nonnun-quam loco participiorum impersonali-um, ἐμοὶ δοκεῖν, pro ἐμοὶ δοκοῦσι, cum mihi uisum esset, δεῖν pro δέον, cum oporteret. Sic etiam in simili uoce, πλεῖν, pro πλέον, plus.
units.tr: The infinitive is also sometimes used in place of impersonal participles: ἐμοὶ δοκεῖν for ἐμοὶ δοκοῦσι, "since it seemed to me"; δεῖν for δέον, "since it was necessary." So too with the similar word πλεῖν for πλέον, "more."

units.la: Phrasis peculiaris per Infinitiuum.
units.tr: A peculiar phrase with the infinitive.

units.la: Quod Latíni dicunt, Vt uno uerboabfoluam, id Græci plerunque efferunt per Infinitiuum expressum uel subaudi tum, his modis, σωσελόντι δ' εἰπεῖν, σὺ λό γῳ δὲ εἰπεῖν, σωσελόντι δὲ φαναι, σωσελόντα δὲ φαναι, καθόλου μὴ οὐ εἰπεῖν: quod etiam fit per Optatiuum sic, σωσελὸν δὲ φαίλω ἄν.
units.tr: What the Latins express by "to finish with one word" (ut uno uerbo absoluam), the Greeks usually render by an infinitive, either expressed or understood, in these ways: σωσελόντι δ' εἰπεῖν, σὺ λόγῳ δὲ εἰπεῖν, σωσελόντι δὲ φαναι, σωσελόντα δὲ φαναι, καθόλου μὴ οὐ εἰπεῖν. This is also done with the optative, thus: σωσελὸν δὲ φαίλω ἄν.

units.la: APPENDIX PRIMA. Ἐλλειψις uerborum.
units.tr: FIRST APPENDIX. Ellipsis of verbs [Ἔλλειψις ῥημάτων].

units.la: VERBA in oratione sæpe omittun-tur ornatus gratia, ὡς λόγῳ, ut fama est. Sic ἀποδειξις δὲ, σημεῖον δὲ, τεκμήριον ἢ, inseruntur orationibus in modum parentheseos, pro, Cuius rei demonstratio est: cuius rei indicium est: & subauditur ἐςω, uel εἶn αὐ.
units.tr: Words are often left out of a sentence for the sake of ornament, as in ὡς λόγῳ, "as the saying goes," or ut fama est, "as report has it." So ἀπόδειξις δέ, σημεῖον δέ and τεκμήριον ἥ are inserted into sentences as parentheses, in the sense of "the proof of this is," "the sign of this is," and ἔστω or εἶναι αὐτό is understood.

units.la: Verbum unū pro integra oratione usurpatur.
units.tr: One word is used in place of a whole sentence.

units.la: Et è cōtrario quibusdam uerbis utun tur solis loco totius orationis. Sic γίνο- μαι capitur pro seruum esse, αὐτὸς γιγνόμε- νος, hoc est, ipsius seruus. Et υἱός, pro esse filium. λέγουσι τὸν υἱὸν ἐκείνου, Dicunt hūc esse filium illius.
units.tr: Conversely, some words are used alone in place of a whole sentence. Thus γίνομαι is taken to mean "to be a slave," as in αὐτὸς γιγνόμενος [being his own man], that is, "of him" as his slave. And υἱός is used for "to be a son," as in λέγουσι τὸν υἱὸν ἐκείνου, "they say he is that man's son."

units.la: Appendix secunda.
units.tr: Second Appendix.

units.la: παρέλκυσι uerba quædam.
units.tr: Certain verbs that are superfluous.

units.la: Quædam etiam quandoque ponun tur quidem in oratione, sed plane abun dant, & prorsus nihil conferunt ad sen tentiam: cuiusmodi sunt, φέρω, ἔχω, εἰμί, φαίνω, εἰπεῖν, & similia. φέρω, ut Greg. τῷ μὲν γε πλήρως φέροντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐγκατέλε- ξαν. nomina inter clericos dare cœpe runt. Chrysost. de facto concione prima: σοὶ δὲ καθάπερ ἐν ἀκροπόλει τῇ κεφαλῇ φέ ερν ὀφθαλμὸς ἐγκατέθηκεν, tibi autem in capite uelut in arce oculos imposuit. Hinc si tollas φέροντες, & φέρον, eadem manebit sententia. Ἐχω, ut μαθὼν ἔχω, pro ἐμαθον, συλλαβὼν ἔχω, pro συνέλαβον.
units.tr: Some verbs are sometimes put into a sentence, yet they are quite redundant and contribute nothing at all to the meaning. Such are φέρω, ἔχω, εἰμί, φαίνω, εἰπεῖν and the like. Take φέρω: Gregory says, "they had fully enrolled themselves" [τῷ μὲν γε πλήρως φέροντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐγκατέλεξαν], that is, "they began to give their names among the clergy." Chrysostom, in the first sermon on the statues: "but to you, as on a citadel, he has set eyes in your head" [σοὶ δὲ καθάπερ ἐν ἀκροπόλει τῇ κεφαλῇ φέρων ὀφθαλμὸς ἐγκατέθηκεν]. Hence if you remove φέροντες and φέρον, the meaning remains the same. Take ἔχω: μαθὼν ἔχω is used for ἔμαθον, and συλλαβὼν ἔχω for συνέλαβον.

units.la: Εἰμὶ, ut ἐν τῷ νυῦ ἑῖ), pro ἐν τῷ νυῦ, in ἀμί. praesentiarum. ἐκὼν εἶ), pro ἐκὼν, uoluntarius. ἐκόντες εἶ), pro ἐκόντες, uoluntarij. Φάναι & εἰπεῖν, ut ἔφη φάναι, ἔφη εἰπεῖν, pro ἔφη, quasi Latine dicas, Infit dicere. φθά-νω, ut ἔφθλω ποιήσας, pro ἐποίησα, φθάνει ἀναλισκόμενον, pro ἀναλίσκεται. ἐφθάκειν φυθόμενον, audieram. τυγχάνω, ut τυγχάνω ὤν, pro εἰμί. διατελῶ, ut διατελῶ ποιῶν, pro ποιῶ.
units.tr: Take εἰμί: ἐν τῷ νῦν εἶμι is used for ἐν τῷ νῦν, "at present"; ἑκὼν εἶμι for ἑκών, "willing"; ἑκόντες εἰσί for ἑκόντες, "willing" in the plural. Take φάναι and εἰπεῖν: ἔφη φάναι and ἔφη εἰπεῖν are used for ἔφη, as if in Latin you said infit dicere, "he begins to say." Take φθάνω: ἔφθασα ποιήσας is used for ἐποίησα, "I did"; φθάνει ἀναλισκόμενον for ἀναλίσκεται, "is consumed"; ἐφθάκειν φθόμενον means "I had heard." Take τυγχάνω: τυγχάνω ὤν is used for εἰμί, "I am." Take διατελῶ: διατελῶ ποιῶν is used for ποιῶ, "I do."

units.la: Οἶμαι, Graecis abundat, quemadmodum dum Latinis, credo. τοιαῦτα ζυλωτὰ ὄζιν οἴμαι, καὶ λαμπρὰ, huiusmodi admiranda sunt, credo, & preclara. οἴει, ut ἐν οἷς ἀναγ καθήσεται; Nonne cogetur, an non tandem cogetur?
units.tr: Οἶμαι is redundant in Greek, just as credo is in Latin. τοιαῦτα ζηλωτὰ ἔστιν οἶμαι καὶ λαμπρά means "such things are, I think, admirable and splendid." For οἴει, as in ἐν οἷς ἀναγκασθήσεται: "Surely he will be compelled, or will he not at last be compelled?"

units.la: Appendix tertia. Enallage numeri.
units.tr: Third Appendix. Enallage of number [Ἐναλλαγὴ ἀριθμοῦ].

units.la: Verbis singularibus abutuntur Atti ci loco pluralium. ἐαν ὑπονεάση, pro ὑπο-νεάσωνται. ὅπως ἐμέση, pro ἐμέσωνται.
units.tr: The Attic writers use singular verbs in place of plurals: ἐὰν ὑπονεάσῃ [if he grows young again] for ὑπονεάσωνται; ὅπως ἐμέσῃ [that he may vomit] for ἐμέσωνται.

units.la: Constructio intricatior.
units.tr: A more intricate construction.

units.la: Vtuntur Graeci frequenter implici-ta orationis structura, ἐμὲ μὴ δλον ἔχεις ἐφ' structura ὅτῳ τῶτο ποιήσεις, pro μὴ δλον ἔχεις ἐφ' ὅτῳ
units.tr: The Greeks often use an involved structure of the sentence, ἐμὲ μὴ ὅλον ἔχεις ἐφ' ὅτῳ τοῦτο ποιήσεις, for μὴ ὅλον ἔχεις ἐφ' ὅτῳ [you have no reason why you should do this for me].

units.la: Enallage numeri. μὴ ἔτο ποιήσεις, Nihil habes quamobrem hoc mihi facias. ἐδὲις ἐκὼν ὑποµένει τὴν ἐλαυθέρων τῶν τοιούτων ἀρχῶν, pro ἐδεὶς τ' ἐλαυθέρων ἐκὼν ὑποµένει, &c. Nemo liber uolens perfert huiusmodi principatum. ὅταν μὴ εἰδότες βασιλεύωμεν, pro μὴ εἰδότες ὅταν βασιλεύωμεν, Ignorantes quando eamus.
units.tr: Enallage of number. You have nothing for which you should do this for me [μὴ ἔτο ποιήσεις]. No free man willingly endures rule of this kind [ἐδεὶς ἐκὼν ὑποµένει τὴν ἐλευθέρων τῶν τοιούτων ἀρχῶν], for ἐδεὶς τ' ἐλευθέρων ἐκὼν ὑπομένει, etc. Not knowing when we are to go [ὅταν μὴ εἰδότες βασιλεύωμεν], for μὴ εἰδότες ὅταν βασιλεύωμεν.

units.la: Infinitiuus
units.tr: The infinitive.

units.la: Infinitiuus præpofito articulo neutro, naturam nominis induit, τὸ φιλοσοφεῖν ἀνδρὸς ἐλαυθέρου, & materialiter capitur, sicut etiam aliæ dictiones, & orationes quandoque, τὸ ἀνθρώπῳ, θεῖον μάθη μα, τὸ γνῶμαί τινα σαυτόν.
units.tr: The infinitive, when preceded by the neuter article, takes on the nature of a noun: τὸ φιλοσοφεῖν ἀνδρὸς ἐλευθέρου ["to philosophize belongs to a free man"]. It is also taken materially, as other words and sometimes whole sentences are: τὸ ἀνθρώπῳ, θεῖον μάθημα, τὸ γνῶθι σαυτόν ["the 'to man', the divine lesson, the 'know yourself'"].

units.la: Item particula ἀν Optatiuo uel Subiunctiuo adiicitur, & potentiam denotat, τῶτο ἂν γένοιτο uel γένηται, Hoc factu esset possibile. Non raro Indicatiuo ἐλε-γον ἄν, ἐγεγράφειν ἄν. Quandoque non expressa apud poetas subintelligitur. ἦλθον uenissem, pro ἦλθον ἄν. Theocr. 1. Idyll.
units.tr: Likewise the particle ἄν is added to the optative or subjunctive and denotes possibility: τοῦτο ἂν γένοιτο or γένηται, "this would be possible." Not infrequently it is added to the indicative: ἔλεγον ἄν, ἐγεγράφειν ἄν ["I would have said," "I would have written"]. Sometimes among the poets it is understood though not expressed: ἦλθον, "I would have come," for ἦλθον ἄν. Theocr. 1. Idyll.

units.la: Infin. cum articulo.
units.tr: The infinitive with the article.

units.la: Partic. ἄν.
units.tr: The participle with ἄν.

units.la: CONSTRVCTIO PARTICIPII.
units.tr: The Construction of the Participle.

units.la: PARTICIPIVM sortitur constructionem sui verbi, quemadmodum apud Latinos.
units.tr: The participle takes the construction of its own verb, as it does in Latin.

units.la: Poetica ἀντιμέρεια.
units.tr: Poetic antimeria.

units.la: Caeterum illud, τόξων εὖ εἰδὼς, Poeticum est, per antimeriam: ac si dicamus, τόξων εἰδ᾽ ἡμῶν, arcuum peritus, hoc est, peritus sagittandi.
units.tr: The phrase τόξων εὖ εἰδὼς [skilled with bows] is poetic, by antimeria. It is as if we said τόξων εἰδ᾽ ἡμῶν [skilled in bows], that is, skilled at shooting.

units.la: Participium absolute sumptum.
units.tr: The participle taken absolutely.

units.la: Genitiuus participij absolute ponitur, ἐμοῦ διδάσκοντος, me docente.
units.tr: The genitive of the participle is used absolutely: ἐμοῦ διδάσκοντος [me teaching], that is, with me teaching.

units.la: Attice pro hoc genitiuo est accusatiuus, & fere cum ὡς & ὥσπερ. ὡς τ' ἀνδρα τὸ τὸ ποιήσαντα, pro τᾶ ἀνδρὸς τὸ τὸ ποιήσαν τῷ, uiro hoc faciente.
units.tr: In Attic, the accusative stands in place of this genitive, and it is used nearly always with ὡς and ὥσπερ: ὡς τ' ἀνδρα τὸ τὸ ποιήσαντα [as for the man doing this], for τᾶ ἀνδρὸς τὸ τὸ ποιήσαν τῷ [for the man doing this], that is, with the man doing this.

units.la: Item Nominatiuus absolute sumptus.
units.tr: Likewise the nominative taken absolutely.

units.la: Etiam Nominatiuus singularis participij neutri generis, ἀκουσάν αὐτό, pro ἀκούσαντος αὐτοῦ. Λέον ἑτερα, pro λεόντων ἑτέρων, cum aliae res conuenirent, ὅξον αὐτὸ ποιῆσαι. ὡς μὴ λέγειν αὐτὸ διαφέρον, tanquam nihil eius interfit. ἐνὸν, ᾧ ϑεῷσῆκοι, παρὸν, ἐνδεχόμενον.
units.tr: The singular nominative of a participle of the neuter gender is also used: ἀκουσάν αὐτό [having heard it], for ἀκούσαντος αὐτοῦ [him having heard]. Λέον ἑτερα [other things], for λεόντων ἑτέρων [other things], when other matters were agreed. ὅξον αὐτὸ ποιῆσαι [to make it sharp]. ὡς μὴ λέγειν αὐτὸ διαφέρον [not to say it matters], as if none of it concerned him. ἐνὸν, ᾧ ϑεῷ σῆκοι [it being possible], παρὸν [being present], ἐνδεχόμενον [admitting of].

units.la: Participium loco uerbi.
units.tr: The participle in place of a verb.

units.la: Fit autem nonnunquam, ut participium coniunctum nomini substantiuo, in obliquo ponatur loco uerbi & nominatiui, idq; propter alium obliquū praecedentem, νομίζω σε, ὡς φίλον μου γνόμενον, pro ὡς φίλῳ μὲ ἐγνοῦ, Puto quod sis factus amicus meus. πιστεύω ἡμᾶς, ὡς ἔχον τας τὴν τῆς Θεοῦ βασιλείαν, pro ὡς ἐχομὲν τὴν τῆς θεῖς βασιλείαν. ἡ γραφὴ λέγει ὡς τ' γυναικὸς, ὡς αἰτίας γνομένης τ' ἁμαρτημάτων, pro ὡς αἰτία ἐγένετο τῆς ἁμαρτημάτων. τὸ τ' ἐστιν τῆς ἀνθρώπων ἵππων, ἡ ὄντων γνομένων, pro οἱ ἵπποι καὶ ὄνοι ἐγένοντο.
units.tr: It sometimes happens that a participle joined to a substantive is put in the oblique case in place of a verb and a nominative, and this on account of another oblique case preceding. νομίζω σε, ὡς φίλον μου γνόμενον [I think you have become my friend], for ὡς φίλῳ μὲ ἐγνοῦ [that you have become a friend to me]: Puto quod sis factus amicus meus. πιστεύω ἡμᾶς, ὡς ἔχον τας τὴν τῆς Θεοῦ βασιλείαν [I believe us to hold the kingdom of God], for ὡς ἐχομὲν τὴν τῆς θεῖς βασιλείαν [that we hold the kingdom of God]. ἡ γραφὴ λέγει ὡς τ' γυναικὸς, ὡς αἰτίας γνομένης τ' ἁμαρτημάτων [Scripture says of the woman that she became the cause of sins], for ὡς αἰτία ἐγένετο τῆς ἁμαρτημάτων [that she was the cause of sins]. τὸ τ' ἐστιν τῆς ἀνθρώπων ἵππων, ἡ ὄντων γνομένων [the horses of men, or the asses that came to be], for οἱ ἵπποι καὶ ὄνοι ἐγένοντο [the horses and asses came to be].

units.la: Συνοίδα ἑμαυτῷ μὴ ϑεῷ ἀποιεμένῳ, pro συνοίδα ἑμαυτῷ, ὅτι μὴ ϑεῷ ἀποιεῖμαι. Conscius sum mihi, quod non dissimulem.
units.tr: Συνοίδα ἑμαυτῷ μὴ ϑεῷ ἀποιεμένῳ [I am conscious to myself of not refusing God], for συνοίδα ἑμαυτῷ, ὅτι μὴ ϑεῷ ἀποιεῖμαι [I am conscious that I do not refuse God]. Conscius sum mihi, quod non dissimulem [I am conscious to myself that I do not dissemble].

units.la: Idem loco Coniunctiui praeteriti,
units.tr: The same in place of the perfect subjunctive.

units.la: Et loco coniunctiui praeteriti perfecti actiui plerunque utuntur Graeci Participijs, ἐὰν ἀδικηθῶσιν τυγχάνῃ, Si iniuria fecerit, ἐὰν τύχῃ πεπλανημένως, Si lactauerit. ὅταν ὦσι βεβλημένοι τὰς ὀδόντας, cum ceciderint dentes.
units.tr: Greek writers very often use participles in place of the perfect active subjunctive: ἐὰν ἀδικηθῶσιν τυγχάνῃ [if they should be wronged], "if he should be wronged"; ἐὰν τύχῃ πεπλανημένως [if he should have strayed], "if he should have gone astray"; ὅταν ὦσι βεβλημένοι τὰς ὀδόντας [when the teeth have fallen out], "when the teeth have fallen".

units.la: Loco Optatiui.
units.tr: In place of the optative.

units.la: Quod etiam fit nonnunquã in Optatiuis, συμβεβηκὼς ἂν εἴη, contigisse uidea tur, γενόμενος ἂν εἴη, facti esse uideantur. Et in Futuris Indicatiui, ἐπιτετυχηκὼς ἔσῃ, pro ἐπιτεύξῃ. κεχαεισμένος ἔσῃ, pro χαρίσῃ.
units.tr: This also happens sometimes with the optative: συμβεβηκὼς ἂν εἴη [he would seem to have happened], "he would seem to have come about"; γενόμενος ἂν εἴη [they would seem to have been made], "they would seem to have become". And in the future indicative: ἐπιτετυχηκὼς ἔσῃ [you will have obtained], for ἐπιτεύξῃ [you will obtain]; κεχαρισμένος ἔσῃ [you will have granted a favour], for χαρίσῃ [you will grant].

units.la: Atticorum mos loquendi.
units.tr: The custom of the Attic writers.

units.la: Et Atticis idem fit in omnibus tem-poribus ac modis, adiunctis his uerbis: τυγχάνω, εἰμί, ὑπάρχω. τίς σὺ τυγχάνεις ὤν; Quis tu es ? ἀπεκτανὼς ἐσι τὸν ἀνθρωπον, Interfecit hominem, ἀνηρηκὼς ἔσομαι, fu-stulero. ἀλλ' ἐχθρὸς γε ὑπῆρχεν ὤν, Non erat quidem inimicus. ἔσεσθε ἐνηφισμένοι, censueritis.
units.tr: The Attics do the same in all tenses and moods, when these verbs are added: τυγχάνω, εἰμί, ὑπάρχω. τίς σὺ τυγχάνεις ὤν; [who are you?] "Who are you?" ἀπεκτανὼς ἐσι τὸν ἀνθρωπον [he has killed the man], "He killed the man." ἀνηρηκὼς ἔσομαι [I shall have destroyed], "I shall have slain." ἀλλ' ἐχθρὸς γε ὑπῆρχεν ὤν [but he was indeed an enemy], "He was not indeed an enemy." ἔσεσθε ἐνηφισμένοι [you will have voted], "you will have decided."

units.la: Participium loco Infinitiui ponitur.
units.tr: The participle is used in place of the infinitive.

units.la: Ponitur praeterea participium non-nunquam uice uerbi Infiniti. Matth. 1. εὐρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα, pro ἔχειν, id est, Re-perta est esse grauida.
units.tr: The participle is also sometimes used in place of the infinitive verb. Matth. 1: εὐρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα [she was found with child], for ἔχειν [to have], that is, was found to be with child.

units.la: Id fit cum uerbis perseuerandi iungitur,
units.tr: This happens when it is joined with verbs of continuing.

units.la: Id quod plerunque fit cum uerbisperseuerādi, ἀγαπῶν με διαπαύει, id est, γαπᾶν με διαπαύεις, Perseuera me amare.
units.tr: This happens most often with verbs of continuing: ἀγαπῶν με διαπαύει [you cease not to love me], that is, γαπᾶν με διαπαύεις [you cease to love me]: Persevere in loving me.

units.la: Math. 11. ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων, pro διαταξαι, Cum consummasset Iesus praecipere, & praecipiedi fecisset finem.
units.tr: Matth. 11: ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς διατάσσων [when Jesus had finished giving orders], for διαταξαι [to give orders]: When Jesus had finished giving his orders, and had made an end of giving instructions.

units.la: Aut verbis desistendi.
units.tr: Or with verbs of ceasing.

units.la: Et in verbis desistendi, ἐ ꝑαύομαι φι λῶν, pro φιλεῖν, Non cessabo amare.
units.tr: And with verbs of ceasing: ἐ ꝑαύομαι φιλῶν [I will not cease loving], for φιλεῖν [to love]: I will not cease to love.

units.la: Vel significantibus affectionem animi.
units.tr: Or with verbs signifying an emotion of the mind.

units.la: Item in verbis significantibus affecti onem animi, idque uarie, nempe in nominatiuo, aut in accusatiuo. μέμνημαι ἱσ̓ὼν, uel μέμνημαι ἱσ̓όντα, pro μέμνημαι ἱσ̓ἔιν, memini uidisse. οὐ συνίεσαν μάτλω ἀπο-νοοῦντες, uel ἀπονοῦντας, pro οὐ συνίεσαν μάτλω ἀπονεῖν, Non intellexerunt se frustra laborare. συνοιδ̓α ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικῶν, uel συνοιδ̓α ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικοῦντα, pro συνοιδ̓α ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικεῖν, Conscius sum mihi iniuriae. Aut etiam in alio quouis casu, cuius est substantiuum, aut pronomen illi adiunctu, ut συνοιδ̓α ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικοῦντι, Conscius fum mihi iniuriae.
units.tr: Likewise with verbs signifying an emotion of the mind, and this in various ways, namely in the nominative or in the accusative. μέμνημαι ἱσ̓ὼν [I remember having seen] or μέμνημαι ἱσ̓όντα, for μέμνημαι ἱσ̓ἔιν [I remember to have seen]: memini uidisse. οὐ συνίεσαν μάτλω ἀπονοοῦντες [they did not understand that they laboured in vain], or ἀπονοῦντας, for οὐ συνίεσαν μάτλω ἀπονεῖν [they did not understand that they were labouring in vain]: They did not understand that they were labouring in vain. συνοιδα ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικῶν [I am conscious to myself of doing wrong], or συνοιδα ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικοῦντα, for συνοιδα ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικεῖν [I am conscious to myself of wronging]: I am conscious to myself of wrongdoing. Or also in any other case, to which the substantive or a pronoun is joined, as συνοιδα ἑμαυτῷ ἀδικοῦντι [I am conscious to myself of wronging]: I am conscious to myself of having done wrong.

units.la: Sic Verg.
units.tr: So Virgil.

units.la: Senfit medios delapfus in hoftes:pro delapfum effe.
units.tr: Senserit medios delapsus in hostes: he perceived that he had slipped into the midst of the enemy, for delapsum esse [to have slipped].

units.la: Appendix.
units.tr: Appendix.

units.la: Participium factum nomen.
units.tr: The participle made a noun.

units.la: Participia transeunt quandoque in nomina, et illorum more construuntur, non ut participia, τὸ καθηκον σε, Officium tuum.
units.tr: Participles sometimes pass over into nouns, and are construed in the manner of nouns and not as participles: τὸ καθῆκον σε [your duty], "your duty."

units.la: Participium παρέλκει.
units.tr: The participle as superfluous (παρέλκει).

units.la: Et quandoque superuacue ponūtur, sic ut ipsis substractis eadē maneret sententia, ὤχόμλω ἀπίων, pro ὤχόμλω. οἴχεται ἀπιών, pro οἴχετα. παίζεις ἔχων, pro παίζς. φλυαρεῖς ἔχων, pro φλυαρεῖς. λπρεῖς ἔχων, pro λπρεῖς. τουτῷ ἔχων, pro τουτῷ, nunc.
units.tr: Sometimes they are used superfluously, so that with them removed the sense would remain the same: ὤχόμλω ἀπίων [I went away going], for ὤχόμλω [I went away]. οἴχεται ἀπιών [he has gone away going], for οἴχετα [he has gone]. παίζεις ἔχων [you are jesting, having], for παίζς [you jest]. φλυαρεῖς ἔχων [you babble, having], for φλυαρεῖς [you babble]. λπρεῖς ἔχων [you talk nonsense, having], for λπρεῖς [you talk nonsense]. τουτῷ ἔχων [having this], for τουτῷ [this], that is, now.

units.la: CONSTRVCTIO ADVERBIORVM.
units.tr: The construction of adverbs

units.la: Aduerbia cum genitiuo.
units.tr: Adverbs with the genitive.

units.la: ADVERBIA sí post se casum habent, construuntur genitiuo, πόρρω τῆς πόλεως, εἰς τὸ μη- νὸς, λάθεα χωεῖς τῶν ἄλλων, φεῦ τῆς μεγέθους.
units.tr: Adverbs that have a case after them take the genitive: far from the city [πόρρω τῆς πόλεως], of the month [εἰς τοῦ μηνός], you withdraw secretly from the others [λάθρα χωρεῖς τῶν ἄλλων], alas for the greatness [φεῦ τῆς μεγέθους].

units.la: Excipe congregandi aduerbia, &c.
units.tr: Except adverbs of gathering, etc.

units.la: Exceptis aduerbijs cōgregandi, quæ datiuo adhærēt, ἁμα τοῖς ἄλλοις. & Iurandi quae accusatiuo, νὴ, ναί, μὰ δία. Etiam deriuatiuis quae primitiuorum structuram sequuntur, ἀξιῶ λόγῳ, ἀξίως λόγου, ὁμοιῶ ὁμοίως τοῖς ἄλλοις.
units.tr: Except the adverbs of gathering, which go with the dative: together with the others [ἅμα τοῖς ἄλλοις]. Also the adverbs of swearing, which go with the accusative: [νὴ, ναί, μὰ Δία]. Likewise derivative adverbs follow the construction of their primitives: [ἀξιῶ λόγῳ, ἀξίως λόγου], [ὁμοιῶ ὁμοίως τοῖς ἄλλοις].

units.la: De aduerbijs exclamandi.
units.tr: On adverbs of exclamation

units.la: Primo de Ω.
units.tr: First, on Ω

units.la: Exceptis etiam aduerbijs exclamandi, quibus competit constructio huiusmodi, ὦ acutitonum iungitur nominatiuo, ὦ λόγε, ὦ φρενες, ὦ σωτερίας, ὦ ἐπιχειρή μάτα, uerba sunt admirantis orationem Libanij.
units.tr: Apart from these, there are also adverbs of exclamation, which take this construction. [ὦ], with the acute accent, is joined to the nominative: [ὦ λόγε], [ὦ φρένες], [ὦ σωτηρία], [ὦ ἐπιχειρήματα]. These are the words of Libanius admiring a speech.

units.la: Construitur etiam cū genitiuo, ὦ Διὸς μάτῳ, ô rei miraculum. Cui quandoq; subiicitur accusatiuus: ὦ Διύμάτῳ τὴν παρθένον τίκτουσαν τὸν Θεὸν, ô rei miraculum, uirginem parientem Deū. Sicut etiā Latini dicūt, ô diī immortales, rē miseram & calamitosam. Interdum sine casu construitur, ὦ πῶς ἀδύνατή τῷ τούτων ἐνέργειᾳ τῷ μνήμῃ.
units.tr: It is also construed with the genitive: [ὦ Διὸς μάτην], O wonder of the thing. Sometimes an accusative follows it: [ὦ Διὸς μάτην τὴν παρθένον τίκτουσαν τὸν Θεόν], O wonder of the thing, a virgin bearing God. In the same way the Latins say "O immortal gods, what a wretched and calamitous thing!" Sometimes it is construed without a case: [ὦ πῶς ἀδύνατα τῶν τούτων ἐνέργειαν τῇ μνήμῃ], O how impossible it is to hold the performance of these things in memory.

units.la: Sic Virgilius.
units.tr: So Virgil.

units.la: O cohibete iras. Et, O quae iā satis ima dehiscat terra mihi. ὦ circunflexū cum uocatiuo, ὦ Απολλον, ô Apollo. Vtun-
units.tr: Thus Virgil: "O, restrain your anger!" And: "O, may the earth now open deep enough for me!" The circumflex ō is used with the vocative: [ὦ Ἄπολλον], O Apollo.

units.la: Vtuntur Græci in inuocationibus genitiuo & uocatiuo eo loco, quo Latini accusatiuo & uocatiuo, ὦ Απολλον δαιμονίας ἐυβολῆς, ô Apollo magnam fœlicitatem. Quem uocatiuum mutant interdum in genitiuum, precedente præpositione θεὸς, ὦ θεὸς τ̃ ἱεῶν τ̃ συμφορᾶς ô Dij, rem calamitosam.
units.tr: In invocations the Greeks use the genitive and the vocative where the Latins use the accusative and the vocative: [ὦ Ἄπολλον δαιμονίας εὐβολῆς], O Apollo, great good fortune. They sometimes change the vocative into the genitive when the word θεός precedes: [ὦ θεὸς τῶν ἱερῶν τῆς συμφορᾶς], O gods, a calamitous matter.

units.la: De ΦΕΥ.
units.tr: On ΦΕΥ

units.la: Φεῦ cum genitiuo, φεῦ τ̃ ἀτιμίας, Heu ignominiam.
units.tr: φεῦ with the genitive: [φεῦ τῆς ἀτιμίας], alas for the dishonour.

units.la: De OIMOI.
units.tr: On OIMOI

units.la: οἴμοι, recto & genitiuo. Recto, οἴμοι ἠχηοδαίμων, ὡς ἀπολωλα, Heu infelix, ut periȷ. Genitiuo, Lucianus, οἴμοι τ̃ ἀγρῶν uerba sunt deplorantis agros perditos. Ponitur etiam sine casu, οἴμοι, heu mihi.
units.tr: [οἴμοι] takes the nominative and the genitive. With the nominative: [οἴμοι ἀθλιοδαίμων, ὡς ἀπόλωλα], alas, unhappy wretch, I am undone. With the genitive, Lucian: [οἴμοι τῶν ἀγρῶν], words of one lamenting ruined fields. It is also used without a case: [οἴμοι], alas for me.

units.la: Loco exclamationis ponitur nonnunquam solus genitiuus, ut dictum est superius.
units.tr: Instead of an exclamation, the genitive alone is sometimes used, as was said above.

units.la: APTI.
units.tr: ἌΡΤΙ

units.la: ἀρτι construitur omnibus temporib. dempto futuro. ἀρτι ποιῶ ἐποίουν, ἐποίησα, ποιήσω, ποιήσω, &c.
units.tr: [ἄρτι] is construed with all tenses except the future: [ἄρτι ποιῶ, ἐποίουν, ἐποίησα, ποιήσω], etc.

units.la: AΥΘΙΣ & ΕΙΣΑΕΙ.
units.tr: ΑΥΘΙΣ & ΕΙΣΑΕΙ

units.la: Αὔθις & εἰσαεὶ adscifcunt futurum. εἰ-σαεὶ ἑξει κίνησις, semper erit motus, αὖθις διδάξω, Rursus docebo.
units.tr: [αὖθις] and [εἰσαεὶ] take the future: [εἰσαεὶ ἕξει κίνησις], there will always be motion; [αὖθις διδάξω], I will teach again.

units.la: AΥΤΙΚΑ.
units.tr: ΑΥΤΙΚΑ

units.la: Αὐτίκα construitur omnibus tempo-ribus, dempto futuro.
units.tr: [αὐτίκα] is construed with all tenses except the future.

units.la: ΕΩΣ.
units.tr: ΕΩΣ

units.la: ἕως, quandiu, gaudet Indicatiuo. ἕως ἕξη, quandiu uiuebat.
units.tr: [ἕως], as long as, takes the indicative: [ἕως ἔζη], as long as he was living.

units.la: Et coniunctiuo, ἕως κρύπτηται, quan-diu occultetur.
units.tr: It also takes the subjunctive: [ἕως κρύπτηται], as long as it is kept hidden.

units.la: ἕως ἄν coniunctiuo: & ubi loquimur de re præterita, optatiuo, ἕως ἂν γένηται. quādiu fiat, ἕως ἂν γένοιτο, quandiu fieret.
units.tr: [ἕως ἄν] takes the subjunctive; when we speak of past matter, the optative: [ἕως ἂν γένηται], as long as it happens; [ἕως ἂν γένοιτο], as long as it might happen.

units.la: Construitur etiam ἕως, & ἕως ἄν, infini-tiuis, ἕως ἀπαγγείλεσθαι, donec porrigam.
units.tr: [ἕως] and [ἕως ἄν] are also construed with the infinitive: [ἕως ἀπαγγείλεσθαι], until I stretch forth.

units.la: MEXPI & AXPI.
units.tr: ΜΕΧΡΙ & ΑΧΡΙ

units.la: μέχρι & ἄχρι, ad hunc ferè modũ con-struuntur cum cæteris orationis partí-bus, μέχρι παντὸς, sine præfinitione tem-poris. Sicut ἐξ ἀεὶ παντὸς, μέχρι τινὸς, quous-que. μέχρι εἰς τὸ τέλος, usque ad finem. μέχρι πόρρω, diu, μέχρι ἀρτίως, nuper pri-mũ, μέχρις ἐνταῦθα, μέχρις τότε, hactenus.
units.tr: [μέχρι] and [ἄχρι] are construed with the other parts of speech in roughly this way: [μέχρι παντός], without any fixed time; [μέχρι τινός], how far; [μέχρι εἰς τὸ τέλος], to the end; [μέχρι πόρρω], far; [μέχρι ἀρτίως], only just now; [μέχρις ἐνταῦθα], [μέχρις τότε], hitherto.

units.la: μέχρις ἕως αὖ, quoad. μέχρι πέρ αὖ ἕ, quousque. μέχρις αὖ, & ἄχρις αὖ, quandiu μέχρι οὗ, & ἄχρι οὗ, quoad quousque. Et construitur plerunque Indicatiuo, μέχρι τοῦ, & ἄχρι τοῦ, usquequo. Præponitur Infinitiuis, μέχρι πᾶν, uel ἄχρι πᾶν ἡ ἐρυθριᾶν, usque quo erubescerem.
units.tr: [μέχρις οὗ] and [ἄχρις οὗ], until; [μέχρι οὗ], [ἄχρι οὗ], as far as, until. It is usually construed with the indicative: [μέχρι τοῦ], [ἄχρι τοῦ], until when. It is placed before infinitives: [μέχρι πότε ἐρυθριᾶν], until when I should blush.

units.la: ΝΥΝ.
units.tr: ΝΥΝ

units.la: Νῶ, omnib. temporibus accommodatur, præter plusquamperfecto, νῦν ᾧ ἐσόμαι, νῦν πεφεύγταγ, νῦν ἐξαπόλωλε, νῦν ἐπόνουν, νῦν ἐνίκησε. Et non est inchoatiuum orationis, sed semper coiunctioni δὲ coniungitur, ᾤμην ταῦτ' εἶπεῖν ἐρεῖν, νῦν δὲ ἐδὲ τότων εἶρηκε.
units.tr: [νῦν] fits all tenses except the pluperfect: [νῦν ὢν ἐσόμαι], [νῦν πεφεύγει], [νῦν ἐξαπόλωλε], [νῦν ἐπόνουν], [νῦν ἐνίκησε]. It is not an opening word of a sentence, but is always joined with [δὲ]: [ᾤμην ταῦτ' εἰπεῖν], I thought to say these things; [νῦν δὲ ἐδὲ τοῦτων εἴρηκε], but now he has said nothing of these things.

units.la: ΗΔΗ.
units.tr: ΗΔΗ

units.la: ἤδη, quando significat tempus, solum constuitur imperfecto, ἤδη ἐγράφον. Et Indefinito, ἤδη ἐγράψα, & plusquamperfecto, ἤδη ἐγεγράφειν.
units.tr: [ἤδη], when it signifies time, is construed only with the imperfect: [ἤδη ἔγραφον], I was already writing. It is also used with the aorist, [ἤδη ἔγραψα], and with the pluperfect, [ἤδη ἐγεγράφειν].

units.la: ΠΑΛΑΙ.
units.tr: ΠΑΛΑΙ

units.la: Huic similem constructionem habet πάλαι, aduerbium πάλαι.
units.tr: [πάλαι] has a construction similar to this, as does the adverb [πάλαι].

units.la: ΟΤΕ & ΤΟΤΕ.
units.tr: ΟΤΕ & ΤΟΤΕ

units.la: ὅτε & τότε construuntur omnibus tēporibus, praeterquam perfecto, ὅτε νοῶ, ὅτε ἐνοόουν, ὅτε ἐνενοήκειν, ὅτε ἐνόησα, ὅτε νοῦν σῶ, sed non ὅτε γενόνκα.
units.tr: [ὅτε] and [τότε] are construed with all tenses except the perfect: [ὅτε νοῶ], [ὅτε ἐνόουν], [ὅτε ἐνενοήκειν], [ὅτε ἐνόησα], [ὅτε νοήσω], but not [ὅτε γεγόνα].

units.la: ΟΠΟΤΑΝ.
units.tr: ΟΠΟΤΑΝ

units.la: ὁπότ᾽ αν, cum fit sermo de re praeterita, iungitur Optatiuo, τί γὰρ ἂν καὶ πάθοιτις, ὁπόταν οἱ θεοὶ βιάζοιντο; Nam quid agetes cum diuinitus cogerere?
units.tr: [ὁπότ' ἄν], when the talk is of past matter, takes the optative: [τί γὰρ ἂν καὶ πάθοιτις, ὁπόταν οἱ θεοὶ βιάζοιντο;] For what would they do, when they were compelled by the gods?

units.la: ΣΗΜΕΡΟΝ.
units.tr: ΣΗΜΕΡΟΝ

units.la: Σήμερον, omnibus temporibus adiungitur, praeterquam plusquamperfecto & futuro.
units.tr: [σήμερον] is joined with all tenses except the pluperfect and the future.

units.la: ΟΥΔΕΠΟΤΕ.
units.tr: ΟΥΔΕΠΟΤΕ

units.la: Οὐδέποτε, solum construitur praeteri to, τοῦτ᾽ οὐδέποτε ἐγένετο, hoc nunquam contigit.
units.tr: [οὐδέποτε] is construed only with the past tense: [τοῦτ' οὐδέποτε ἐγένετο], this never happened.

units.la: ΠΡΙΝ.
units.tr: ΠΡΙΝ

units.la: πρὶν construitur praeterito Indicatiui. Πρὶν εἰπεῖν, priusquam dixit. Et Infinitiuo, πρὶν εἰπεῖν, priusquam diceret. Quod fit intercedente ἢ. Matth. 1. πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτούς, priusquam ipsi conuenirent. Quemadmodum interuenit ἂν cum additur coniunctiuo in re futura, aut Optatiuo in re praeterita. πρὶν ἂν γέ-νηται, υητα, priusquam fiat. πεὶν ἂν γένοιτο, priusquam fieret. Iungitur etiam πεὶν ἢ Optatiuo & Coniunctiuo in re praeterita. πεὶν ἢ γένοιτο, & πεὶν ἢ γένη, priusquam fieret. Iungitur etiam in eodem sensu Indicatiuo, πεὶν ἔλυσε, priusquam absoluēret.
units.tr: [πρὶν] is construed with the past indicative: [πρὶν εἰπεῖν], before he spoke. It is also construed with the infinitive: [πρὶν εἰπεῖν], before he should speak. This happens with [ἢ] intervening. Matthew 1: [πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτούς], before they came together. As [ἂν] intervenes when it is added to the subjunctive for future matter, or to the optative for past matter: before it happens [πρὶν ἂν γένηται]; before it might happen [πρὶν ἂν γένοιτο]. [πρὶν ἢ] is also used with the optative and the subjunctive in past matter: before it might happen [πρὶν ἢ γένοιτο], and before it happened [πρὶν ἢ γένη]. It is also used in the same sense with the indicative: before he released [πρὶν ἔλυσε].

units.la: Aduerbiorum nonnullorum relatio.
units.tr: Some adverbs and their correlatives.

units.la: Quemadmodum nominibus τοῖος, τό οῖος, πηλίκος, respondent οἷος, ὅσος, ηλί-κος. Sic aduerbijs τῆμος, τότε, τέως, τηνίκα, τόφρα, respondent ἡμος, ὅτε, ἕως, νίνικα, ὄφρα. Et in Syntaxi sese mutuo praecedūt et sequuntur, quemadmodum illa nomina. τόφρα δ' ἐς ὅτι ζώεσι τίθει κεάτος, ὄφρ' αὐ ἀχαιοὶ ὑὸν ἐμὸν τίσωσι, Eousque Troia nis uires adde, quousque Graeci filium honorent meum.
units.tr: Just as the nouns τοῖος, τό οῖος, πηλίκος correspond to οἷος, ὅσος, ηλί-κος, so the adverbs τῆμος, τότε, τέως, τηνίκα, τόφρα correspond to ἡμος, ὅτε, ἕως, νίνικα, ὄφρα. In syntax, too, they go before and after one another, as those nouns do. Homer: "τόφρα δ' ἐς ὅτι ζώουσι τίθει κράτος, ὄφρ' αὐ Ἀχαιοὶ υἱὸν ἐμὸν τίσωσι" [So long as they live, grant strength to the Trojans, until the Greeks pay honour to my son].

units.la: LOCALIA.
units.tr: Local adverbs.

units.la: Atticismus.
units.tr: Atticism.

units.la: Atticis aduerbiorū localium circunstantiae confunduntur, ita ut quae significant ad locum, ponantur pro significantibus in loco, & contra, ut οἶκλον, pro οἴκοι. ἔνδοθεν, pro οἴκοθ. Quomodo Vergil. Eiectum littore egentem sufcepi, dixit, pro Eiectum ad littus.
units.tr: Among the Attic writers the circumstances of local adverbs are confused, so that words that signify motion towards a place are put for words that signify being in a place, and the reverse. Thus οἶκλον is put for οἴκοι (at home), and ἔνδοθεν for οἴκοθ (from home). So Virgil says "Eiectum littore egentem suscepi" (I took in the needy man cast out on the shore), meaning "cast out to the shore."

units.la: Qualitatis.
units.tr: Of quality.

units.la: Aduerbia qualitatis gaudent his uerbis, ἔχω, δέομαι, & similibus, ἐνδεὴς ἔχω, indigeo. πονηρῶς ἔχω, uel δύσκολα ... ma le affectus sum.
units.tr: Adverbs of quality go with verbs such as ἔχω (I am), δέομαι (I need) and similar ones: ἐνδεὴς ἔχω (I am in want, I lack). πονηρῶς ἔχω (I am in a bad way) or δύσκολα ... (I am ill affected).

units.la: Quibus addi poteft genitiuus fignificans id quod afficitur, οὕτως ἔχω γνώμης, fic animo affectus fum. πονηρῶς ἔχω τ σῶ μ[?]τ, male affectus fum corpore.
units.tr: To these can be added a genitive signifying that by which one is affected: οὕτως ἔχω γνώμης (I am thus disposed in mind), so I am affected in mind. πονηρῶς ἔχω τῷ σώματι (I am ill in body), that is, I am ill in body.

units.la: ΠΛΗΝ.
units.tr: Πλήν (except).

units.la: Exceptionis aduerbium πλὴν, quan do conftruitur cum genitiuo ualet præ ter, πλὴν ἀλλων, præter alios. Sine geniti uo quandoque fignificat præterquam.
units.tr: The adverb of exception πλήν, when it is construed with the genitive, means "besides": πλὴν ἄλλων (besides others). Without a genitive it sometimes means "except that."

units.la: Lucianus de sacrificiis, αἱ ἡ θυσίαι τῆ παρ' ἐκείνοις αἱ ἄντα, πλὴν ὅτι πενθῶσι τὸ ἱερεῖον, sacrificia apud illos sunt eadem, præter quam quod hostiam lugeant. Quandoque uerum, ueruntamen. Matth. 26. παρελθέτω ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο. πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω, Transfeat à me calix hic: ueruntamen non ut ego uolo. Quod idem nonnunquam fignificat, ubi cōstruitur cum
units.tr: Lucian, in his work on sacrifices: "The sacrifices among them are the same as those of the others, except that they mourn the victim" (αἱ θυσίαι ... πλὴν ὅτι πενθῶσι τὸ ἱερεῖον). Sometimes it means "but yet" or "nevertheless." Matt. 26: "Let this cup pass from me; nevertheless not as I will" (παρελθέτω ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω). Sometimes it has the same sense when it is construed with ἀλλά.

units.la: Verum. Notes beside the final paragraph of the page. cum ἀλλὰ. Lucian. in ludi. dearum, οὐχ ὅτι διδῷς τὰ ἡμέτερα, πάλιν ἀλλ' ἀπιθι, veruntamen abi.
units.tr: "Verum." (A marginal note beside the last paragraph of the page.) With ἀλλά. Lucian, in the Dialogues of the Gods: "Not that you give me my due, but go away, nevertheless" (οὐχ ὅτι διδῷς τὰ ἡμέτερα, πάλιν ἀλλ' ἄπιθι), "but yet go away."

units.la: Πάλιν abundans.
units.tr: Πάλιν used redundantly.

units.la: Nonnunquam etiam abundat in oratione, ueluti cũ πάλιν ἀλλ' ἥ, ponitur pro ἀλλ' ἥ, & πάλιν εἰ μὴ, pro εἰ μὴ, ut Aristot. prim. Metaph. ἀνθρωπον ὑγιάζει ὁ ἰατρῶν, πάλιν ἀλλ' ἥ κατὰ συμβεβηκός. Is qui medetur nō sanat hominem, nisi per accidens. Sic etiam χωρὶς εἰ μὴ, non plus ualet quàm εἰ μή.
units.tr: Sometimes too it is redundant in a sentence, as when πάλιν ἀλλ' ἤ is used for ἀλλ' ἤ, and πάλιν εἰ μή for εἰ μή. Aristotle, in the first book of the Metaphysics: "The physician does not heal a man, except by accident" (ἀνθρωπον ὑγιάζει ὁ ἰατρῶν, πάλιν ἀλλ' ἤ κατὰ συμβεβηκός). So too χωρὶς εἰ μή has no more force than εἰ μή.

units.la: Οὕτω sæpe subauditur.
units.tr: Οὕτω is often understood.

units.la: His contrarium est in aduerbio similitudinis οὕτω, quod frequenter non expressum, subauditur: ut Matth. 6. ἐλθάτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, pro οὕτω καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Fiat uoluntas tua quemadmodū in coelo, ita & in terra. et Ioan. 20. καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέ με ὁ πατὴρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς, pro καὶ οὕτως ἐγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς. Quemadmodū misit me pater, ita etiam ego mitto uos.
units.tr: The opposite happens with the adverb of likeness οὕτω, which is often not expressed but understood: as in Matt. 6: "Let your kingdom come, let your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth" (ἐλθάτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς), for οὕτω καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς: "Thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven." And John 20: "As the Father has sent me, so also I send you" (καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέ με ὁ πατήρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς), for καὶ οὕτως ἐγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς: "As the Father sent me, even so I send you."

units.la: Dicitur etiā οὕτως ὄναιο, quod est bene precantis, sicut Latinis, Macte uirtute.
units.tr: Also οὕτως ὄναιο is used, which is a form of blessing, like the Latin "Macte virtute" (may you prosper in your virtue).

units.la: Ως.
units.tr: Ὡς.

units.la: ὡς præponitur superlatiuis, ὡς λαμ-πρότατον, quàm splendidissimum, ὡς τάχιστα, simul ut.
units.tr: ὡς is placed before superlatives: ὡς λαμπρότατον, as splendid as possible; ὡς τάχιστα, as quickly as possible, at the same time as.

units.la: ΩΣ ΩΤΙ
units.tr: ὡς ὅτι

units.la: Quod etiam fit intercedente ὅτι, ὡς ὅτι λευκότατον, per quàm candidum.
units.tr: This also happens with ὅτι intervening: ὡς ὅτι λευκότατον, exceedingly white.

units.la: ὡς postpositum.
units.tr: ὡς placed after.

units.la: Quàdoqʒ etiam postponitur, & tum significat λίαν. ἐχαρφυῶς μὴν ἔν, ἔφη, ὡς βούλομαι, magnopere, inquit, cupio. Θαυμαστῶς ὡς ἀθλιώτατα γέγονε, Mirum in modum miser factus est. Θαυμαστῶς ὡς ἐπεθύμησα, Mirum in modum petij.
units.tr: It is also sometimes placed after, and then it means λίαν (very much). ἐχαρφυῶς μὴν ἔν, ἔφη, ὡς βούλομαι: "I desire it greatly, he said." Θαυμαστῶς ὡς ἀθλιώτατα γέγονε: "He has become wretchedly miserable, wonderfully so." Θαυμαστῶς ὡς ἐπεθύμησα: "I desired it wonderfully."

units.la: In quo etiá significato nonnunquam præponitur, ὡς ἀλλοτρίως, quàm uere, ὡς ἑτέρως, longe aliter.
units.tr: In this same sense it is sometimes placed before: ὡς ἀλλοτρίως, truly; ὡς ἑτέρως, quite otherwise.

units.la: ὡς pro ὥςτε.
units.tr: ὡς for ὥστε.

units.la: Si uero præponatur Infinitiuo, ualet ὥστε. ὅπως ὅδε ἀπαιδεύτῳ, ὡς μηδὲν εἰδέναι, Tam est ineruditus, ut nihil sciat.
units.tr: But if it is placed before an infinitive, it has the force of ὥστε (so that). ὅπως ὅδε ἀπαιδεύτῳ, ὡς μηδὲν εἰδέναι: "He is so uneducated that he knows nothing."

units.la: ὡς pro πρὸς Attice.
units.tr: ὡς for πρός in Attic.

units.la: Atticis autem cõstruitur accusatiuis pro πρὸς, & pro εἰς, ὡς Λακεδαιμονίους, ad Lacedæmonios. ὡς μακεδονίαν, ad Macedoniam. ΩΣ
units.tr: Among the Attics, however, it is construed with accusatives for πρός and for εἰς: ὡς Λακεδαιμονίους, to the Lacedaemonians; ὡς Μακεδονίαν, to Macedonia.

units.la: Ω Σ.
units.tr: Ὡς.

units.la: ὡς acutitonum, idem est quod ὅτως. Vnde illud, ἐςιν ὡς, pro quodammodo, & quadantenus ponitur, ut dictum est superius.
units.tr: ὡς with an acute accent has the same meaning as ὅτως (thus). Hence ἐστιν ὡς is used for "in a certain way" and "to some extent," as was said above.

units.la: ὡς digressiuum aduerbium.
units.tr: ὡς as a digressive adverb.

units.la: ὡς aduerbium digressiuum ccnstrui tur Indicatiuis, ὡς λέγει, itaque dicit, idem Attice.
units.tr: The digressive adverb ὡς is construed with the indicative: ὡς λέγει, so he says; the same in Attic.

units.la: Et optatiuis, ὡς λέγοι ἄν, itaque dicat.
units.tr: And with the optative: ὡς λέγοι ἄν, so he might say.

units.la: Et infinitiuo, ὡς λέγειν.
units.tr: And with the infinitive: ὡς λέγειν.

units.la: ὡς Similitudinis aduerbium.
units.tr: ὡς as an adverb of similarity.

units.la: Significas autem similitudinem, aut æquiparantiam, construitur tā post nomen, quàm post aduerbium.
units.tr: When it signifies similarity or equivalence, it is construed both after a noun and after an adverb.

units.la: Post nomen, ut τοιοῦτός ἐςιν, ὡς τε καὶ νο= ὡς ἐςι post ἐν, καὶ λέγειν τὰ λέοντα, Talis est ut cogitet, & dicat quæ oportet. τηλικοῦτός ἐςιν, ὡς τε πάντας ὑπερβάλλειν, Tatus est, ut omnes superet.
