units.tr: After a noun, as τοιοῦτός ἐστιν, ὡς τε καὶ νοεῖν (ὡς ἐστι after ἐν), and λέγειν τὰ δέοντα: "He is such that he thinks and says what is fitting." τηλικοῦτός ἐστιν, ὡς τε πάντας ὑπερβάλλειν: "He is so great that he surpasses all."

units.la: Post aduerbium ἔτως, ὡς πάντας ἄν Post adu. μάζει, sic ut omnes admirentur.
units.tr: After the adverb ἔτως: ὡς πάντας ἂν θαυμάζει, so that all admire. (After the adverb, as ὡς πάντας ἂν θαυμάζειν: so that everyone would admire.)

units.la: De negatiuis & prohibitiuis.
units.tr: On negatives and prohibitives.

units.la: In orationibus negatiuis Græci ple= runque præponunt negationē utrique uer= bo, quam Latini duntaxat alteri præponunt, ὃ φημί σε εἰδέναι, pro φημί σε οὐκ εἰδέναι. Dico te nescire, μὴ ἀγνοεῖν τοῦτο εἰδέναι, pro ἀγνοοῦμαι τὸ μὴ εἰδέναι. Dissimulo hoc scire. ὃ ἀξιῶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν, pro ἀξιῶ τοῦτο μὴ ποιεῖν, Indignum puto hoc facere. ὃ νομίζω εἶ, pro νομίζω μὴ εἶναι, οὐκ οἶομαι ὃ δ᾽ εἶν, pro οἶομαι ὃ δ᾽ εἶν: & sic de aliis.
units.tr: In negative sentences the Greeks mostly place the negation before both verbs, whereas the Latins place it only before one of them: ὃ φημί σε εἰδέναι, for φημί σε οὐκ εἰδέναι: "I say you do not know." μὴ ἀγνοεῖν τοῦτο εἰδέναι, for ἀγνοοῦμαι τὸ μὴ εἰδέναι: "I pretend not to know this." ὃ ἀξιῶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν, for ἀξιῶ τοῦτο μὴ ποιεῖν: "I think it unworthy to do this." ὃ νομίζω εἶναι, for νομίζω μὴ εἶναι; οὐκ οἶομαι, ὃ δ᾽ εἶν, for οἶομαι ὃ δ᾽ εἶν: and so on for the others.

units.la: Anastrophe negationis.
units.tr: Anastrophe of the negation.

units.la: Quod si quandoque inveniatur negatio postpositā verbis, hoc fit per figuram Anastrophen, κοιμησόμεθα οὐ, pro ὃ κοιμησόμεθα.
units.tr: If a negation is sometimes found placed after its verb, this happens by the figure anastrophe, as in [κοιμησόμεθα οὐ] (we shall sleep not), for [οὐ κοιμησόμεθα].

units.la: Οὐ uarie scribitur.
units.tr: The spelling of [οὐ] varies.

units.la: Si præcedat dictionem incipientem à uocali non aspirata, scribitur ὃκ, ὃκ ἔχω μαι, ὃκ ἐποίησα, ὃκ ἔσιν.
units.tr: If it precedes a word beginning with an unaspirated vowel, it is written [οὐκ], as in [οὐκ ἔχω] (I do not have), [οὐκ ἐποίησα] (I did not make), [οὐκ ἔστιν] (it is not).

units.la: Si uero præcedat eam quæ incipit à uocali aspirata, scribitur ὃχ, ὃχ ἡμεῖς, οὐχ ὁρᾷς, ὃχ ἕλκεται.
units.tr: But if it precedes a word beginning with an aspirated vowel, it is written [οὐχ], as in [οὐχ ἡμεῖς] (we not), [οὐχ ὁρᾷς] (you do not see), [οὐχ ἕλκεται] (it is not drawn).

units.la: Sed si præcedat inchoatam à consonante, scribitur ὃ, ut ὃ ποιεῖς, ὃ λέγω.
units.tr: But if it precedes a word beginning with a consonant, it is written [οὐ], as in [οὐ ποιεῖς] (you do not do), [οὐ λέγω] (I do not say).

units.la: Οὐ cum alijs partibus.
units.tr: The negation with other parts of speech.

units.la: In hunc fere modum construitur negatio gatio ἁ, cum cæteris orationis partibus peculiariter.
units.tr: The negation is construed in roughly this way with the other parts of speech, in a particular manner.

units.la: ὅσον ἁ, ὅσον ἅπω, μόνον ἁ, pro fermè, citer. ὅσον ἁδ' ἑπω, ὅσον ἁν ἡδη, pro quamprimum, iamiam. ἁ μόνον δἑ, dicunt pro, neque hunc solum, uel neque has solas, uel neque hic solus, uel neque hæc sola: & ita per omnia genera, & per omnes casus, ἀπέκτειναν τους φίλους, ἁ μόνον δἑ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν πατέρα, Occidit amicos, & nō hos solum, sed etiam patrem. ἀπολείπουσιν γε τουτες πάντες, ἁ μόνον δἑ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ, Relinquuntur omnes uicini, & non hi solum, uerumetiã pater. ἁδ᾽ εἴπ μᾶλλον, Atticis capitur pro οὐδαμῶς, uel potius pro nihilo magis. τᾶτο μὲν εἰδὼς, οὐδ' εἴπ μᾶλλον ὑπισχύμην χρήματα, Hoc cũ nouissem, nequaquam uel nihilo magis no uissem literas.
units.tr: [ὅσον οὐ], [ὅσον οὔπω], [μόνον οὐ] mean nearly, almost. [ὅσον οὐδέπω] and [ὅσον οὐκ ἤδη] mean as soon as possible, now at once. They say [οὐ μόνον δέ] for: not this one alone, nor these alone, nor this man alone, nor this woman alone; and so through all genders and all cases. For example, [ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς φίλους, οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν πατέρα]: he killed his friends, and not only these but also his father. [ἀπολείπουσιν γε τούτους πάντες, οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ πατήρ]: all the neighbours are left behind, and not only these but even the father. [οὐδ' ἔτι μᾶλλον] is used by the Attic writers for in no way, or rather for not at all more. [τοῦτο μὲν εἰδώς, οὐδ' ἔτι μᾶλλον ὑπεσχόμην χρήματα]: knowing this, I by no means (or not at all more) promised money.

units.la: Resolutio negationis.
units.tr: Resolution of the negation.

units.la: Cōposita ex negatione & nomine numerali, nonnunquā soluuntur, & quandoque per Tmesim, ἁδ' εἰς, pro ἁδ' εἰς. ἁδ' οἱ, pro ἁδ' ἐν. ἁδ' αὖ εἰς, pro ἁδὲ εἰς αὖ. μηδ' αὖ εἰς pro μηδὲ εἷς αὖ. μηδ' αὖ μία, pro μηδεμία αὖ.
units.tr: Compounds made of the negation and a numeral are sometimes resolved, and sometimes by tmesis: [οὐδ' εἰς] for [οὐδὲ εἷς]; [οὐδ' οἱ] for [οὐδ' ἐν]; [οὐδ' αὖ εἰς] for [οὐδὲ εἷς αὖ]; [μηδ' αὖ εἰς] for [μηδὲ εἷς αὖ]; [μηδ' αὖ μία] for [μηδεμία αὖ].

units.la: Οὐ uaria significatio & constructio.
units.tr: The various meanings and constructions of [οὐ].

units.la: Οὐ τίν' ἕν, nullum penitus. ἀλλ' ὅπ οὐ̓, nihil quicquam, ἀχ ὅσον, ἀχ οἷον, nedum. Οὐκ ἐδ' ὅπως, nullo pacto, ut ἀκ ἐδ' ὅπως ἀκ εἴ, Fieri non potest, quin fis. Οὐκ ἐδ' ὅτι, nihil. ἀκ ἔσιν ἐφ' ὅτω, in nullo. ἀκ ἔσιν οἱ τινες, nulli.
units.tr: [οὐ τίν' ἕν]: not any one at all. [ἀλλ' ὅπ οὐ]: nothing whatever. [οὐχ ὅσον], [οὐχ οἷον]: not to say, far less. [οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως]: by no means; as in [οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐ γίγνῃ], it is impossible but that you should become (it). [οὐκ ἔστιν ὅτι]: nothing. [οὐκ ἔστιν ἐφ' ᾧ]: in nothing. [οὐκ ἔστιν οἵτινες]: none.

units.la: Οὐ ῥ, nónne, an nō. ἡ ῥ ἀ̓ή, ualet absfit. Pro quo etiam capitur ἀκ ἀγαθὲ, absfit. ἡ ῥ ἀλ̓, alioqui non. οὐ ῥ ἀλ̓ τοῦ & οὐ μὴν ἀλ̓, nequaquam, minime uero, οὐ ῥ ἀλλὰ, enimuero, uerum enimuero. Ponitur enim abundante negatione pro ἡ ῥ, ut μὴ σπαῖτε, οὐ ῥ ἀλλ' ἔχω κακῶς. Ne cauillare, etenim male habeo. οὐ ῥ ὅπως, non enim hoc modo, neque enim tantummodo.
units.tr: [οὐ ῥα] means "is it not?" or simply "not". [ἦ ῥα μή] means "may it not be": far from it. The same is rendered by [οὐκ ἀγαθέ], far from it. [ἦ ῥα ἀλλ' οὔ]: otherwise not. [οὐ ῥα ἀλλὰ τοῦ] and [οὐ μὴν ἀλλά]: by no means, certainly not. [οὐ γὰρ ἀλλά]: indeed, but truly. For it is put, with the negation redundant, for [ἦ ῥα], as in [μὴ σκῶπτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀλλ' ἔχω κακῶς]: do not scoff, for I am unwell. [οὐ γὰρ ὅπως]: for not in this way, nor only in this way.

units.la: Οὐχ ὅπως, non solum, non solum non, significat etiam non ut. Et pro eo οὐχ ὡς sæpe dicitur.
units.tr: [οὐχ ὅπως] means not only, not only not; it also means not that. And [οὐχ ὡς] is often said in its place.

units.la: Μὴ ὅτι, non solum, non solum non. Idem significat οὐχ ὅτι, quod etiam capitur pro, non quod, & tū solum construitur Indicatiuo.
units.tr: [μὴ ὅτι] means not only, not only not. [οὐχ ὅτι] has the same meaning; it is also used for not that, and it is construed only with the indicative.

units.la: Οὐχ ὅτι μὴ, non quin. οὐχ ὅτι μὴ κα̈λὸν ῾Ω οἶμαι, nō quín honestū esse censeam.
units.tr: [οὐχ ὅτι μή]: not but that. [οὐχ ὅτι μὴ καλὸν εἶναι οἶμαι]: I do not think it is not honourable.

units.la: Οὔτοι, nequaquam. ἦν, id est, ἀbundat enim ν, sicut in φαίνῃ. ἦν ᾧ, an forte, num forte.
units.tr: [οὔτοι]: by no means. [ἦν] (the ν being added superfluously, as in [φαίνῃ]). [ἦ ᾧ]: perhaps, or possibly.

units.la: ἁ μὲν ἀλλὰ, uel ἁ μὲν ἀλλά γε, enimuero, at uero, quín etiam, sed tamen. ἁ μὲν ἀλλ᾽ ἔγω, uerum esto, sed sit sane, quod concedentis est.
units.tr: [οὐ μὲν ἀλλά] or [οὐ μὲν ἀλλά γε]: indeed, but truly; nay even; but yet. [οὐ μέν, ἀλλ' ἔστω]: granted, but let it be so; this is the language of one conceding.

units.la: Interdum per Tmesim profertur, οὐ ᾗ μὲν αὐτὸς γε, ἀλλά, pro ἁ μὴν ἀλλὰ αὐτὸς sε.
units.tr: Sometimes it is pronounced with tmesis: [οὐ μὲν αὐτός γε, ἀλλά], for [οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ αὐτὸς γε].

units.la: Quod si ex ἁ μὴν ἀλλά, tollatur ἀλλά, iam erit negatio, ἁ μὲν, nec uero.
units.tr: If [ἀλλά] is removed from [οὐ μὴν ἀλλά], there will then be the negation [οὐ μήν]: nor indeed.

units.la: Quandoque dicunt, ἁ μὲν τοι ἀλλά, & ἁ μὲν τοι ἀλλά γε, pro ueruntamen.
units.tr: Sometimes they say [οὐ μέντοι ἀλλά] and [οὐ μέντοι ἀλλά γε] for nevertheless.

units.la: Οὐ μέντοι γε, non quidem, ἁ μέντοι certe non, ueruntamen non.
units.tr: [οὐ μέντοι γε]: not indeed. [οὐ μέντοι]: certainly not; nevertheless not.

units.la: Οὔτ᾽ μὴν, ἀλλ᾽ ἐ μὲν, nec uero, nec tamē. ἁ μὲν πω, haud dum tamen, ἁ μὴν ἀλλ᾽ ἐ, οὐ μὲν ἔτι, non tamen, ueruntamen non.
units.tr: [οὔτε μήν, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ μέν]: nor indeed, nor yet. [οὐ μέν πω]: not yet, however. [οὐ μὴν ἀλλ' οὔ] and [οὐ μὲν ἔτι]: not however; nevertheless not.

units.la: Duæ negationes affirmant.
units.tr: Two negations affirm.

units.la: Quandoque fit apud Græcos, ut duę negationes affirment, sicut Latinis, οὐκ ἐὰν ὅπως ἂν ἔχητε μὴ τὰ χρήματα, certe uos habetis pecuniam meam, Aristophan. ἂν ἐὰν ὅπως ἂν ἐξελῶ σ᾽ τ̂ οἰκίας. Nullo modo non eíciam domo, hoc eft, omnino eíciam & abdicabo.
units.tr: Sometimes among the Greeks two negations affirm, as they do among the Latins: [οὐκ ἐᾷ ὅπως ἂν ἔχητε μὴ τὰ χρήματα], certainly you have my money (Aristophanes). [οὐκ ἐάσω ὅπως ἂν ἐξελῶ σε τῆς οἰκίας]: I will in no way not drive you out of the house; that is, I will altogether drive you out and disown you.

units.la: Vel uehementius negant.
units.tr: They negate more vehemently.

units.la: Verum ut plurímum duæ negationes uehementius negãt, uel altera abun-dat, οὐ μὴ ποιήσω, Nequaquam faciam. Sic Ioan.15. χωρὶς ἐμοῦ ἀδυνατεῖτε ποιεῖν οὐ-δέν, Sine me non poteftis facere quic-quam. Homerus, ἐ μὴ ϑῦ ἀπόλλωνα, negationis habet repetitionem.
units.tr: But for the most part two negations negate more emphatically, or one of them is redundant: [οὐ μὴ ποιήσω], I will by no means do it. So John 15: [χωρὶς ἐμοῦ ἀδυνατεῖτε ποιεῖν οὐδέν]: without me you can do nothing. Homer, [ἐ μὴ θῦ Ἀπόλλωνα], contains a repetition of the negation.

units.la: De μὴ negatione.
units.tr: On the negation [μή].

units.la: Nec eft fímilis loquendi ratio, in ναὶ, μὴ, nam μὴ per fe negat, ut μὴ δία, non per Iouẽ: ναὶ μὴ uero affirmat, ναὶ μὴ τόδε σὺν πλεῖν, pro νὴ τόδε σὺν πλεῖν, per hoc fce-ptrum: quo in loco μὴ abundat.
units.tr: The manner of speaking is not similar with [ναὶ μή]. For [μή] by itself negates, as in [μὴ Δία], not by Zeus; but [ναὶ μή] affirms, as in [ναὶ μὴ τόδε σκῆπτρον] for [νὴ τόδε σκῆπτρον], by this sceptre; where [μή] is redundant.

units.la: Οὐδαμῆ ἀδαμῶς, nullo prorsus pacto. Hic etiam negatio altera uidetur ex su-perfluo addita, & eft folum ἀργνπτικόν. Verum μηδαμῆ μηδαμῶς idē significat.
units.tr: [οὐδαμῆ], [οὐδαμῶς]: in no way at all. Here too a second negation seems to be added superfluously, and it is only negative (ἀρνητικόν). But [μηδαμῆ], [μηδαμῶς] mean the same.

units.la: Sed ἀπαγορευτικὸν etiã effe poteft. His opponitur πάντη πάντως, ufquequaque.
units.tr: But it can also be prohibitive (ἀπαγορευτικόν). Opposed to these is [πάντη πάντως], in every way.

units.la: Οὐ abundat quandoq.
units.tr: [οὐ] is sometimes redundant.

units.la: Et οὐ ϑὲ ἀλλὰ, ex abundantia negatio-nis capitur quandoque pro ναὶ ϑὲ. Ari-stophaftophanes in Ranis. μὴ σκῶπτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀλλ' ἔχω κακῶς, Ne cauillare, etenim male ha beo.
units.tr: And [οὐ δὲ ἀλλά], from the redundancy of the negation, is sometimes taken for [ναὶ δέ]. Aristophanes in the Frogs: [μὴ σκῶπτε, οὐ γὰρ ἀλλ' ἔχω κακῶς]: do not jest, for I am unwell.

units.la: Similiter in hoc, οὐδ' ἐς πολλῷ δεῖ, nequa quam multum abest, uirtute geminatur negatio, ut patet cum dicitur, ταῦτα μή- πω γέγονεν, οὐδ' ἐς πολλῷ δεῖ, Haec nondum facta sunt, nec multum abest ut fiant. Nā nihil refert si negationem auferas, & dicas, ταῦτα μήπω γέγονεν, καὶ πολλῷ δεῖ, & multum abest ut fiant.
units.tr: Similarly in [οὐδ' ἐς πολλῷ δεῖ], by no means is it far off, the negation is doubled in force; this is clear when one says [ταῦτα μήπω γέγονεν, οὐδ' ἐς πολλῷ δεῖ]: these things have not yet happened, nor is it far off that they should. For it makes no difference if you remove the negation and say [ταῦτα μήπω γέγονεν, καὶ πολλῷ δεῖ]: and it is far off that they should.

units.la: Quín & contraria dictione idem significatur, οὐδ' ὀλίγου δεῖ, neque parum abest, id est, multum abest. Quia hic negatio uim suam seruat, quae in illo, οὐδὲ πολλοῦ δεῖ, ornatus causa, & Attice ponitur.
units.tr: Indeed, the same is signified by the contrary expression [οὐδ' ὀλίγου δεῖ]: it is not a little off, that is, it is far off. For here the negation keeps the force it has, whereas in the other, [οὐδὲ πολλοῦ δεῖ], it is used for ornament, in the Attic manner.

units.la: Negatio uerbis negatiuis additur per πλεονασμόν.
units.tr: A negation is added to negative verbs by pleonasm [πλεονασμόν].

units.la: Fit etiam ex abundantia negationis quod Attici addant negationes uerbis, quae per se sunt negatiua, qualia sunt ἀπαγορεύω, κωλύω, ἀρνοῦμαι, ἐπέχω, &c. ξαρνός εἰμι μὴ ποιῆσαι, Nego me fecisse, κωλύσαι μὴ ἐξάγειν, Vetare quo minus. exportent. ὑκ ἀξαρνῆμαι, μὴ γεγονέναι ἐγὼ πκὸς, Non eo infícias, me in amore fuisse procliuem.
units.tr: It also happens, from the redundancy of negation, that the Attic writers add negations to verbs which are negative in themselves, such as [ἀπαγορεύω], [κωλύω], [ἀρνοῦμαι], [ἐπέχω], etc. [ἀρνητής εἰμι μὴ ποιῆσαι]: I deny that I did it. [κωλύσαι μὴ ἐξάγειν]: to prevent them from exporting. [οὐκ ἀρνοῦμαι μὴ γεγονέναι ἐγὼ φιλικός]: I do not deny that I was inclined to love.

units.la: Duae negationes cum Infinitiuo.
units.tr: Two negatives with the Infinitive.

units.la: In locutionibus quoque, quae per Infinitiuo finitiuū efferuntur, geminatur quando que negatio per μὴ ὲ uel μὴ οὐχὶ, ut οὐκ ἀν ἐξαρνῶ φνοιο, μὴ οὐκ ἐμὸς ὑὸς εἶ), Non potes negare, quod fis filius meus. οὐ θέμις, μὴ οὐχὶ προσθυμῶ εἶ) τοῖς φίλοις, Ne fas est quod nō fis paratus amicis. Quae duplicatio negationum quandoque seruata eadem constructione, significat nisi. μὴ ἐλπίζε τὸν θεὸν ἱλάσκεσθαι, μὴ οὐκ ἀπὸ χεῖρας καλίας, hoc est, ἵω μὴ ἀπέχης. In qua locutione ἐφ' ὧ uel ὅτι τῷ subaudiri uidetur, quasi dicatur, ἐφ' ᾧ μὴ οὐκ ἀπὸ χεῖρας.
units.tr: In expressions that are rendered by the infinitive in place of the finite verb, the negation is sometimes doubled by μὴ with οὐ or μὴ with οὐχί, as in οὐκ ἂν ἐξαρνῷο φύνοιο [οὐκ ἂν ἐξαρνῷο φύνοιο] (μὴ οὐκ ἐμὸς υἱὸς εἶ): "You cannot deny that you are my son." οὐ θέμις, μὴ οὐχὶ προθυμῶ εἶ τοῖς φίλοις: "It is not right that you should not be willing toward your friends." When this doubled negation keeps the same construction, it means "unless": μὴ ἐλπίζε τὸν θεὸν ἱλάσκεσθαι, μὴ οὐκ ἀπὸ χείρας καλίας, that is, "unless you cease" (ἵνα μὴ ἀπέχῃς). In this expression ἐφ' ᾧ or ὅτι τῷ seems to be understood, as if one said ἐφ' ᾧ μὴ οὐκ ἀπὸ χείρας.

units.la: Significat etiam seruata eadem constructione, quin, quo minus. τὸν γὰρ ἕτερον ἐν ὀφθαλμὸν, οὐδὲ ἑμία μηχανὴ μὴ οὐκ ἀμβλύτερον ἀλεξήρεω, Nullo pacto fieri potest, quín alter oculus obtusius uiderit.
units.tr: With the same construction it also means "but that" or "so as not to." τὸν γὰρ ἕτερον ἐν ὀφθαλμὸν, οὐδὲ ἑμία μηχανὴ μὴ οὐκ ἀμβλύτερον ἀλεξήσειν [ἀμβλύτερον ἀλεξήσειν]: "By no means can it be that the other eye does not see more dimly," that is, "it cannot be that one eye does not see more dimly than the other."

units.la: Mὴ
units.tr: μὴ

units.la: Μὴ ἐ cum Participio.
units.tr: Μὴ οὐ with the participle.

units.la: Construitur etiam μὴ οὐ, uel μὴ οὐχὶ, quando significat quin, uel nisi, cū participio, οὐκ ἂν ἀξιόπιστ᾽ ὢν εἶλω λέγων, μὴ ἐχὶ πιστεύειν ἀληθεύσαμεν, Non esset credendum, quod dico, nisi prius uera dixissem. ἐ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνα ἀναξαπτεῖν, μὴ ἐχὶ τῶν ἀναπεσόντων, Ruere illa nō possūt, quin & hæc concidant.
units.tr: μὴ οὐ or μὴ οὐχί is also construed with the participle when it means "but that" or "unless": οὐκ ἂν ἀξιόπιστος ὢν εἶλον λέγων, μὴ οὐχὶ πιστεύειν ἀληθεύσαμεν [οὐκ ἂν ἀξιόπιστος ὢν…]: "What I say would not be credible, unless I had first spoken the truth." ἐ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνα ἀναξαπτεῖν, μὴ οὐχὶ τῶν ἀναπεσόντων: "Those things cannot fall, but these things too will collapse."

units.la: Μὴ ἐχὶ cum Infinitiuo.
units.tr: Μὴ οὐχί with the infinitive.

units.la: Item ponitur pro, non etiam, quando construitur cum Infinitiuo, addita ἢ coniunctione, τόλε οὐδαμῶς ῥᾳδίον πολλὰ κακὰ δρῶντα τὰς ἄλλους, μὴ οὐ ἢ πάσχειν αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἕτερα, Illud nequaquam fa-cile fit, ut qui in alios multa mala commit-tit, non etiam patiatur & ipse multa alia. Quod etiam per alteram tantum negationem dici potest, μὴ καὶ πάσχειν αὐτὸν, uel οὐ καὶ πάσχειν αὐτὸν, Non patiatur & ipse.
units.tr: It is also used for "not even" when it is construed with the infinitive, with the particle ἢ added: τόδε οὐδαμῶς ῥᾴδιον, πολλὰ κακὰ δρῶντα τοὺς ἄλλους, μὴ οὐ ἢ πάσχειν αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἕτερα: "It is by no means easy that one who does many evil things to others should not also suffer many other things himself." This can also be said with only one negation, μὴ καὶ πάσχειν αὐτὸν, or οὐ καὶ πάσχειν αὐτὸν: "let him not suffer himself as well."

units.la: Μὴ ἐχὴ cum Indicatiuo.
units.tr: Μὴ οὐχί with the indicative.

units.la: Inuenitur etiam μὴ οὐ, uel μὴ οὐχὶ con-strui Indicatiuis, pro nequaquam.
units.tr: μὴ οὐ or μὴ οὐχί is also found construed with indicatives, meaning "by no means."

units.la: Arist. 2. Politicon, μὴ γὰρ οὐ μᾶτλω τλω πρὸς ἑαυτὸν αὐτὸς ἔχει φιλίαν, Nequaquam temerarium est, quod sibi sit unusquisque amicus.
units.tr: Aristotle, Politics book 2: μὴ γὰρ οὐ μᾶλλον πρὸς ἑαυτὸν αὐτὸς ἔχει φιλίαν [μὴ γὰρ οὐ μᾶλλον πρὸς ἑαυτὸν αὐτὸς ἔχει φιλίαν]: "It is by no means rash that each man should be a friend to himself."

units.la: Οὐ μὴ Subiunctiuo, Indicatiuo & Optatiuo gaudet.
units.tr: Οὐ μὴ takes the subjunctive, indicative and optative.

units.la: Quod si has particulas inuertas, ut sit οὐ μὴ, subiunctiuum fere poscunt, raro etiam Indicatiuum, aut optatiuum, eodē significato, hoc est, pro nequaquam. Lucianus, Θαρρεῖ, οὐδὲν οὐ μὴ ψύντα ἀ-ξίνον, διηγοσωνῆς τοῦτης παρέσης, Cōfide, haudquaquam enim iniustum fieri potest, cum iustitia adsit.
units.tr: If these particles are inverted, so that it is οὐ μή, they usually take the subjunctive, and rarely the indicative or optative, with the same meaning, that is, "by no means." Lucian: Θάρρει, οὐδὲν οὐ μὴ ψεῦδος ἀξιόπιστον, δια­γιγνώσκει τούτης παρούσης [Θάρρει, οὐδὲν οὐ μὴ ψεῦδος…]: "Take heart, for by no means can an injustice happen while justice is present."

units.la: Cum Indicatiuo, τὰς μὲν γὰρ πονηρὰς μὴ ποτε βελτίους ποιήσετε, Prauos nequaquam reddetis meliores.
units.tr: With the indicative: τὰς μὲν γὰρ πονηρὰς μὴ ποτε βελτίους ποιήσετε [τὰς μὲν γὰρ πονηρὰς μὴ ποτε βελτίους ποιήσετε]: "You will by no means make the wicked better."

units.la: Cum Optatiuo, ἐὰν μή ποτε καταχύσῃ τῷ περιχότῳ, Nequaquam praevalere posset aduersus ea quae accidunt.
units.tr: With the optative: ἐὰν μή ποτε καταχύσῃ τῶν περιόντων [ἐὰν μή ποτε καταχύσῃ τῷ περιόντι]: "He could by no means prevail against the things that happen."

units.la: Attica Eclipsis negationis.
units.tr: The Attic ellipsis of the negation.

units.la: Sicut Atticis quandoque abundat negatio, ita etiā eisdem saepe deest & subauditur. Sic Demost. οὐδὲ ἀπαρ. ἀπὸ ὅπως ἂν τῶν ἀπολογήσηται, dixit, pro ἀλλὰ ἀλλ' ὅπως ἀπολογήσεται.
units.tr: Just as the Attic writers sometimes have an excess of negation, so too they often leave it out and have it understood. Thus Demosthenes wrote: οὐδὲ ἀπαρ. ἀπὸ ὅπως ἂν τῶν ἀπολογήσηται [οὐδὲ ἀπαρ…], for ἀλλὰ ἀλλ' ὅπως ἀπολογήσεται: "but rather, but he shall defend himself as he may."

units.la: Mὴ praeterito & praesenti Indicatiui iungitur.
units.tr: μὴ is joined with the perfect and present indicative.

units.la: Mὴ negatiuum, iungitur indicatiuo in praeteritis, & in praesenti. δέδοικα μὴ λελήθαμεν, Vereor ne nō intelligamus. δέδοικα μὴ τῇ νῇ σέ τι τῶν ἐπιέχει ξεν, Vereor ne te quippiā horum conturbarit.
units.tr: Μὴ, the negative, is joined to the indicative in past and present tenses: δέδοικα μὴ λελήθαμεν [δέδοικα μὴ λελήθαμεν], "I fear we may not understand"; δέδοικα μὴ τῇ νῇ σέ τι τῶν ἐπιέχει ξεν [δέδοικα μὴ τῇ νῇ σέ τι τῶν ἐπιέχει ξεν], "I fear that something of these things has troubled you."

units.la: In praesenti, φοβεῖδε μὴ δυσκολωτέρᾳν τι νῦν δήκεμαι.
units.tr: In the present: φοβοῦμαι μὴ δυσκολώτερόν τι νῦν δήκεμαι [φοβεῖδε μὴ δυσκολωτέρᾳν τι νῦν δήκεμαι], "I am afraid that I now feel something rather troublesome."

units.la: Idem Optatiuo gaudet.
units.tr: The same particle takes the optative as well.

units.la: Iūgitur etiam μὴ, similiter ὅπως μὴ, & ὡς μὴ, optatiuis: ἐγὼ σε κήδομαι, μὴ, uel ὅ-πως μὴ, uel ὡς μὴ ἀδικοίης. Ego gero curā tui, ne quis afficiat te iniuria.
units.tr: μὴ is also joined with optatives, and similarly ὅπως μὴ and ὡς μὴ: ἐγώ σε κήδομαι, μὴ, or ὅπως μὴ, or ὡς μὴ ἀδικοίης: "I take care of you, lest anyone wrong you." Ego gero curam tui, ne quis afficiat te iniuria.

units.la: Idem Coniunctiuo ἐλλειπτικῶς.
units.tr: The same with the subjunctive, by ellipsis.

units.la: Similiter coniunctiuis ἐλλειπτικῶς, de ficiēte scilicet σκότει, uel ὄρα, aut alio simi li uerbo, ἀλλὰ μὴ λάθωμεν ἑαυτὲς: uel sic, ἀλλ' ὅπως μὴ λάθωμεν ἑαυτὲς, sed uidendū nobis ne per imprudentiam erremus.
units.tr: Similarly with subjunctives by ellipsis, the verb σκόπει, or ὅρα, or some other like verb being understood: ἀλλὰ μὴ λάθωμεν ἑαυτούς, or thus, ἀλλ' ὅπως μὴ λάθωμεν ἑαυτούς: "but we must take care lest we go astray through carelessness."

units.la: Mὴ ἀπαγορευτικόν.
units.tr: μὴ as a prohibition.

units.la: Et accipitur saepe μὴ pro ὰ, sed nun- quam οὐ pro μή. Mὴ ἀπαγορευτικῶς constr-uitur omnib. modis, dempto Indicatiuo, μὴ λέγε, Ne dic, μὴ γνῶς, ne nosca s, μὴ γνώῃς, ne noueris, μὴ γνῶναι, ne noueris.
units.tr: μὴ is often taken for ἁ, but οὐ is never used for μή. μὴ with the prohibitive sense is construed in all moods except the indicative: μὴ λέγε, "Do not say"; μὴ γνῷς, "do not know"; μὴ γνῷς, "may you not know"; μὴ γνῶναι, "not to know."

units.la: Mǹ quæsitiuum.
units.tr: μὴ as an interrogative.

units.la: Dum est interrogatiuum iungitur Indicatiuo, Μὴ Θέλεις φαγεῖν; An non uis comedere?
units.tr: When it is interrogative it is joined with the indicative: Μὴ θέλεις φαγεῖν; "Do you not wish to eat?"

units.la: De compositis cum μὴ & ǜ.
units.tr: On compounds of μὴ and οὐ.

units.la: Vt μὴ construitur ἀπαγορευτικῶς & ǜ ἀρνητικῶς. Sic etiam eorum composita, uidelicet μήποι, μήποιγε, μήποτε, & similia, ἀπαγορευτικῶς. Et ἤτοι, ἤποτε, οὐδὲ ἢτα, & alia huiusmodi, ἀρνητικῶς, atque apagoreutica, pro arneticis accipiuntur, non contra, arnetica pro apagoreuticis.
units.tr: μὴ is construed prohibitively, and οὐ negatively. Their compounds are likewise so construed: μήποι, μήποιγε, μήποτε and similar forms are prohibitive. ἤτοι, ἤποτε, οὐδὲ ἤτα and other such words are negative, and the prohibitive and the negative forms are taken for the negative, not the reverse, the negative for the prohibitive.

units.la: Coniungitur μὴ cæteris orationis partibus in hunc fere modum, μήπ μὴ, nónne, μήτις, nunquis, μήπ, nūquid, uel nequid.
units.tr: μὴ is joined with the other parts of speech more or less in this way: μήπ μή, "surely not"; μήτις, "whether anyone"; μήπ, "whether anything," or "whether nothing."

units.la: De μήποτε significatione & constructione.
units.tr: On the meaning and construction of μήποτε.

units.la: Μήποτε, an, construitur non tam percunctanter, quàm dubitanter, ἀλλὰ μήποτε οὐ τοῦτο ἢ τὸ αἴτιον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ᾱ̈ρημένον; An potius non hæc causa est, sed supra dicta? μήποτε ἄγαν εὔνοιας ἢ, Haud scio an stultum sit.
units.tr: μήποτε, "perhaps," is construed not so much as a question but as an expression of doubt: ἀλλὰ μήποτε οὐ τοῦτο ἢ τὸ αἴτιον, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἰρημένον? "Is it not perhaps the case that this is not the cause, but the thing said above?" μήποτε ἄγαν εὔνοιας ἢ: "I hardly know whether it is foolish."

units.la: Construitur Coniunctiuis & Indicatiuis, unde licet dicere, Μήποτε λέγε- ταὶ. tau, uel μήποτε λέγηται.
units.tr: It is construed with subjunctives and indicatives, whence one may say μήποτε λέγεται or μήποτε λέγηται: "perhaps it is said."

units.la: Est etiā quandoque negatiuum uel optatiuum, μήποτε τοσοῦτον ἀμελήσωμεν τῆς ἀρετῆς. Abfit, ut tantum negligamus uirtutem.
units.tr: It is sometimes also negative or optative: μήποτε τοσοῦτον ἀμελήσωμεν τῆς ἀρετῆς: "Far be it that we should neglect virtue so much."

units.la: Capitur etiam pro ἀδήποτε, nūquam. μήποτοιγε, nequaquam, saltem, certe, ὅτι μὴ, nisi μήν, μήν δὴ, μήν γε, μήν γέ δὴ, μήτε δὴ γε, μήτοι γε, μὴ ὅτι γε, μὴ ὅτι, ualet nedū.
units.tr: It is also taken for ἀδήποτε, "never." μήποτοιγε, "by no means, at least, certainly"; ὅτι μή, "except"; μήν, μήν δή, μήν γε, μήν γέ δή, μήτε δή γε, μήτοι γε, μὴ ὅτι γε, μὴ ὅτι: "not to mention," is equivalent to nedum ("much less").

units.la: Et huic postremo respondet in constructione ἀλλά, ut μὴ ὅτι καλὸν, ἀλλὰ καλλίσον, nō solū honestū, sed honestissimū.
units.tr: And to this last the apodosis in construction answers with ἀλλά, as μὴ ὅτι καλόν, ἀλλὰ καλλίστον: "not only honourable, but most honourable."

units.la: Μὴ δὲ ὅτι, non solum enim. μὴ δὴ ἵνα, abfit. ut μὴ δὴ ἵνα φίλε, hoc est, abfit ut hoc facias amice.
units.tr: μὴ δὲ ὅτι: "not only, for." μὴ δὴ ἵνα: "far be it." As in μὴ δὴ ἵνα φίλε, that is, "far be it that you should do this, friend."

units.la: Ponitur etiam, pro Diȷ auertant, diȷ meliora.
units.tr: It is also used for "God forbid," "may the gods avert it."

units.la: Pro hoc etiā ponitur μὴ γὰρ δή, uel μὴ δὲ γε, ut μὴ δὲ δὴ γνώμης ἡμῶν κατίχειν τὴν τύχην. Abfit enim ut praeualeat proposito noftro fortuna ὅπως μὴ, pro μὴ ponitur.
units.tr: For this also μὴ γὰρ δή or μὴ δὲ γε is used, as μὴ δὲ δὴ γνώμης ἡμῶν κατισχεῖν τὴν τύχην: "For far be it that fortune should prevail over our purpose." ὅπως μὴ is used for μή.

units.la: Lucian. in Iudicio dearum. ὅπως μὴ χαλεπὴ τὴν δίκην, ne molesti sitis iudici.
units.tr: Lucian, in the Judgement of the Goddesses: ὅπως μὴ χαλεπὴ τὴν δίκην, "take care that you are not harsh to the judge."

units.la: Coniectandi.
units.tr: Of conjecturing.

units.la: Aduerbia coniectandi iunguntur Indicatiuis, ἴσως ἐρῶ, fortassis dicam.
units.tr: Adverbs of conjecture are joined to the indicative: ἴσως ἐρῶ, "perhaps I shall say."

units.la: Quod si optatiuo iungantur aut Con-iunctiuo, non fiat sine coniunctione ἄν, expressa, uel saltem subaudita. ἴσως φαίη ἄν, forsan dixerit, ἴσως ἂν ἔλθω, forsitā ue-nero: quod commune est omnibus ad-uerbijs cum uerbo constructis.
units.tr: If they are joined to the optative or the subjunctive, this is not done without the particle ἄν, either expressed or at least understood: ἴσως φαίη ἄν, "perhaps he would say"; ἴσως ἂν ἔλθω, "perhaps I may come." This is common to all adverbs construed with a verb.

units.la: Εὖ ἂν ἔχοι, bene habeat. τάχα ἂν εἴη, procul absit. νὴ Δί᾽ εἴποιμ᾽ ἄν, per Iouem di-xerim: & ita in aliis.
units.tr: Εὖ ἂν ἔχοι, "it would be well"; τάχα ἂν εἴη, "far be it"; νὴ Δί᾽ εἴποιμ᾽ ἄν, "I would say, by Jove." So also in other cases.

units.la: Imperatiuis uero non construuntur aduerbia coniectandi: nō enim dicitur, τάχα γράφε, τυχὸν λέγε.
units.tr: Adverbs of conjecture are not construed with imperatives: one does not say τάχα γράφε or τυχὸν λέγε.

units.la: Interrogandi.
units.tr: Of asking.

units.la: Interrogandi aduerbia pręponuntur uerbis, πόθεν, πορρῶ, πότε ἦλθες;
units.tr: Interrogative adverbs are placed before the verb: πόθεν, πορρῶ, πότε ἦλθες; "Whence, from afar, when did you come?"

units.la: Anastrophe aduerb.
units.tr: Anastrophe of adverbs.

units.la: Quod si quando postponātur, id fiet per figuram Anastrophen, ἔρχῃ πότε; ὑ-πάγεις πόθεν;
units.tr: But when they are placed after the verb, this happens by the figure anastrophe: ἔρχῃ πότε; "When are you coming?" ὑπάγεις πόθεν; "Whence are you going?"

units.la: Quæ figura frequentius fit in aduer-bio, πῶς, ut ἔσῃ δ᾽ ἐκ τῶν πῶς; At hoc quo-nam pacto fieri poterit; γένοιτ᾽ δ᾽ ἐκ πῶς; At id quonam modo euenturum est?
units.tr: This figure occurs more often with the adverb πῶς, as in ἔσῃ δ᾽ ἐκ τῶν πῶς; "But how will it be possible in this way?" and γένοιτ᾽ δ᾽ ἐκ πῶς; "But how on earth would that come about?"

units.la: Πῶς Emphaticum.
units.tr: Emphatic πῶς.

units.la: Ponitur etiam πῶς interdum non in-terrogatiue, sed emphaseos gratia, significans plurimum, & quasi admirabunde profertur, ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐ τούτου τῆ τεσπου πῶς εἰμὶ ἀεὶ, At ego mire hoc ingenio prædi-tus sum.
units.tr: πῶς is also sometimes used not interrogatively but for emphasis, signifying a great deal, and is spoken as if in wonder: ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἐ τούτου τῆ τεσπου πῶς εἰμὶ ἀεὶ, "But I am wondrously endowed with this talent."

units.la: Πῶς ἃ, assentientis est.
units.tr: Πῶς ἂ, expressing assent.

units.la: Πῶς ἃ, in responsionibus assentionem significat, ϖῶς οὐ; Quid ni? ϖῶς οὐχ ἀδικεῖς; Nónne tu improbus es? πῶς ἂν αἰσχρὸν; Nónne turpe est?
units.tr: Πῶς ἂ, in replies, signifies assent: πῶς οὐ; "Why not?" πῶς οὐχ ἀδικεῖς; "Do you not do wrong?" πῶς ἂν αἰσχρόν; "Is it not shameful?"

units.la: De aduerbio ϖῆ.
units.tr: On the adverb πῇ.

units.la: Πῇ; Quomodo? qua ratione? Huic respondet ῇ, ut dictum est.
units.tr: πῇ; "How? In what way?" To this corresponds ῇ [ῇ], as was said.

units.la: Πῇ cum μὲν & δὲ.
units.tr: Πῇ with μὲν and δὲ.

units.la: Cum autē apponitur μὲν & δὲ, significat partim, τῇ μὲν διαφέρει, τῇ δὲ ὁμοίως ἔχει, partim differt, partim similiter se habet, quod etiam significat, τῇ μὲν, τῇ δὲ, ut dictum est superius.
units.tr: When μὲν and δὲ are added, it signifies "partly": τῇ μὲν διαφέρει, τῇ δὲ ὁμοίως ἔχει, "in one respect it differs, in another it is similarly disposed." That is, it differs partly and is partly alike. This also signifies τῇ μὲν, τῇ δὲ, as said above.

units.la: De accentu interrogatiuorum.
units.tr: On the accent of interrogatives.

units.la: Πῶς & ϖῆ dum accipiuntur interro-gatiue, circūflectuntur; alia uero acuun-tur in penultima; dum uero capiuntur indefinite loci, aut figurae, aut modi significatiua, inclinantur, nisi fuerint trisyllaba: nihil enim inclinatur, quod sit plus quàm disfyllabum, πόθεν ἐρχῃ; Unde uenis? ἐρχόμενος & ληπόθεν, alicūde uenien s. πῶς ἔχει, Quo modo habet. οὕτω πῶς ἔχει, Sic habet. πότ' ἦλθες; Quando uenefti? ἦλθον ληπότε, Veni aliquando.
units.tr: Πῶς and πῇ, when taken interrogatively, have a circumflex; the others are accented on the penultima. When they are taken as indefinite words of place, manner or mode, they are enclitic, unless they are trisyllabic, for nothing that has more than two syllables is enclitic: πόθεν ἐρχῃ; "Whence do you come?" ἐρχόμενος ἀλ' ληπόθεν, "coming from somewhere else." πῶς ἔχει, "How is he?" οὕτω πῶς ἔχει, "He is somehow so." πότ' ἦλθες; "When did you come?" ἦλθον ληπότε, "I came at some time."

units.la: Ποτε mediante ἡ crebro postponitur infinitis dictionibus.
units.tr: ποτε, with ἡ between, is often placed after indefinite words.

units.la: Et hoc pacto frequenter postponi-tur ποτε, dictionibus infinitis, mediante coniunctione ἡ, ὁπόσον ἡ ποτε, quantu-cunque. ὁπόσον ἡ ποτε, quotuslibet. ὁπότε ἐάν ἡ ποτε, uterlibet. ὁπότε ποτε, ὅπου ἡ ποτε, ubicunque. ὁπῶς ποτε, ὅπως ἡ ποτε, ὅπως ἡ ποτ' ἄν, ὅπῃ ἡ ποτε, quouis modo, quo-modocunque, utcunque. ὃ ἡ ποτε, ἃ ἡ ποτε, ὅτι ἡ ποτε, quoduis. ποῖ & ἡ ποτε; interrogatiue, qualis tandem?
units.tr: In this way ποτε is frequently placed after indefinite words, with the conjunction ἡ intervening: ὁπόσον ἡ ποτε, "however much"; ὁπόσον ἡ ποτε, "however many"; ὁπότε ἐάν ἡ ποτε, "whichever"; ὁπότε ποτε; ὅπου ἡ ποτε, "wherever"; ὁπῶς ποτε, ὅπως ἡ ποτε, ὅπως ἡ ποτ' ἄν, ὅπῃ ἡ ποτε, "in whatever way, however, howsoever"; ὃ ἡ ποτε, ἃ ἡ ποτε, ὅτι ἡ ποτε, "whatever"; ποῖ & ἡ ποτε, interrogatively, "of what sort then?"

units.la: Optandi.
units.tr: Of wishing.

units.la: Εἴθε & αἴθε aduerbia optandi costruuntur uerbis Optatiui modi, εἴθε γράψει ἂν, Vtinam scriberet. αἴθε γράφοιμι, Vtinam scriberem.
units.tr: The optative adverbs εἴθε and αἴθε are construed with verbs of the optative mood: εἴθε γράψει ἂν, "Would that he might write"; αἴθε γράφοιμι, "Would that I might write."

units.la: Cum autem adduntur Indicatiuis, faciunt ut optatiuam recipiant constru-ctionem, εἴθε ἔγραψεν, utinam scripsisset. εἴθε ἦν ποιεῖν, Vtinam licuisset facere, αἴθ' ὄφελες, habet quidem significationē optationis, uerum hoc differt ab aliis optandi aduerbijs, quòd semper construatur in secunda persona ἱλιάδ. α. αἴθ' ὄφελες πα-ρὰ νηυσὶν ἀλάλκυρτος [?], ἠδ' ἀπήμων ἤδαν, uti-nam sederes.
units.tr: When they are added to indicatives, they take an optative construction: εἴθε ἔγραψεν, "Would that he had written"; εἴθε ἦν ποιεῖν, "Would that it had been possible to do"; αἴθ' ὄφελες, "Would that you had." This has the sense of a wish, but it differs from the other optative adverbs in that it is always construed in the second person: Iliad 1, αἴθ' ὄφελες παρὰ νηυσὶν ἀλάλκυρτος [?], ἠδ' ἀπήμων ἤδαν, "Would that you had sat beside the ships..."

units.la: Dicitur etiam ὡς ὄφελες, interdū enim ὡς additur, interdum non additur.
units.tr: ὡς ὄφελες is also said, for sometimes ὡς is added and sometimes it is not.

units.la: Dicunt praeterea, εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον, pro ὤφε-λον.
units.tr: They also say εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον, for ὤφελον.

units.la: Praeterea plura Graecae linguae fche-mata apud probatos authores obseruare licebit studioso, ut συλλαβῇς ὅσον δύναμις, comprehendito totis uiribus, ὅσον ὀλίγον ἀπέχει, aliquantulum distat. Defecti-uas orationes, οὗ ξόπον, pro καθ' οὗ ξόπον. τὸ δή. δὶ ὃ δή, διότερ, ὅμων διόμων, &c.
units.tr: Besides, the student will be able to observe more constructions of the Greek language in approved authors, such as συλλαβῇς ὅσον δύναμις, "seize as much as your strength allows"; ὅσον ὀλίγον ἀπέχει, "it is a little way off." Defective expressions: οὗ ξόπον for καθ' οὗ ξόπον; τὸ δή; δὶ ὃ δή; διότερ; ὅμων διόμων; etc.

units.la: CONSTRUCTIO PRAEPOSITIONVM. EN.
units.tr: THE CONSTRUCTION OF PREPOSITIONS. EN.

units.la: DATIVO ἐν construitur, ἐν οἴκῳ.sed ἐν Διδασκάλῳ, defecti uum Atticum est, pro ἐν οἴκῳ τῷ διδασκάλῳ, ἐν αὐθεντῇ, ἐν ἀκμῇ, In ipso ætatis flore, in robore ætatis. ἐν καλῷ, commodum, honestum. ἐν καλλίστῳ, commodíssimum. ἐν παιδὶ, in pueritia. ἐν ὀργῇ ἔχειν, offendísse. ἐν χαρᾷ ἔχειν, Poeti ce ἐν uel ἐνί, ἐνί uero, pro ἐνεστί, sí nō pasfum fuerit ἀναςροφῶ, ut ὧ ἐνί.
units.tr: ἐν is construed with the dative: ἐν οἴκῳ [en oikō], in the house. But ἐν διδασκάλῳ [en didaskalō] is an Attic defective construction for ἐν οἴκῳ τῷ διδασκάλῳ, in the teacher's house. ἐν αὐθεντῇ [en authenti], in the prime of life, in the bloom of age. ἐν καλῷ [en kalō], conveniently, honourably. ἐν καλλίστῳ [en kallistō], most conveniently. ἐν παιδὶ [en paidi], in boyhood. ἐν ὀργῇ ἔχειν [en orgē echein], to have given offence. ἐν χαρᾷ ἔχειν [en charǣ echein], to hold in joy. In poetry, ἐν or ἐνί is used, and ἐνί stands for ἐνεστί [enesti], when it is not permitted to change the word, as in ὧ ἐνί [ō eni].

units.la: Quadoque etiam capitur una cum fuo casu, aduerbij loco, ἐν οἷς, quamobrem. ἐν μέρει, uiciffim, figillatim. ἐν ὁσίῳ, opportune. ἐν βραχεῖ, paucis, in summa. ἐν ὀλίγῳ, summatim. ἐν χρῷ, ad cutem, ad uiuum prope. ἐν ᾧ, quando.
units.tr: Sometimes it is also taken together with its case as an adverb: ἐν οἷς [en hois], for which reason. ἐν μέρει [en merei], in turn, one by one. ἐν ὁσίῳ [en hosiō], opportunely. ἐν βραχεῖ [en brachei], briefly, in short. ἐν ὀλίγῳ [en oligō], in summary. ἐν χρῷ [en chrō], close to the skin, almost to the quick. ἐν ᾧ [en hō], when.

units.la: EIΣ.
units.tr: EIΣ.

units.la: Eis uel εἰς, Accusatiuo, ποιεῖσθαι εἰς ἑαυτὸν, Periculum fuí facere. εἰς τὸ ἔσχατον, Ad summum discrimen. εἰς τετάρτῳ, die quarto, εἰς τὸ ὕμπαλιν, in contrarium. εἰς πόλιν. At εἰς διδασκάλς, εἰς ἄλλου, defe ctiuum est.
units.tr: εἰς or εἰς (eis), with the accusative: ποιεῖσθαι εἰς ἑαυτὸν [poieisthai eis heauton], to make trial of oneself. εἰς τὸ ἔσχατον [eis to eschaton], to the utmost danger. εἰς τετάρτῳ [eis tetartō], on the fourth day. εἰς τὸ ὕμπαλιν [eis to ympalin], to the contrary. εἰς πόλιν [eis polin], into the city. But εἰς διδασκάλς and εἰς ἄλλου are defective constructions.

units.la: Ad inanimata sæpius refertur εἰς, ut εἰς ἀγρὸν πορεύομαι, Eo in forum. ᾱεὸς ad animata, ᾱεὸς διηγεσὶς πέμπω χρυσίον, ᾱεὸς σέ.
units.tr: εἰς is more often used of inanimate things, as εἰς ἀγρὸν πορεύομαι [eis agron poreuomai], I go into the field, I go to the market. For persons, πρὸς is used, as πρὸς διηγεσὶς πέμπω χρυσίον [pros ... pempō chrysion], I send gold, and πρὸς σέ [pros se], to you.

units.la: Etiam εἰς magis ad laudē, ᾱεὸς in ma lum fumitur. ὑμνῶ εἰς Ἀπόλλωνα, Hymnus in laudem Apollonis. Et ad relatio nem ἀναφέρειν εἰς ἀρχοντα, Retulit ad prę torem. πολεμεῖ ᾱεὸς παῖδα. ᾱεὸς ὁμόρους, aduersus finitimos.
units.tr: εἰς is also used more of praise, while πρὸς is used for blame. ὑμνῶ εἰς Ἀπόλλωνα [hymnō eis Apollōna], a hymn in praise of Apollo. It is also used of reference: ἀναφέρειν εἰς ἀρχοντα [anapherein eis archonta], he referred it to the praetor. πολεμεῖ πρὸς παῖδα [polemei pros paida], he makes war on the boy. πρὸς ὁμόρους [pros homorous], against neighbours.

units.la: Et est quando εἰς capitur in malum. ἠγνωμόνησαν εἰς ἡμᾶς, Ingrati fuerunt in nos. Quandoque significat usq; εἰς ἐμέ, usque ad ætatem meam. Quandoque apud εἰς Μακεδόνας, apud Macedones. Quandoq; circiter, εἰς ἄνδρας δισχιλίους, circiter ducentos uiros. Quādoque ob, εἰς δυσγνώμην λοιδορεῖν, Ob ignobilitatem conuitiari.
units.tr: εἰς is sometimes taken in a bad sense: ἠγνωμόνησαν εἰς ἡμᾶς [ēgnōmonēsan eis hēmas], they were ungrateful to us. Sometimes it means as far as, up to my time, εἰς ἐμέ [eis eme]. Sometimes it means among, as εἰς Μακεδόνας [eis Makedonas], among the Macedonians. Sometimes it means about, as εἰς ἄνδρας δισχιλίους [eis andras dischilious], about two hundred men. Sometimes it means on account of, as εἰς δυσγνώμην λοιδορεῖν [eis dysgnōmēn loidorein], to revile on account of ignobility.

units.la: Capitur etiā unà cū suo casu quando que aduerbialiter, εἰς τὰ μάλιςα, εἰς τὸ πρῶτα, εἰς τὸ ἔσχατα, εἰς τὸ ἀνεἰβέςατον, εἰς ἐμβολὴν, ἐν τοῖς μάλιςα, summe, maximε. εἰς Λέον, opportune. εἰς Λυσάμυν, quàm potuit maxime. εἰς καλὸν, commode. εἰς σὺν, simul. Etiam σὺν accusatiuo constructum pro εἰς ponitur apud Pindarum. σὺν νόμῳ.
units.tr: It is also taken with its case adverbially at times: εἰς τὰ μάλιςα [eis ta malista], especially, most of all. εἰς τὸ πρῶτα [eis to prōta], at first. εἰς τὸ ἔσχατα [eis to eschata], at last. εἰς τὸ ἀνεἰβέςατον [eis to aneiploiseraton], most unfortunately. εἰς ἐμβολὴν [eis embolēn], in the nick of time. ἐν τοῖς μάλιςα [en tois malista], above all, very much. εἰς Λέον [eis Leon], opportunely. εἰς Λυσάμυν [eis Lysamyn], as much as possible. εἰς καλὸν [eis kalon], conveniently. εἰς σὺν [eis syn], together. σὺν with the accusative, used in place of εἰς, is also found in Pindar: σὺν νόμῳ [syn nomō], according to custom.

units.la: EK EΞ.
units.tr: EK EΞ.

units.la: Εξ, uocali, uel σὺν consonante sequẽte, iungitur genitiuo, ἐξ ἀργυρᾶ, ἐξ ἀμάξης λαλεῖν, ἐ plaustro loqui. ἐξ ἀφεαξίας θεά-γματα, ex otio negotiũ. σὺν νεότητος, σὺν λύ-κης σόματος, ex ore lupi, σὺν ἀδαλόγος, ex insperato. σὺν ἀδαλλήλας, per alternitatẽ, uel ex geminatione. σὺν θεωπῆς ὁρᾶν, ob liquis oculis uidere. σὺν παντὸς, subaudi-tur ξόπτος, omni pacto.
units.tr: ἐξ, before a vowel, or σὺν before a following consonant, takes the genitive: ἐξ ἀργυρᾶ [ex argyra], of silver. ἐξ ἀμάξης λαλεῖν [ex amaxēs lalein], to speak from a cart, that is, to speak plainly. ἐξ ἀφεαξίας θεά-γματα [ex apheaxias theamata], business from leisure. σὺν νεότητος [syn neotētos], from youth. σὺν λύκης σόματος [syn lykēs stomatos], from the mouth of a wolf. σὺν ἀδαλόγος [syn adalogos], unexpectedly. σὺν ἀδαλλήλας [syn adallēlas], by turns, or by repetition. σὺν θεωπῆς ὁρᾶν [syn theōpēs horan], to see with clear eyes. σὺν παντὸς, where ξόπτος [tropos] is understood, in every way.

units.la: Capitur etiam hæc præpositio unà cum suo casu aduerbij loco, σὺν θεοῖς, σὺν θεαυρέσεως, cõsulto. σὺν παλαιῶς, olim. σὺν πολλᾶ ἤδη, iam pridẽ, σὺν τῷ, propterea quod, ἐξ ὧν, propterea quod, eò quod. Quod soluitur quandoq; per Tmesim, σὺν μὴ ὧν, pro ἐξ ὧν μὴ.
units.tr: This preposition is also taken with its case as an adverb: σὺν θεοῖς [syn theois], by the gods' help, σὺν θεαυρέσεως, deliberately. σὺν παλαιῶς [syn palaiōs], long ago. σὺν πολλᾶ ἤδη [syn pollǣ ēdē], already long since. σὺν τῷ [syn tō], for this reason, because. ἐξ ὧν [ex hōn], for this reason, because. This is sometimes split by tmesis: σὺν μὴ ὧν [syn mē hōn], for ἐξ ὧν μὴ [ex hōn mē].

units.la: ΣΥΝ.
units.tr: ΣΥΝ.

units.la: Συν semper cum datiuo, συν λόγῳ, cũ ratione, συν Θεᾷ, cũ deo. συν Θεῷ εἰρηνάθαι, didictū esse deo fauente. οὐ Θεοῖς, deorum pace, diis exoratis. Attice ξεὺ, ἱλιάδος υ. καὶ ἦλθεν ἀργυρότοξ᾽ ἀρτέμιδι ξεύ, Et venit Apollo cū Diana, ξεῶοικ, pro σύνοικ, cohabitator.
units.tr: συν always takes the dative: συν λόγῳ [syn logō], with reason. συν Θεᾷ [syn theǣ], with God. συν Θεῷ εἰρηνάθαι [syn theō eirēnasthai], to have been taught with God's favour. οὐ Θεοῖς [ou theois], by the peace of the gods, with the gods appeased. Attic ξεὺ, in the Iliad, υ. καὶ ἦλθεν ἀργυρότοξ᾽ ἀρτέμιδι ξεύ, And Apollo of the silver bow came with Artemis. ξεῶοικ, for σύνοικ [synoik], a co-inhabitant.

units.la: ΠΡΟΣ.
units.tr: ΠΡΟΣ.

units.la: Πεὸς Attice ὡς, Ionice ποτὶ, uel ποτί. ὀδὸς. Ꞓ. Dorice ποδ᾽ὶ, cum genitiuo significat motū à persona, πεὸς Θεῦ τὰ ἀγαθὰ, à deo bona.
units.tr: Πεὸς, in Attic ὡς, in Ionic ποτὶ, or ποτί [poti]. ὀδὸς. Dorically ποδ᾽ὶ [pod'i]. With the genitive it denotes motion from a person: πεὸς Θεῦ τὰ ἀγαθὰ [pros theou ta agatha], good things from God.

units.la: Vel nota est: iurādi, ἦνε πεὸς θεῦ. πεὸς ἡελίοιο κελεύθου. uel contra, corámue denotat, πεὸς θεῶν μακάρων, coram diis beatis. Aut officium, πεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστιν, officii no stri est. οὐ πεὸς ἰατρου τῶτο ποιεῖν, Non est medici hoc agere. Aut originem, πεὸς μητρὸς γένου, à matre genus. Aut quantum pertinet, πεὸς τὴν θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων, quantum pertinet ad deos, aut ad homines.
units.tr: It also marks an oath: ἦνε πεὸς θεῦ [ēne pros theou], by God. πεὸς ἡελίοιο κελεύθου [pros hēelioio keleuthou], along the sun's path. Or the reverse, it denotes in the presence of: πεὸς θεῶν μακάρων [pros theōn makarōn], in the presence of the blessed gods. Or duty: πεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστιν [pros hēmōn estin], it is our duty. οὐ πεὸς ἰατρου τῶτο ποιεῖν [ou pros iatrou touto poiein], it is not the physician's business to do this. Or origin: πεὸς μητρὸς γένου [pros mētros genou], of a mother's kin. Or as far as concerns: πεὸς τὴν θεῶν καὶ ἀνθρώπων [pros tēn theōn kai anthrōpōn], as far as concerns gods or men.

units.la: Habet etiam cū genitiuo peculiares quasdā constructiones, quales sunt hæ, πεὸς ξόπε θέλι μοι, Est mihi conueniens, est mihi consentaneum. πεὸς τινὸς ἔῃ, alicui studere, fauere, & eum tueri. Sicut apud Ciceronē, à reo dicere, à cau sa bonorum stare, ⲁ̀ⲡⲟ κακοῦ ὄν, incommodum.
units.tr: It also has peculiar constructions with the genitive, such as πρὸς ἔοικέ μοι [πρὸς ἔοικέ μοι], "it is fitting for me, it is agreeable to me"; πρὸς τινὸς εἶναι [πρὸς τινὸς εἶναι], "to side with someone, to favour him and defend him." So also in Cicero: "to speak on behalf of the defendant" (à reo dicere), "to stand on the side of the good cause" (à causa bonorum stare), and "ἀπὸ κακοῦ ὄν" [ἀπὸ κακοῦ ὄν], "to be to someone's disadvantage."

units.la: Cum datiuo significat prope, iuxta, πρὸς τοῖς πόσιν, prope pedes. Aut præte rea, πρὸς τούτοις, ad hæc, præterea. Aut apud, πρὸς τῆς Δεσμοθέτας, apud iudices Autassiduitatem, πρὸς τοῦτο εἰμί, sum de ditus, siue occupatus in ea re: πρὸς λόγῳ ἔχειν, meditatur, & occupatur in oratio- ne. πρὸς αὐτὸν ἑαυτόν, secum meditari.
units.tr: With the dative it means near, beside: πρὸς τοῖς πόσιν [pros tois posin], near the feet. Or besides: πρὸς τούτοις [pros toutois], in addition to these, moreover. Or before: πρὸς τῆς Δεσμοθέτας [pros tēs desmothetas], before the judges. Or by way of constant application: πρὸς τοῦτο εἰμί [pros touto eimi], I am devoted to, or occupied with, that matter; πρὸς λόγῳ ἔχειν [pros logō echein], to be engaged in and occupied with speech. πρὸς αὐτὸν ἑαυτόν [pros auton heauton], to meditate with oneself.

units.la: Cum accusatiuo motū ad personam, habitum uel imitatione, πρὸς σε ἐρχομαι. ὡς τὰ δύο πρὸς τέσσαρα, ὅτι ἡ τὰ τέσσαρα πρὸς ὀκτώ, ἀδ' εἰ πρὸς ἀυλόν. Aut contra, μὴ πρὸς λέοντα δόρκας, Ne caprea contrà leonem. Aut inter, πρὸς ἡμᾶς φιλίᾳ, amicitia, quæ inter nos est.
units.tr: With the accusative it denotes motion towards a person, a condition or an imitation: πρὸς σε ἐρχομαι [pros se erchomai], I come to you. As two is to four, as four is to eight [ὡς τὰ δύο πρὸς τέσσαρα, ὅτι ἡ τὰ τέσσαρα πρὸς ὀκτώ]; ἀδ' εἰ πρὸς ἀυλόν [ad' ei pros aulon]. Or the reverse: μὴ πρὸς λέοντα δόρκας [mē pros leonta dorkas], a roe-deer not against a lion. Or between: πρὸς ἡμᾶς φιλίᾳ [pros hēmas philia], the friendship which is between us.

units.la: Aut sconuenit permutationibus, aut compensationibus, πρὸς ἀργύριον πολλῆ ἀγῆ, Vendi pecunia. βίον πρὸς κέρδη καταλλάττεσθαι, Vitam uēdere lucris. Aut propter, πρὸς ὃν λέγω. Aut seruit compa ratioNi, πρὸς ῥόδα ἀνεμώνη.
units.tr: It is also used of exchanges or equivalents: πρὸς ἀργύριον πολλῆ ἀγῆ [pros argyrion polle agē], to sell for money, at a great price. βίον πρὸς κέρδη καταλλάττεσθαι [bion pros kerdē katallattesthai], to sell one's life for gains. Or on account of: πρὸς ὃν λέγω [pros hon legō], on account of which I speak. It also serves for comparison: πρὸς ῥόδα ἀνεμώνη [pros rhoda anemōnē], the anemone in comparison with the rose.

units.la: Singularia funt illa, πρὸς αὐτὸν αὐτὸς, sibi conuenienter. πρὸς ἐχθρὸν inimico animo. πρὸς, πρὸς δ᾽ἐ, πρὸς ἐπὶ capiuntur loco aduerbiorum, praeterea, amplius, εἴκοσι ἢ πρὸς uiginti & amplius.
units.tr: These are special uses: πρὸς αὐτὸν αὐτὸς [pros auton autos], himself, suitably to himself. πρὸς ἐχθρὸν [pros echthron], with hostile intent. πρὸς, πρὸς δ᾽ἐ, πρὸς ἐπὶ [pros, pros d'e, pros epi] are used in place of adverbs: moreover, further, εἴκοσι ἢ πρὸς [eikosi ē pros], twenty and more.

units.la: ΠΡΟ.
units.tr: PRO.

units.la: Περὶ cum genitiuo, ante, siue pro significat enim locum & tempus, περὶ τῆς πόλεως λαῶν. περὶ Συρῶν, pro foribus. πρὸ ἔργου θρασύς, ante negotium audax. πρὸ Δούλου δεσπότης, Dominus praestat seruo. πρὸ ἔργου, siue πρὸ ἔργας, quod operaepretium est, praeuertendumque, & coducibile: pro quo etiam capitur, πρὸ ὀδῷ, quod significat etiam promptum & obuium. πρὸ ὀλίγου, paulo ante.
units.tr: Peri with the genitive means "about" or "for," and it signifies place and time: peri tēs poleōs [περὶ τῆς πόλεως], "about the city" of the people; peri Syrōn [περὶ Συρῶν], "in front of the doors." Pro ergou thrasys [πρὸ ἔργου θρασύς], "bold before the task." Pro doulou despotēs [πρὸ δούλου δεσπότης], "the master is superior to the slave." Pro ergou, or pro ergas, means "worth the effort," that which is to be preferred and is profitable. It is also used in pro hodou [πρὸ ὁδοῦ], which means "ready" and "at hand." Pro oligou [πρὸ ὀλίγου] means "a little while ago."

units.la: ΑΝΑ.
units.tr: ANA.

units.la: Ἀνὰ, accusatiuo, ἀνὰ σεάτον, ἀνὰ μέλαν αἷμα, per atrum sanguinem.
units.tr: Ana with the accusative: ana sesaton [ἀνὰ σέατον], ana melan haima [ἀνὰ μέλαν αἷμα], "through the black blood."

units.la: Significat etiam distributionem, ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔτος, quotannis. ἀνὰ μέρος, partim. Lucae 9. ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας, Singuli duas tunicas.
units.tr: It also signifies distribution: ana pan etos [ἀνὰ πᾶν ἔτος], "every year"; ana meros [ἀνὰ μέρος], "in part." Luke 9: ana dyo chitōnas [ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας], "each to have two tunics."

units.la: Composita denotat sursum uel re, ἀνὰ βαίνω, ἀναζεύγω. Homerus χευσέω, ἀνὰ συνπρὸ, pro σὺν cecinit.
units.tr: In compounds it denotes upward motion or going back: anabainō [ἀνὰ βαίνω], anazeugnymi [ἀναζεύγνυμι]. Homer used ana for syn [σύν] in a compound form.

units.la: Κατὰ uel κατὰι, cum genitiuo notat contra, κατ' αἰχίνα ὀλόγῳ. μὴ κ᾽ βοὸς ἑὺ-χου, Ne contra bouem opta. Aut super, κατὰ πέξῶν ἀπείρεις, Super saxa feminas, εὐδὲι κατὰ γῆς. Aut de, κατ' ἀνθρώπου λέ-γεται τὸ ζῷον, de homine dicitur, animal. κ᾽ νώτῳ, à tergo. Poeta κατ' ἀλύμπιοιο κα-ρῶν, dixit pro ὄπισθ.
units.tr: Kata, or kat' [κατὰ], with the genitive means "against": kat' aichmēs; mē kat' boos eukou [μὴ κ᾽ βοὸς εὔχου], "do not pray against the ox." Or "upon": kata petrōn [κατὰ πέτρων], "upon the rocks," super saxa, "women over the rocks." Or "concerning": kat' anthrōpou legetai to zōion [κατ᾽ ἀνθρώπου λέγεται τὸ ζῷον], "the animal is said of man." Kata nōtō [κ᾽ νώτῳ], "from behind." The poet kat' Olympiou karēna [κατ᾽ Ὀλυμπίοιο κάρηνα] used it for "behind" (opisthen [ὄπισθ]).

units.la: Cum accusatiuo secundum, κ᾽ μοίεαν, secundum fatum, hoc ἔστι rite, ut decuit. κατὰ τὸν ὁμηγον. κ᾽ λόγον, id est, probabi-liter. Aut per, κατὰ νῆας ἀχαιῶν, per naues Græcorum. Vel in, κατὰ χώεαν, in regione.
units.tr: With the accusative, it means "according to": kata moiran [κ᾽ μοίραν], "according to fate," that is, "rightly, as was fitting"; kata ton homoion [κατὰ τὸν ὁμοῖον], "according to the like"; kata logon [κ᾽ λόγον], that is, "probably." Or "through": kata nēas Achaiōn [κατὰ νῆας ἀχαιῶν], "through the ships of the Greeks." Or "in": kata chōran [κατὰ χώραν], "in the region."

units.la: Secundum hanc significationem dicitur breuitatis causa, κατὰ τλὼ ἐμῶ, pro mea quidem sententia. Aut significat circa, aut in aliquo, οὐδὲ κα᾽ θ᾽ εν, in nullo. κα᾽ θ᾽ εν, in uno. κατὰ ναῦ, circa nauem. κατ' αὐτὸ, eodem tempore. Inde & κα᾽ ἑαυτὸν dicitur, Secum ipse solus, κατὰ ἑ-μὲ, &c.
units.tr: In this sense, for the sake of brevity, one says kata to emon [κατὰ τὸ ἐμόν], "for my part," that is, "in my own opinion." Or it means "concerning" or "in something": oude kat' hen [οὐδὲ κατ᾽ ἕν], "in nothing"; kath' hen [κα᾽ θ᾽ ἕν], "in one"; kata naun [κατὰ ναῦν], "concerning the ship"; kat' auto [κατ᾽ αὐτὸ], "at the same time." Hence also kath' heauton [κα᾽ ἑαυτὸν], "by himself alone," kata eme [κατ᾽ ἐμέ], and so on.

units.la: Aut significat tempus, κα᾽ ἡμᾶς γέ-γονεν, Nostris temporibus factum est. Aut quod Latinis significant aduerbia in im, κατ᾽ἔτος, annuatim, siue quotannis, κατ᾽ἀμφω, utrinque. κατ᾽ἀνδρα, uiritim. Sic Luc. 8. κατ᾽ πόλιν ἡ κώμην, oppidatim, castellatim, id est, per singulas ciuitates & castella.
units.tr: Or it signifies time: kath' hēmas egeneto [κα᾽ ἡμᾶς γέγονεν], "it happened in our times." Or what the Latins express by adverbs in -im: kat' etos [κατ᾽ ἔτος], "yearly, or every year"; kat' amphō [κατ᾽ ἀμφω], "on both sides"; kat' andra [κατ᾽ ἄνδρα], "man by man." So Luke 8: kata polin ē kōmēn [κατ᾽ πόλιν ἡ κώμην], "town by town, village by village," that is, through each single city and village.

units.la: ΔΙΑ.
units.tr: DIA.

units.la: Διὰ cum genitiuo, per, διὰ πυρὸς και ξιφῶν, Per ignem & enses. ὑς διὰ πόλεως, Sus per rosas. διὰ σῦ. διὰ τ᾽ ἀγρέας. διὰ τοίχου λαλεῖν, Per parietem loqui.
units.tr: Dia with the genitive means "through": dia pyros kai xiphōn [διὰ πυρὸς καὶ ξιφῶν], "through fire and swords"; hōs dia poleōs, "as through the city"; dia sou [διὰ σοῦ], "through you"; dia tēs agreas [διὰ τῆς ἀγρέας], "through the country"; dia toichou lalein [διὰ τοίχου λαλεῖν], "to speak through a wall."

units.la: Dicunt etiam λέγειν διὰ πλειόνων, καὶ βραχύτερον, διὰ βραχέων, pro multis et paucis dicere. Et διὰ μακρῆς, διὰ πολλῆς, διὰ χρόνου, pro longo interuallo, diu, multo post.
units.tr: They also say legein dia pleionōn [λέγειν διὰ πλειόνων] and brachyteron, dia brachéōn [διὰ βραχέων], "to speak in many words" and "in few," that is, to say much or little. And dia makras [διὰ μακρᾶς], dia pollēs [διὰ πολλῆς], dia chronou [διὰ χρόνου], mean "after a long interval," "for a long time," "long afterwards."

units.la: Et διὰ τιμῆς ἄγειν, in honore habere. διὰ αἰδοῦς ἄγειν, uenerari, ueneratione dignari. Et διὰ τρίτης, tertio die. διὰ βίου, Per totam uitam. διὰ τέλους, continue, assidue. διὰ μιᾶς γνώμης ὁρμῶμενοι, Vno animo consentientes. διὰ δορατῶν μάχεσθαι, Eminus pugnare.
units.tr: Also dia timēs agein [διὰ τιμῆς ἄγειν], "to hold in honour"; dia aidous agein [διὰ αἰδοῦς ἄγειν], "to revere, to deem worthy of reverence." And dia tritēs [διὰ τρίτης], "on the third day"; dia biou [διὰ βίου], "throughout the whole life"; dia telous [διὰ τέλους], "continually, constantly"; dia mias gnōmēs hormōmenoi [διὰ μιᾶς γνώμης ὁρμῶμενοι], "agreeing with one mind"; dia doratōn machesthai [διὰ δορατῶν μάχεσθαι], "to fight at a distance with spears."

units.la: Cum accusatiuo, propter, διὰ τὲ ταῦτα ποιῶ. Dicunt etiam διὰ ἐμέ γε, Quantum in me est. Etiam per apud Homeras rum δ᾽ ἀτεα, ἡ̓ μέλαν αἷμα, Per arma, & atrum sanguinem.
units.tr: With the accusative it means "on account of": dia te tauta poiō [διὰ τὲ ταῦτα ποιῶ], "I do this on account of these things." They also say dia eme ge [διὰ ἐμέ γε], "as far as I am concerned." Homer also has "through" in dia t' area, ē melan haima [διὰ τ᾽ ἄρεα, ἡ μέλαν αἷμα], "through arms and black blood."

units.la: META.
units.tr: META.

units.la: Μετὰ cum genitiuo significat cum, ὐ- δὴς μετὰ φίλων ὁ βίος, Suauis cum amicis uita. At μετὰ τεσσάρτοισι ἀναστὰς Home ricum est. μετ᾽ ἀνδράσι, Cum tertijs impe rauit.
units.tr: Meta with the genitive means "with": hōdys meta philōn ho bios [ὡδὺς μετὰ φίλων ὁ βίος], "life is sweet with friends." But meta tessarakontoisi anastas [μετὰ τεσσαράκοντα ἀναστὰς] is Homeric. Met' andrasi [μετ᾽ ἀνδράσι] means "he gave orders with the third" (of the men).

units.la: Cum accusatiuo, post, μετὰ τὸν ἑορτήν. Vsurpatur etiam quandoque pro ἐν, uel δι᾽ ἀ, μὴ χεῖρας ἔχειν, In manibus habuit.
units.tr: With the accusative it means "after": meta tēn heortēn [μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν], "after the feast." It is also sometimes used for en [ἐν] or dia [διὰ]: mē cheiras echein [μὴ χεῖρας ἔχειν], "to have in the hands," that is, "he held in his hands."

units.la: ΠΑΡΑ.
units.tr: PARA.

units.la: Παρὰ, παρ, παραὶ, cum genitiuo, significat motum à persona, παρὰ Θεῦ τ᾽ ἀγαθά à deo bona. παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ δοῦναι, de meo, siue de mea pecunia dare.
units.tr: Para, par, parai [παρὰ, παρ, παραί], with the genitive, signifies motion from a person: para theou ta agatha [παρὰ Θεοῦ τ᾽ ἀγαθά], "good things from God"; par' emou dounai, "to give from what is mine," that is, from my own money.

units.la: Cū datiuo, apud, prope, παρ' ἐντέρῳ κύων, iuxta intestina canis. παρὰ σοί, In te est situm, penes te est. παρ᾽ ἐμοί.
units.tr: With the dative it means "at," "near": par' enterōi kyōn [παρ᾽ ἐντέρῳ κύων], "a dog beside the intestines"; para soi [παρὰ σοί], "it lies in you," "it is in your keeping"; par' emoi [παρ᾽ ἐμοί], "with me."

units.la: Accusatiuo, ad, παρὰ σὲ ἔρχομαι, Ad te uenio. Aut propter, παρὰ τί, propter quid, unde, quamobrem, παρὰ τὸ ἀδικεῖν ἢ τιμωρία, Propter iniuriam supplicium. Aut præter, παρὰ γνώμην συμβαίνει, Præter opinionem accidit. παρὰ τὸ μέλος.
units.tr: With the accusative it means "to": para se erchomai [παρὰ σὲ ἔρχομαι], "I come to you." Or "on account of": para ti, "on account of what, whence, why"; para to adikein ē timōria [παρὰ τὸ ἀδικεῖν ἢ τιμωρία], "punishment on account of injustice." Or "beyond" or "contrary to": para gnōmēn symbainei [παρὰ γνώμην συμβαίνει], "it happens beyond expectation"; para to melos [παρὰ τὸ μέλος], "out of tune," that is, "unfittingly."

units.la: μέλᾳ, id est, inepte. Aut relationem, τὴν πορφύραν παρὰ πορφύραν, Purpuram iuxta purpuram. Aut supra, sive ultra, ὠφελῶ παρὰ τὰς ὑὲς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, Specio sus supra filios hominum.
units.tr: Or it means relation: tēn porphyran para porphyran [τὴν πορφύραν παρὰ πορφύραν], "purple beside purple." Or "above" or "beyond": ōpheleō para tas hyeis tōn anthrōpōn, "I hold in higher regard than the sons of men."

units.la: Poteft etiam dici hoc modo, παρ' ἡμέραν, ἐαν, παρ' ἔτος, παρὰ μῆνα, Alternis dieb. alternis annis, alternis mensibus.
units.tr: It can also be used in this way: par' hēmeran [παρ᾽ ἡμέραν], par' etos [παρ᾽ ἔτος], para mēna [παρὰ μῆνα]: "on alternate days, in alternate years, in alternate months."

units.la: Quandoque importat tempus idem, παρὰ τὸ ἐλεῖπνον, tempore coenę. παρὰ τὸν ὁλον, inter nauigandum. παρὰ πάντα χρόνον, omni tempore. Hinc fit ἀπὸ αὐτῆς, ἡ ἀπὸ αὐτὰ, & ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, iam inde, ex illa hora.
units.tr: Sometimes it denotes the same time: para to deipnon [παρὰ τὸ δεῖπνον], "at the time of supper"; para ton holon [παρὰ τὸν ὅλον], "during the voyage"; para panta chronon [παρὰ πάντα χρόνον], "at all times." Hence come apo autēs [ἀπὸ αὐτῆς], apo autou [ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ], "from then on, from that hour."

units.la: Quandoque significat contra, οὐδὲν παρὰ signi παρὰ τὸ θεοῦ ὁ δίκαιος φεύγεται, Nihil ficat contra contra legem Dei agit iustus. Aut post, παρὰ τὰ δεινὰ φρονιμώτερον, Post mala prudentior.
units.tr: Sometimes it means "against": ouden para ton nomon tou theou [οὐδὲν παρὰ τὸν νόμον τοῦ θεοῦ], "the righteous man does nothing against the law of God." Or "after": para ta deina phronimōteros [παρὰ τὰ δεινὰ φρονιμώτερος], "wiser after misfortunes."

units.la: Dicitur etiam aduerbialiter, παρ' ἓν, ἀδαμικρὸν, fermè, pro nihilo. παρ' ὅσον, uel παρ' ὅσα, quatenus, quoniam.
units.tr: It is also used adverbially: par' hen [παρ᾽ ἕν], "almost," that is, "as good as nothing"; par' hoson [παρ᾽ ὅσον], or par' hosa [παρ᾽ ὅσα], "in so far as," "since."

units.la: Item παρὰ πολύ, quasi οὐκ ὡς πολλῷ, ut παρὰ πολὺ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἐποίησα, Minus quã spes erat feci. Sic παρὰ τοσοῦτον, modo capitur pro tantum,siue tam multum, mo do pro tantulum,siue tam parum.
units.tr: Likewise para polu [παρὰ πολύ], as if "not as much": as in para poly tēs elpidos epoiēsa, "I did less than hope had been." So para tosouton [παρὰ τοσοῦτον] is sometimes taken for "so much," or "so very much," and sometimes for "so little," or "so very little."

units.la: ANTI.
units.tr: ANTI.

units.la: Αντὶ semper construitur genitiuis, & significat pro, ἀντὶ πολλῶν χρημάτων. ἀντὶ τῆ σώματος σκιά, pro corpore umbra. ἀντὶ τῆς σῆς, cōtra, seu pro te. ἀντ' ἑρμίου, Hermionis uice, Dicunt etiam ἀντ' ἡμέρας, Per totam diem.
units.tr: Αντὶ [antí] is always construed with the genitive and means "for" or "instead of": ἀντὶ πολλῶν χρημάτων [antì pollῶn chrēmátōn], for much money; ἀντὶ τῆς σώματος σκιά [antì tês sṓmatos skiá], a shadow for the body, that is, a shadow instead of the body; ἀντὶ τῆς σῆς [antì tês sês], against you, or for you. They also say ἀντ' ἑρμίου [ant' hermíou], in place of Hermion, and ἀντ' ἡμέρας [ant' hēmérās], through the whole day.

units.la: Compofita par,uel cōtra denotat, ἀντιθέτω, πολύφημος, par uel cōtrarius deo, Polyphemus.
units.tr: In compounds it denotes "opposite" or "against": ἀντιθέτω [antithétō], placed opposite; πολύφημος [polýphēmos], Polyphemus, that is, one who is equal or opposed to a god.

units.la: Aduerbialiter etiam dicunt, ἀντ' ὧν, quamobrem,quare. Significat etiam eo quod,propterea quod. Lucian. ἀντ' ὧν σε διεπορθμεύσαμεν, Redde pro eo quod te transuexi, ἀντ' ὅτε, idem est, ἐκ οἶδ' ἀντ' ὅτε, Nescio quamobrem.
units.tr: As an adverb they also say ἀντ' ὧν [ant' hōn], wherefore, why. It also means "because" or "on the ground that." Lucian: ἀντ' ὧν σε διεπορθμεύσαμεν [ant' hōn se dieporthmeúsamen], repay me because we ferried you across. ἀντ' ὅτε [ant' hote] has the same sense: ἐκ οἶδ' ἀντ' ὅτε [ek oîd' ant' hote], I do not know why.

units.la: ΕΠΙ.
units.tr: ΕΠΙ.

units.la: Ἐπὶ cum genitiuo, in uel circa. βοὺς ἐπὶ γλωττης, Bos in lingua. ἐπὶ καλάμης ἀρότρω, In culmo arare. ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς, Secum ipse solus. ἐπὶ τῷ βασιλεῖ, circa Regem. Aut super, ἐπὶ γῆς, per terram. ἐπὶ καθέδρας Μωσέως, Super cathedram Mosfeos. ἐπὶ ὑπὲρ ἀκρῶν δακτύλων, Super summos pedum digitos. Aut sub, uel tempus, ἐπὶ ἀρχοντος ἀυγούστου, Sub principe Augusto. ἐφ' ἡμῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν παρῳχηκότων τῶν ἡμετέρων, Temporibus nostris, & temporibus maiorum nostrorum. ἐπὶ τῆς κρόνου, Temporibus Saturni. Capitur etiam aduerbialiter ἐπ' ἄλλων, alias.
units.tr: Ἐπὶ [epí] with the genitive means "in" or "about": βοὺς ἐπὶ γλωττης [boûs epì glṓttēs], an ox on the tongue; ἐπὶ καλάμης ἀρότρω [epì kalámēs arótrō], to plough on stubble. ἐφ' ἑαυτῆς [eph' heautês], by herself alone. ἐπὶ τῷ βασιλεῖ [epì tṓ basiléi], about the king. It can also mean "upon": ἐπὶ γῆς [epì gês], upon the earth; ἐπὶ καθέδρας Μωσέως [epì kathédras Mōyséōs], upon the seat of Moses; ἐπὶ ὑπὲρ ἀκρῶν δακτύλων [epì hyper akrōn daktýlōn], upon the tips of the toes. Or "under," or of time: ἐπὶ ἀρχοντος ἀυγούστου [epì archontos Augoústou], under the emperor Augustus; ἐφ' ἡμῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν παρῳχηκότων τῶν ἡμετέρων [eph' hēmōn, kaì epì tōn parōichēkótōn tōn hēmetérōn], in our times and in the times of our forefathers; ἐπὶ τῆς κρόνου [epì tês krónou], in the time of Saturn. It is also used adverbially: ἐπ' ἄλλων [ep' allōn], otherwise.

units.la: Cum genitiuo, etiam ad, contra, ἐφ' ἑλάδος ; ἐπὶ ἀρκτῴου βορέου ; ἐπὶ αἰτωλίας, Ad Orientem.
units.tr: With the genitive it can also mean "towards" or "against": ἐφ' ἑλάδος [eph' heládos], towards Greece; ἐπὶ ἀρκτῴου βορέου [epì arktṓou boréou], towards the north wind; ἐπὶ αἰτωλίας [epì aitōlías], towards Aetolia, that is, to the east.

units.la: Dum datiuo propter, ἐπὶ τούτοις, Ob hæc, uel inter hæc, ἐπὶ οὐδενί ; Propter nullum fructum. Aut post ; ἐπὶ τούτοις πολλὰ ἐτέρα διηγήσεται, Post hæc multa alia narrabat.
units.tr: With the dative: "propter" (on account of), ἐπὶ τούτοις, "ob haec" (for these things), or "inter haec" (in the meantime); ἐπὶ οὐδενί, "propter nullum fructum" (for no profit). Or "post" (after): ἐπὶ τούτοις πολλὰ ἑτέρα διηγήσεται, "post haec multa alia narrabat" (after these things he went on to narrate many other things).

units.la: Aut super, ἐποικοδομηθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ θεμελίῳ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, Aedificati super fundamentum apostolorum & prophetarum.
units.tr: Or "upon": ἐποικοδομηθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ θεμελίῳ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν [epoikodomēthéntes epì tṓ themelíōi tōn apostólōn kaì prophētṓn], built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets.

units.la: Aut in, ἐπὶ γνάθοις βοῶν φέρει, In faucibus bouem portat. ἕως ἐπὶ σωρῷ, Bos in aceruo. ἕως ἐπὶ φάτνῃ. ἐπ' ἡμέρᾳ, Intra unū diem, Aut modū, ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς, Certis conditionibus legibusq̄.
units.tr: Or "in": ἐπὶ γνάθοις βοῶν φέρει [epì gnáthois boṓn phérei], he carries in the jaws of an ox, that is, in the mouth of an ox; ἕως ἐπὶ σωρῷ [héōs epì sōrṓi], an ox in a heap; ἕως ἐπὶ φάτνῃ [héōs epì phátnēi], an ox in the manger. ἐπ' ἡμέρᾳ [ep' hēmérāi], within one day. Or of manner: ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς [epì rhētoîs], on certain conditions and laws.

units.la: y Dicitur etiam aduerbialiter, ἐπ' ἀεἰσι εφ', Sinistrorsum.
units.tr: It is also used adverbially: ἐπ' ἀεἰσι εφ' [ep' aeísi eph'], leftward.

units.la: Cum accusatiuo motum ad aliquid, ἐπὶ ξυνον. ἐπὶ ἴδιον ἀξίεσμα ὁ κύων, Canis ad propriū uomitū. ἐπὶ ὄνος, Ad asinos. ἐπὶ πῦρ ϑηλὸς, Ad ignem titio.
units.tr: With the accusative it denotes motion towards something: ἐπὶ ξυνον [epì xunon], towards the common place. ἐπὶ ἴδιον ἀξίεσμα ὁ κύων [epì ídion axíesma ho kýōn], the dog to its own vomit. ἐπὶ ὄνος [epì ónos], to the asses. ἐπὶ πῦρ ϑηλὸς [epì pŷr thēlós], the brand to the fire.

units.la: Secundum hanc formā dicitur etiam ἐπὶ ἀξίαν ποιεῖν, Ad dignitatem & authoritatem, & potentiam promouere.
units.tr: In this same construction one also says ἐπὶ ἀξίαν ποιεῖν [epì axían poiein], to promote someone to dignity, authority and power.

units.la: Dicitur etiam aduerbialiter cum suo casu, ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖσον, plerunque, pluri‑mum. ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ, Magna ex parte. ἐφ' ὅσον, pro quo Attice dicitur, ἐφ' ὅσα quatenus, in quantum. ἐφ' ὅ, secundum quod cuius causa, ob quod, ἐφ' ᾧ, quamobrem.
units.tr: It is also used adverbially with its case: ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖσον [epì tò pleîston], for the most part, mostly, chiefly; ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ [epì tò polý], for the greater part. ἐφ' ὅσον [eph' hóson], which in Attic is ἐφ' ὅσα [eph' hósa], as far as, in so far as. ἐφ' ὅ [eph' hó], according to which; of whose cause, on account of which; ἐφ' ᾧ [eph' hō], wherefore.

units.la: Eφ' ᾧ uariam sortitur constructionem.
units.tr: ἐφ' ᾧ [eph' hō] has a varied construction.

units.la: Construitur enim cum indicatiuo in praeterito, ἐφ' ᾧ ἐγραψεν, quare scripsit. In futuro, ἐφ' ᾧ τοὺς ἀνδρας κομιοῦται, Eo ut uiros accipiat. Et cum infinitiuo in praesenti & praeterito, ἐφ' ᾧ μεμνῆσθαι, pro ἐπὶ τὸ μεμνῆσθαι, uel ἕνεκα τοῦ μεμνῆσθαι, Et in futuro, ἐφ' ᾧ βοηθήσειν, Eò ut ferat auxilium. Iungitur etiam aduerbio. Actor. ἐγλύετο ἐπὶ ξὶς, Factum est tertio.
units.tr: It takes the indicative in the past tense: ἐφ' ᾧ ἐγραψεν [eph' hō egrapsen], wherefore he wrote. In the future: ἐφ' ᾧ τοὺς ἀνδρας κομιοῦται [eph' hō tous andras komioûtai], so that he may receive the men. And with the infinitive in the present and past: ἐφ' ᾧ μεμνῆσθαι [eph' hō memnēsthai], for ἐπὶ τὸ μεμνῆσθαι [epì tò memnēsthai] or ἕνεκα τοῦ μεμνῆσθαι [hénekha tou memnēsthai], to remember; and in the future: ἐφ' ᾧ βοηθήσειν [eph' hō boēthḗsein], so that he may bring help. It is also joined to an adverb. Acts: ἐγλύετο ἐπὶ ξὶς [eglýeto epì xis], it happened the third time.

units.la: ΠΕΡΙ.
units.tr: ΠΕΡΙ.

units.la: Πεϱὶ cum genitiuo significat de, uel pro, ϭεϱὶ τῆς ϰϱεῶν λαγῶς, De carnibus lepus. ϭεϱὶ πατϱὰς ἀμυνέσθαι, Pro patria pugnare.
units.tr: Περὶ [perí] with the genitive means "about" or "for": περὶ κρεῶν λαγώς [perì kreōn lagṓs], a hare concerning meat; περὶ πατρίδος ἀμύνεσθαι [perì patrídos amýnesthai], to fight for one's country.

units.la: Cum datiuo pro, Ἀέδοινα ϭεϱὶ ξανθῷ μίμελάῳ, Timui pro flauo Menelao.
units.tr: With the dative it means "for": Ἔδεισα περὶ ξανθῷ Μενελάῳ [Édeisa perì xanthṓi Menelāoi], I feared for fair Menelaus.

units.la: Construitur peculiariter cum genitiuo, unà cum hoc uerbo ποιῶ, ϭεϱὶ πλείονος σὲ ποιῶ ἐκείνω. Pluris te facio quam illum, ϭεϱὶ ὀλίγω ποιεῖσθαι, parui facere. ϭεϱὶ πλεῖ σ' ποιεῖσθαι ἁπάντων, Omnium maximi facere. ϭεϱὶ ἀδενὸς ποιεῖσθαι, nihili facere. Quod etiam fit cum uerbo substantiuo, ϭεϱὶ πολλῶν ἡμῖν τυγχάνει ὤν, magni fit apud nos.
units.tr: It has a special construction with the genitive together with the verb ποιῶ [poiṓ]: περὶ πλείονος σὲ ποιῶ ἐκείνου [perì pleíonos sè poiṓ ekeínou], I value you more than him; περὶ ὀλίγου ποιεῖσθαι [perì olígou poieîsthai], to make little of; περὶ πλείστου ποιεῖσθαι ἁπάντων [perì pleístou poieîsthai hapántōn], to value most highly of all; περὶ οὐδενὸς ποιεῖσθαι [perì oudenòs poieîsthai], to make nothing of. This also happens with the substantive verb: περὶ πολλοῦ ἡμῖν τυγχάνει ὤν [perì polloû hēmîn tynkhánei ṓn], he is held in high regard among us.

units.la: Cū accusatiuo significat circū, iuxta, ϭεϱὶ ἅλα, ηρὶ κύαμον, Circa salē & fabam, ϭεϱὶ Θύρας, circa fores. ϭεϱὶ ὃ, quocirca.
units.tr: With the accusative it means "around" or "near": περὶ ἅλα, περὶ κύαμον [perì hála, perì kýamon], around the salt and the bean; περὶ θύρας [perì thýras], around the doors. περὶ ὅ [perì hó], wherefore.

units.la: At ϭεϱὶ πύργῳ, ϭεϱὶ δὲ ἑλ, Homerica sunt. Composita signat circum, con, uel excellentiam, ϭεϱιέμι, ϭεϱίεχω, ϭεϱιέλυτο.
units.tr: περὶ πύργῳ, περὶ δὲ ἕλε [perì pýrgōi, perì dè hél(e)], about the tower, but he took, are Homeric usages. Compounds signify "around," "with," or excellence: περιέμι, περιέχω, περιέλυτο [periémi, periékhō, periélyto], I go around, I embrace, he was wrapped around.

units.la: AMΦI.
units.tr: AMPHI.

units.la: Αμφὶ eiusdem cuius significati,et constructionis est, & quandoque simul componūtur, ἀμφιπεδισπώφα. Dicitur tamen ἀμφ' αὐτῷ, pro illo, siue illius causa.
units.tr: Amphi has the same meaning and construction as its root, and sometimes the two are compounded together, as in amphipedispophā [ἀμφιπεδισπώφα]. It is said, however, amph' autō [ἀμφ' αὐτῷ], meaning for him, or for his sake.

units.la: ΑΠΟ.
units.tr: APO [ΑΠΟ].

units.la: Ἀπὸ semper cū genitiuo, ἀπὸ σκοπιᾶς, ἐspecula. ἀπὸ κώπης, à remo. ἀπὸ χόματος εἰπεῖν, ἀπὸ γλώττης εἰπεῖν, memoriter recitare, ἀπὸ τ' ἴσης ἀσίας, Ex æquis uiribus.
units.tr: Ἀπό always takes the genitive: from a lookout [ἀπὸ σκοπιᾶς], from a watch-tower; from the oar [ἀπὸ κώπης]; to speak from the mouth [ἀπὸ στόματος εἰπεῖν], that is, to recite by heart; to speak from the tongue [ἀπὸ γλώττης εἰπεῖν], to recite from memory; with equal strength [ἀπὸ τῆς ἴσης ἰσχύος].

units.la: Quandoq; habet uim aduerbij huius ἀπόθεν, procul. Hinc fit quod dicitur, ἀπ' ἐκατ, procul ab auribus, ἀπὸ τῆς σκοπῆς, præter propositum. ἀπὸ ξόπης, Alienum ab honestis moribus. Huic opponitur ἀπὸ ξόπης, quemadmodū Latin. ere, opponitur illi, ab re, ἀπὸ κωρῆς, intepestiuū.
units.tr: Sometimes it has the force of the adverb ἀπόθεν, from afar. Hence the phrases: far from the ears [ἀπ' ἀκοῆς], away from the purpose [ἀπὸ τῆς σκοπῆς], and [ἀπὸ τρόπου], contrary to honourable manners. Its opposite is ἀπὸ καιροῦ, untimely, just as in Latin "ab re" is opposed to the other expression, so that ἀπὸ καιροῦ means unseasonable.

units.la: Dicunt etiam loco aduerbij, ἀφ' ὧν, propterea, ἀπ' ἀρτι, post hoc, ex hoc tempore. ἀπ' ἐκείνης, iam tum, ex illo tempore, ἀπὸ ταυτομάτως, fortuito.
units.tr: They also use it adverbially: ἀφ' ὧν, for this reason; ἀπ' ἄρτι, from now on, from this time; ἀπ' ἐκείνης, from that time on, from that moment; ἀπὸ ταὐτομάτου, by chance.

units.la: ΥΠΟ.
units.tr: ΥΠΟ.

units.la: Ὑπὸ ὑπαί genitiuo sub, ὑφ' εἰμάτῳ, sub uefte, ὑπὸ κόλπῳ τῆς χείρας ἔχειν, sub sinu manum habere. Aut propter, οὐδὲ ὑπὸ. τὸ παντὸς περιπέτειας ... Necq; benefacio pro pter paupertatem.
units.tr: With the genitive, ὑπό means "under": ὑφ' εἱμάτῳ, under the garment; ὑπὸ κόλπῳ τῆς χείρας ἔχειν, to hold the hand under the fold, "sub sinu manum habere." It can also mean "on account of": οὐδὲ ὑπὸ [οὐδὲ ὑπὸ], and "I do not benefit on account of poverty."

units.la: Item cum datiuo etiam significat sub, ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῷ, uel ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῆς, In potestate sua redigere, potestatis suae facere. ὑπὸ ἀλςίδρῳ, uel ἀλςίδρου κάθημαι.
units.tr: With the dative, ὑπό also means "under": ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῷ [ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῷ], or ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῆς [ποιεῖσθαι ὑφ' ἑαυτῆς], to bring under one's power or to make subject to one's authority; ὑπὸ ἀλσίδρῳ [ὑπὸ ἀλσίδρῳ], or ἀλσίδρου κάθημαι [ἀλσίδρου κάθημαι], I sit under the grove.

units.la: ΥΠΕΡ.
units.tr: ΥΠΕΡ.

units.la: Ὑπὲρ, ὑπείρ cum genitiuo significat su per, de. ὑπὲρ κάπνῃς, super fumum. σκιᾶς ὄνου, De asini umbra. ὑπὲρ ὧν εἶπον, de quibus dixi. Dicunt etiam, ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ere noftra. Aut pro, ὑπὲρ κτησιφῶντος ὁ λόγος, pro Ctesiphonte oratio. ὑπὲρ τοῦ φίλου κινδυνεύω, Pro amico periclitor. Quod idem nonnunquam etiam significat cum datiuo poetice, ὑπὲρ τῷ φίλῳ κινδυνεύω. Nonnunquam etiam capitur pro cōtra. Sic Homerus, ὑπὲρ σέθεν, pro σὲ dixit.
units.tr: ὑπέρ with the genitive means "over" or "concerning": ὑπὲρ κάπνης [ὑπὲρ κάπνης], over the smoke; σκιᾶς ὄνου [σκιᾶς ὄνου], concerning the shadow of the ass; ὑπὲρ ὧν εἶπον [ὑπὲρ ὧν εἶπον], concerning what I have said. They also say ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν [ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν], for us, that is, "for our sake." It also means "for" or "on behalf of": ὑπὲρ Κτησιφῶντος ὁ λόγος [ὑπὲρ Κτησιφῶντος ὁ λόγος], the speech for Ctesiphon; ὑπὲρ τοῦ φίλου κινδυνεύω [ὑπὲρ τοῦ φίλου κινδυνεύω], I run danger for my friend. The same sense is sometimes given by the dative in poetry: ὑπὲρ τῷ φίλῳ κινδυνεύω [ὑπὲρ τῷ φίλῳ κινδυνεύω]. Sometimes it is also taken to mean "against." Thus Homer used ὑπὲρ σέθεν [ὑπὲρ σέθεν] for σέ, "for you."

units.la: Accusatiuo supra uel ultra, ὑπὲρ ἀνθρωπον φρονεῖ, Supra hominem sapit. τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς, Ea quae sunt supra nos. ὑπὲρ τὸν Θράκην ἢ Μακεδονίαν, Vltra Thraciam Macedonia. ὑπὲρ τὴν ὥραν φρονεῖν, Vl-tra peram sapere.
units.tr: With the accusative it means "above" or "beyond": ὑπὲρ ἀνθρωπον φρονεῖ [ὑπὲρ ἀνθρωπον φρονεῖ], he thinks above man, "he is wiser than a man"; τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς [τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς], the things above us; ὑπὲρ τὸν Θράκην ἢ Μακεδονίαν [ὑπὲρ τὸν Θράκην ἢ Μακεδονίαν], beyond Thrace or Macedonia; ὑπὲρ τὴν ὥραν φρονεῖν [ὑπὲρ τὴν ὥραν φρονεῖν], to be wise beyond one's purse.

units.la: ɣ 3 Capitur etiam aduerbialiter cum suo casu, ὑπὲρ ὧν, iccirco.
units.tr: ɣ 3 It is also used adverbially with its case, ὑπὲρ ὧν [ὑπὲρ ὧν], therefore.

units.la: Præpositiones compositæ cum verbis.
units.tr: Compound prepositions with verbs.

units.la: Præpositiones verbis cōpositæ, eundem casum quē extra compositionem expetunt, ὑπὲρ σē, ὑπερέχω σε.
units.tr: Prepositions compounded with verbs take the same case that they take outside composition: ὑπὲρ σε [ὑπὲρ σε], ὑπερέχω σε [ὑπερέχω σε].

units.la: Varius usus, uariaq; structura præpo sitionum poetis ἀσπὶς pro ὑπὸ, παρὰ pro ἀπὸ, ὑπὸ pro μή, Pindarus.
units.tr: Poets use prepositions in varied ways and structures: ἀσπὶς for ὑπό [ἀσπὶς], παρὰ for ἀπό [παρὰ], ὑπὸ for μή [ὑπὸ]; Pindar.

units.la: Celebre est poetis præpositiones cō positas dissoluere per alterius dictionis epenthesim, κατὰ χαῖα κάλυψε, pro χαῖα κατακάλυψε, ὡς δ' ἐγέλασε pro ἐξεγέλασε, ὅ, ἔρον εἶπο, pro ἔξεντο ἔεγν.
units.tr: It is common for poets to separate compound prepositions by inserting another word (epenthesis): κατὰ χαῖα κάλυψε [κατὰ χαῖα κάλυψε] for χαῖα κατακάλυψε [χαῖα κατακάλυψε]; ὡς δ' ἐγέλασε [ὡς δ' ἐγέλασε] for ἐξεγέλασε [ἐξεγέλασε]; ἔρον εἶπο [ἔρον εἶπο] for ἔξεντο ἔεγν [ἔξεντο ἔεγν].

units.la: Interdum plures dictiones intercedunt, οἱ κᾶ βᾶς ὑπέρ ὀν ἡλίου ἡάτιον, pro κατηδιον.
units.tr: Sometimes several words come between them: οἱ κᾶ βᾶς ὑπέρ ὀν ἡλίου ἡάτιον [οἱ κᾶ βᾶς ὑπέρ ὀν ἡλίου ἡάτιον] for κατηδιον [κατηδιον].

units.la: Insuper præpositiones dictionibus componere solent poetæ, à quibus resolvendæ sunt, ἰδάκλω καταπολεμένσι, pro πολεμένσι κατ' ἰδάκλω.
units.tr: Poets also often join prepositions to words from which they must be separated: ἰδάκλω καταπολεμένσι [ἰδάκλω καταπολεμένσι] for πολεμένσι κατ' ἰδάκλω [πολεμένσι κατ' ἰδάκλω].

units.la: Anastrophe præpositionum.
units.tr: Anastrophe of prepositions.

units.la: Deniq; præpositiones sæpe suis casi bus postponuntur apud poetas, κατὰ ὧν ἐξ, ἀρτέμιδι ξωῷ. Et in bissyllabis pyrrhichijs accentus transfertur, ὑπὸ, ξαν- θῶ ἐπὶ Διννέντι. In oratione uero pedestri solum ὦ postponitur, τύπων ὦ: alias ὦι sine casu cum accentu in prima, ad uerbium est, significatio excellenter sic πάεα praesto.
units.tr: Finally, prepositions are often placed after their cases by the poets: κατὰ ὧν ἐξ [κατὰ ὧν ἐξ], ἀρτέμιδι ξωῷ [ἀρτέμιδι ξωῷ]. In dissyllabic pyrrhics the accent is moved back: ὑπὸ, ξανθῶ ἐπὶ Διννέντι [ὑπὸ, ξανθῶ ἐπὶ Διννέντι]. In prose, only ὦ is placed after its case: τύπων ὦ [τύπων ὦ]. Otherwise ὦι is used without a case, with the accent on the first syllable, as an adverb; its meaning is excellently shown by πάεα, "at hand" [πάεα].

units.la: CONSTRVCTIO CONIVNCTIONVM.
units.tr: CONSTRUCTION OF CONJUNCTIONS.

units.la: Oniunctiones non modo reli quas orationis partes connectendi uim habet, uerū etiam inter se, & unà cum aduerbijs uarie connexae, variam obtinent significationem, & constructionem, quarum hic aliquot subijciemus exempla.
units.tr: Conjunctions not only have the power of connecting the other parts of speech, but when they are variously linked with one another and with adverbs they also take on various meanings and constructions. Here we shall set out a few examples.

units.la: AΛΛΑ.
units.tr: ALLA.

units.la: ἀλλὰ γὰρ, ἀλλὰ δὴ, ἀλλὰ νῦ δέγ, uel νῦ δὴ ἀνὰ. ἀλλὰ, id est, at enim. ἀλλ᾽ ἔν, saltem, tamē, potius. ἀλλὰ μὴ; nunquid? quandoq; nō interrogatiue, pro, non autem, ἀλλὰ δὴ κρ̀, quinimo, atque etiam, esto, concedendi. ἀλλά τοι, atqui, at uero. ἀλλὰ μὲν, atqui, at uero. In principio orationis significat enimuero, ἀλλὰ μὲν οὐδ᾽, neque uero, sed nec{y}. ἀλλ' ἢ, sed nūquid. ἀλλ' ὅτι; ἀλλ' ὅτι ἢ; utrum? nunquid ? ἀλλ' ὅτι, nisi quod, quàm quod, ut ἐχ' ἑτέρου, ἀλλ' ὅτι. nō aliud, nisi quod, uel quàm quod. ἀλλ' εἰ πέρ, de quo dicetur postea.
units.tr: ἀλλὰ γὰρ, ἀλλὰ δὴ, ἀλλὰ νῦ δέ, or νῦ δὴ ἀνά [ἀλλὰ γὰρ, ἀλλὰ δὴ, ἀλλὰ νῦ δέ, νῦ δὴ ἀνά]: "alla" means "but indeed" or "but for that matter". ἀλλ᾽ ἔν [ἀλλ᾽ ἔν]: at least, yet, rather. ἀλλὰ μὴ [ἀλλὰ μὴ]: surely not? Sometimes, when not interrogative, it means "but not". ἀλλὰ δὴ καί [ἀλλὰ δὴ καί]: nay rather, and indeed; also, granted. ἀλλά τοι [ἀλλά τοι]: but truly, but yet. ἀλλὰ μέν [ἀλλὰ μέν]: but truly, but yet. At the beginning of a sentence it means "indeed". ἀλλὰ μὲν οὐδέ [ἀλλὰ μὲν οὐδέ]: nor indeed, but not even. ἀλλ᾽ ἦ [ἀλλ᾽ ἦ]: but surely not? ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι [ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι]; ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι ἦ [ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι ἦ]: whether? surely not? ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι [ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι]: except that, or than that, as in ἐχ᾽ ἑτέρου, ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι [ἐχ᾽ ἑτέρου, ἀλλ᾽ ὅτι]: not another thing, except that or than that. ἀλλ᾽ εἰ πέρ [ἀλλ᾽ εἰ πέρ], of which more will be said later.

units.la: ΔΕ.
units.tr: DE.

units.la: Δέγε, δ' ἔπει, δ' ἔτοι, autem. δ' ἐ δ' ἡ, porrò autē, ut ἐαν δ' ἐ δ' ἡ συμφέρει, Porrò autem si conferat, μεταβατικόν ὄξιν.
units.tr: δέγε, δ᾽ ἔπει, δ᾽ ἔτοι [δέγε, δ᾽ ἔπει, δ᾽ ἔτοι]: "but", "indeed". δ᾽ ἐ δ᾽ ἡ [δ᾽ ἐ δ᾽ ἡ]: "moreover, but", as in ἐὰν δ᾽ ἐ δ᾽ ἡ συμφέρῃ [ἐὰν δ᾽ ἐ δ᾽ ἡ συμφέρῃ]: "moreover, if it be advantageous". It is a transitional usage.

units.la: MEN.
units.tr: MEN.

units.la: Δὲ δὲ μὲν, sefe in oratione mutuo con- sequuntur, sic ut μὲν quidem praecedat, δὲ uero sequatur. ἐτῶ μὲν λαλεῖ, ἐκεῖνος δὲ σωπᾷ, Hic quidem loquitur, ille uero filet.
units.tr: δὲ and μὲν follow each other in a sentence, so that μὲν, "indeed", comes first and δὲ, "but", follows. ἑτῷ μὲν λαλεῖ, ἐκεῖνος δὲ σιωπᾷ [ἑτῷ μὲν λαλεῖ, ἐκεῖνος δὲ σιωπᾷ]: "This one indeed speaks, but that one keeps silent."

units.la: HMEN HAE.
units.tr: HMEN HAE.

units.la: Similiter sefe confequuntur eorum compofita, ἠμὲν & ἡδὲ, quę quidem sunt inchoatiua orationis, & ἠμὲν quidē praecedit, ἡδὲ uero sequitur. ἠμὲν ὅσοι ναίουσι ἂεἠνὸν, ἡδὲ ὅσοι κληρώσαντο χθόνα, Et quicunque habitant cœlum, & quicunque fortiti sunt terram.
units.tr: Their compounds follow each other in the same way: ἠμὲν and ἠδὲ [ἠμὲν, ἠδὲ], which introduce a sentence; ἠμὲν, "indeed", comes first, and ἠδὲ, "and", follows. ἠμὲν ὅσοι ναίουσι [ἠμὲν ὅσοι ναίουσιν οὐρανόν], ἠδὲ ὅσοι κληρώσαντο χθόνα [ἠδὲ ὅσοι κληρώσαντο χθόνα]: "both all who dwell in heaven and all who have been allotted the earth."

units.la: MENTOI.
units.tr: MENTOI.

units.la: Μεντοι, uero, sane, assentientis est: interdum terdum ornatus caufa magís quàm fi-gnificationis ponitur, uel explendæ ora tionís gratia, ut τᾶτο μὲν τοι τοιᾶτο, Hoc fa nè tale eft. Sic Ariftoph. in Pluto, καὶ τῶν τὰ μὲν τοι ταῦτα: quę locutio eft Attica, pro eo quod eft, Atq︰ hæc quidem funt huiufcemodi, uel ita fe habent. Clausula eft fuperioris fermonis, & transit ad a-lium.
units.tr: μέντοι, "truly", "certainly", expresses assent. Sometimes it is placed for ornament rather than meaning, or to fill out the sentence, as in τοῦτο μὲν τοι τοιοῦτον [τᾶτο μὲν τοι τοιᾶτο]: "this is indeed of such a kind". So Aristophanes in the Plutus: καὶ τῶν τὰ μὲν τοι ταῦτα [καὶ τῶν τὰ μὲν τοι ταῦτα]: "and of these things, indeed, such are they", which is an Attic idiom meaning "and indeed these things are of this kind, or stand thus". It is a closing formula for the preceding discourse, and passes on to something else.

units.la: Dicitur etiam fic, καὶ ταῦτα μὲν τοι ταῦ-τη, Sed de his hactenus.
units.tr: It is also said in this way: καὶ ταῦτα μὲν τοι ταύτῃ [καὶ ταῦτα μὲν τοι ταύτῃ]: "but so much for these matters".

units.la: Accipitur etiam μὲν δή, ut respondeat particulæ μὲν, sic ut μὲν præcedente, se-quatur μέντοι, positum pro δέ.
units.tr: It is also taken as μὲν δή [μὲν δή], to answer the particle μὲν [μὲν], so that when μὲν comes first, μέντοι [μέντοι] follows, put in place of δέ [δέ].

units.la: Est etiam aduersatiuum, sicut Latinis uerum.
units.tr: It is also adversative, as verum is in Latin.

units.la: MENT AN.
units.tr: MENTAN.
