units.la: Μεντᾶν, atqui, at. Δικαίως μὲν τᾶν ἀπέ-δωκον, Atqui iuste morte affectus fuis-sem, μαίνοιτο μὲν τᾶν, at infaniret. μὲν ἔγγε ναὶ, quinimo, uero, atqui, μέντοι τι, μέν-τοι γε, nimirum, tamen.
units.tr: μεντᾶν, "but yet", "but". Δικαίως μὲν τᾶν ἀπέδωκον [Δικαίως μὲν τᾶν ἀπέδωκον]: "Yet I would have been justly put to death"; μαίνοιτο μὲν τᾶν [μαίνοιτο μὲν τᾶν]: "but he would have been mad". μὲν ἔγγε ναί [μὲν ἔγγε ναί]: "nay rather, indeed, but yet"; μέντοι τι [μέντοι τι], μέντοι γε [μέντοι γε]: "certainly, nevertheless".

units.la: KAI.
units.tr: KAI.

units.la: Καὶ præponitur dictionibus in ora-tione, τε uero sequitur inclinata, Θεοί τε,
units.tr: καί is placed before words in a sentence, while τε, which is enclitic, follows: θεοί τε [θεοί τε]...

units.la: γ ς ἢ ἀνέρες, Diíῳ & uiri. Et ita inter sese cõ struuntur, ut π̈ precedat, ἢ sequatur. καί τοιγε, καίτοι, atqui, etiã, uerum, sed, quan-quam & quidem, proinde, itaᾳ.
units.tr: "...gods and men [θεοί τε ἠδ᾽ ἄνδρες]", "gods and men". And so they are construed with each other, so that καί comes first and ἠ follows. καί τοιγε, καίτοι [καί τοιγε, καίτοι]: "but yet", "also", "indeed", "however", "although", "and yet", "certainly", "therefore", "thus".

units.la: Καὶ δή, continuo, protinus, hoc est, i-deo. καὶ μὲν, atqui. καὶ Atticis sæpe ge-minatur, ἢ μὲν τοι καὶ, atque etiam. καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἐγώ, etenim ego quoque, καὶ δὴ καὶ, e-quidem etiam, καὶ Τοι καὶ, atque adeo. καὶ γὰρ αὖ καὶ, & rursus etiam. καὶ ἵνα δὴ καὶ, & ut etiam, καὶ μὲν καὶ, quin etiam. ἢ ἐγωγε ἢ αὐτὸς, & ego ipse. Nam ἢ Atticis qui-dem παρέλκει.
units.tr: καὶ δή [καὶ δή]: "at once", "immediately", that is, "for this reason". καὶ μέν [καὶ μέν]: "but yet". Among the Attic writers καί is often doubled: ἢ μὲν τοι καί [ἢ μὲν τοι καί]: "and indeed also". καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἐγώ [καὶ γὰρ καὶ ἐγώ]: "for I too". καὶ δὴ καί [καὶ δὴ καί]: "indeed also". καὶ τοι καί [καὶ τοι καί]: "and indeed even". καὶ γὰρ αὖ καί [καὶ γὰρ αὖ καί]: "and again also". καὶ ἵνα δὴ καί [καὶ ἵνα δὴ καί]: "and that also". καὶ μὲν καί [καὶ μὲν καί]: "nay, even". ἐγὼ γε ἢ αὐτός [ἐγὼ γε ἢ αὐτός]: "I myself also". For among the Attic writers ἢ [ἢ] is often redundant.

units.la: KAN.
units.tr: KAN.

units.la: Καν, pro ἢ ἐαν, & si, uel quod si, uel sin, cõstruitur Coniunctiuis, καν ἀναγκασθῇ, quod si cogatur.
units.tr: καν, for ἢ ἐάν [ἢ ἐάν], "and if", "or even if", "but if", is construed with the subjunctive: καν ἀναγκασθῇ [καν ἀναγκασθῇ]: "but if he is compelled".

units.la: Cum uero significat quamuis, gau-det Optatiuis, etiam si tanquam de præ-senti sermo sit. Quomodo & Plato secū do de Rep.de cane loquens, οὐ δ᾽ἂν γνῶ-εἰμον ἰδ᾽ ἡ ἀπαξ ἀζεται, καν μηδὲν ὠώποτε ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἀγαθὸν πεπόνθοι, Quemcunque conspexerit notum, salutat, quamuis ni-hil unquam ab eo susceperit boni.
units.tr: When it means "although", it takes the optative, even if the discourse is about the present, as Plato says in the second book of the Republic about a dog: "Whomever it has seen before it greets, even though it has never received any good from him" [οὗ δ᾽ ἂν γνῷ εἰδὼς ἰδὼν ἢ ἅπαξ ἀσπάζεται, καν μηδὲν ποτὲ ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἀγαθὸν πεπόνθοι].

units.la: Cum autem significat atque adeo, uel etiam, iungitur etiam Optatiuo atqz Indicatiuo.
units.tr: When it means "indeed" or "even", it is joined both to the optative and to the indicative.

units.la: Indicatiuo καὶ ἐπῄνεν, καὶ στέφανον λέγον, Ego laudassem, & coronandos cē suissem.
units.tr: With the indicative: καὶ ἐπῄνεν, καὶ στέφανον λέγων [καὶ ἐπῄνεν, καὶ στέφανον λέγων]: "I would have praised him, and said that he should be crowned".

units.la: Optatiuo, Aristoph. καὶ θεγοπατάτι νη γὰρ ὁμόσαι ξιώβολον. Significat etiam saltem.
units.tr: With the optative, in Aristophanes: καὶ θεὸν πατάξαι, νὴ γὰρ ὀμόσαι ξιώβολον [καὶ θεὸν πατάξαι, νὴ γὰρ ὀμόσαι ξιώβολον]: "even to strike a god, for by Zeus, to swear by a two-obol piece". It also means "at least".

units.la: Et quando sæpe geminatur in oratione, ponitur pro siue.
units.tr: And when it is often doubled in a sentence, it is put for "whether... or whether".

units.la: Est etiam quandoque particula potentialis.
units.tr: It is also sometimes a potential particle.

units.la: KAN EI.
units.tr: KAN EI.

units.la: Καὶ εἰ, Indicatiuo iungitur, καὶ εἰ πάντα τὰ ταῦτα ὑπῆρχεν, & si in eo omnia hæc essent.
units.tr: καὶ εἰ is joined to the indicative: καὶ εἰ πάντα τὰ ταῦτα ὑπῆρχεν [καὶ εἰ πάντα τὰ ταῦτα ὑπῆρχεν]: "even if all these things were in him".

units.la: Ponitur etiam cum Optatiuo, & per Tmesim, καὶ ἀσέβειαν εἰ καταγνωσοι τις, Et si impietatem condemnet quis. Vnde frequens est apud Aristotelem, καὶ εἴτι τοιοῦτον εἴπερ, & si quid aliud simile.
units.tr: It is also placed with the optative, and by tmesis: καὶ ἀσέβειαν εἰ καταγνοίη τις [καὶ ἀσέβειαν εἰ καταγνοίη τις]: "even if someone should condemn impiety". Hence it is frequent in Aristotle: καὶ εἴ τι τοιοῦτον εἴπερ [καὶ εἴ τι τοιοῦτον εἴπερ]: "and if anything else of the kind".

units.la: KAN EI MH.
units.tr: KAI EI MĒ.

units.la: Καὶ εἰ μὴ, & si, tametsi, si non, ut καὶ εἰ μὴ, δι' ἄλλην αἰτίαν, ἀλλὰ δι' αὐτὴν, & si non ob aliam caufam, certe ob iftam.
units.tr: Καὶ εἰ μὴ: and if, although, if not. For example: "and if not because of another cause, but certainly because of this one" [καὶ εἰ μὴ, δι' ἄλλην αἰτίαν, ἀλλὰ δι' αὐτὴν].

units.la: Kaì etiam per fe fignificat etiam fi, ut πότερ᾽ ἂν μηδ᾽ εἰ ἀδίκων φαίνηται τὴν πόλιν, ἢ καὶ ἀδίκων σκοπεῖτε, utrū fi publice infons fit, an etiam fi nocens confyderate.
units.tr: Kai also by itself means "even if", as in: "whether, even if the city should appear unjust, or even if you consider it unjust" [πότερ᾽ ἂν μηδ᾽ εἰ ἀδίκων φαίνηται τὴν πόλιν, ἢ καὶ ἀδίκων σκοπεῖτε].

units.la: H.
units.tr: Ē.

units.la: H uel, dum capitur definite, uel declaratiue fola iacet, ut ἰλιάδ᾽ α. βούλομ᾽ ἐγὼ λαὸν σοὸν ἐμμεῖναι, ἢ ἀπολέσθαι, Ego malo populum faluum effe, et nō perire. Quo in loco ἡ fignificat, & non.
units.tr: Ē, either when it is taken disjunctively or when it lies alone in a declarative sense, as in Iliad 1: "I would rather that your people be safe than perish" [βούλομ᾽ ἐγὼ λαὸν σοὸν ἐμμεῖναι, ἢ ἀπολέσθαι]. In this passage ē means "and not".

units.la: Capitur etiam dubitatiue, τί δὲ λαὸν ἤγαγεν ἐνθάδε, ἢ ἀχ' ἑλένης ἕνεκόμεθα; Quid autem populum adduxit huc? an non propter Helenam formosam?
units.tr: It is also taken interrogatively: "But why did he bring the people here, or did we not come for the sake of beautiful Helen?" [τί δὲ λαὸν ἤγαγεν ἐνθάδε, ἢ ἀχ᾽ ἑλένης ἕνεκόμεθα;]

units.la: HTOI.
units.tr: ĒTOI.

units.la: Hτοι quandoqz idem ualet quod μὲν, & eft initialis in oratione, ut ἢτοι ὃ γ᾽ ὡς εἶπων κατ᾽ ἀρ᾽ ἔζετο, Ille quidem fic fatus cõ fedit.
units.tr: Ētoi sometimes has the same force as men ("indeed") and stands at the beginning of a sentence, as in: "He, indeed, having spoken thus, sat down" [ἢτοι ὃ γ᾽ ὡς εἶπων κατ᾽ ἀρ᾽ ἔζετο].

units.la: Quandoque eft difiunctiua æquiualens coniunctioni ἢ, quam præcedit in oratione, ἢτοι ἀγαθὸν, ἢ φαῦλον, uel bonum uel malum.
units.tr: Sometimes it is disjunctive, equivalent to the conjunction ē, which precedes it in the sentence, as in: "either good or bad" [ἢτοι ἀγαθὸν, ἢ φαῦλον].

units.la: HΠOΥ.
units.tr: ĒPOU.

units.la: Hπου ualet ἢτοι, & eodem modo post ponitur ei in oratione, ἢ, ut ei ζῷον, ἄνοῦν ἢ πτε λογικὸν, ἢ μὴ, Si animal, igitur rationa le est, uel irrationale.
units.tr: Ēpou means ētoi, and in the same way ē is placed after it in the sentence, as in: "If it is an animal, then it is either rational or irrational" [εἰ ζῷον, ἢπου λογικὸν ἢ μή].

units.la: Ponitur etiam pro ἢ, quam, ut, ᾧ ολὺ μᾶλλον, ἢ πτε τὶς ἄλλῳ, Multo magis, quã quiuis alius.
units.tr: It is also used for ē, "than", as in: "much more than anyone else" [ᾧ πολὺ μᾶλλον, ἢ ὁτιοῦν τις ἄλλῳ].

units.la: EI.
units.tr: EI.

units.la: Ei construitur plerunque Indicatiuo, & habet uim optatiui, uel optatiui certe loco ponitur, cum ei additur ἀν particu la potentialis. Ioan. 8. εἰ ὁ Θεὸς πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἦν, ἠγαπᾶτε ἂν ἐμέ, Si deus esset pater ue ster, diligeretis me.
units.tr: Ei is mostly construed with the indicative and has the force of the optative, or it stands in place of the optative when the potential particle an is added. John 8: "If God were your Father, you would love me" [εἰ ὁ Θεὸς πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἦν, ἠγαπᾶτε ἂν ἐμέ].

units.la: Nonnunquam cum optatiuo, εἰ ἡδὺ νῦν τ᾽ ἀγαθὸν εἴη, ταύτῃ ἂν ὁςὶ ζοιτο ἡ εὐδαιμονία, Si uoluptas ipsum bonum esset, hoc pacto definiri posset felicitas.
units.tr: Sometimes it is used with the optative: "If pleasure were itself the good, happiness could be defined in this way" [εἰ ἡδὺ νῦν τ᾽ ἀγαθὸν εἴη, ταύτῃ ἂν ὁρίζοιτο ἡ εὐδαιμονία].

units.la: Interdum cum coniunctiuo, præser= tim si cũ aliis cõiunctionibus capiatur. ἰλιάδ. α. εἴπερ γάρ τε χόλον γε καὶ αὐτὴ μὴ καταπέψῃ, quod si iram ipso die conco= xerit. εἰ μὴ, id est nisi, ut τί δ᾽ἐ, εἰ μὴ, quid aliud nisi. εἰ ὃ μὴ, sin minus, alioqui. εἰ δ᾽ ἄγε, age, agedum. εἰ γοῦν, si saltem. εἰ γὰρ ὤφελον, dicitur, pro, εἴθε ὤφελον, utinam. εἰ δ᾽ ἀρα, εἴπερ ἀρα, ἀλλ᾽ εἴπερ, ἐὰν δ᾽ἐ, Hę clau fulæ, dum per parenthesim inseruntur orationibus, significant, quod si quando id faciendum sit, uel quod si quoddam est huiusmodi, aut aliud simile, prout oratio postulat, ἀμπελον ὑ δλεῖ ἀπλεῶς περιπάζοντ᾽ ὁ τὸ βόξυ᾽, ἀλλ᾽ εἴπερ, ὅταν δέομαι λαμβάνῃ, quod si quando id faciendum sit, tum certe demum, cum nigra iam uua fuerit. ἀπέχεσθαι οἱ μοναχοὶ τῆς σαρκοφαγίας, εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα, ἐν ἀδρεία, Abstinent monachi ab esu carnium, quod si quando uescantur carnibus, id in ægritudine est. οὐδεὶς εἰς ψάμμον ἀπείρει, ἐαν δ᾽ ἑ, τῆς γεωργίας ἀπὸ ἑῳς ἔξιν. Nullus arenæ mandat femina, quod si quis sit huiusmodi, is agriculturæ inexpertus est.
units.tr: At other times it is used with the subjunctive, especially when it is taken together with other conjunctions. Iliad 1: "for if she does not digest her anger on the same day" [εἴπερ γάρ τε χόλον γε καὶ αὐτὴ μὴ καταπέψῃ]. Ei mē, that is "unless", as in "what else but" [τί δ᾽ ἐ, εἰ μὴ]. Ei ho mē, "but if not, otherwise". Ei d' age, "come, come on". Ei goun, "if at least". Ei gar ōphelon is used for ei thě ōphelon, "would that". Ei d' ara, eiper ara, all' eiper, ean de: these clauses, when they are inserted into sentences by way of parenthesis, signify "if at any time this is to be done", or "if there is anything of this kind, or something similar", as the sentence requires, as in: "the vine, if the grape is not simply to be gathered, but when it is wanted" [ἄμπελον ὑπὸ δλεῖ ἁπλῶς περιπάζοντα ὁ τὸ βότρυ᾽, ἀλλ᾽ εἴπερ, ὅταν δέομαι λαμβάνῃ]: "if at any time it is to be done, then certainly at last, when the grape is already black". "The monks abstain from eating flesh; but if they ever eat meat, it is in sickness" [ἀπέχεσθαι οἱ μοναχοὶ τῆς σαρκοφαγίας, εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα, ἐν ἀρρωστίᾳ]. "No one sows seed in sand; but if anyone does so, he is inexperienced in farming" [οὐδεὶς εἰς ψάμμον ἀπείρει, ἐὰν δέ τις, τῆς γεωργίας ἄπειρος ἔστιν].

units.la: EAN KAI EΠEIΔAN.
units.tr: EAN KAI EPEIDAN.

units.la: ἐαν & ἐπεὶ ἀν, gaudent Coniunctiuo, ut ἐαν θέλης, si uelis. ἐπειδὰν ἴδωσι, cum uidissent.
units.tr: Ean and epeidan (epeidan), that is ean and epeidan, take the subjunctive, as in: "if you wish" [ἐαν θέλῃς]; "when they had seen" [ἐπειδὰν ἴδωσι].

units.la: ΕΠΕΙ & ΕΠΕΙΔΗ.
units.tr: EPEI AND EPEIDĒ.

units.la: ἐπεὶ & ἐπειδή, iunguntur Indicatiuo & Infinitiuo, ἐπεὶ δ᾽ ὥφθη, ἐπειδή δ᾽ ἡμέραν, ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα, simul atque, simul ut, hoc est, ὡς τάχιστα.
units.tr: Epei and epeidē are joined with the indicative and the infinitive: "as soon as it appeared" [ἐπεὶ δ᾽ ὥφθη]; "when day came" [ἐπειδὴ δ᾽ ἡμέρα]; "as soon as" [ἐπειδὴ τάχιστα], that is, "as soon as possible" [ὡς τάχιστα].

units.la: INA.
units.tr: HINA.

units.la: ἵνα construitur Coniunctiuis, ἵνα ἵδὲ ξῳ, ut doceam. Et Optatiuis, si de re praeterita fiat sermo, ἀφίκετο, ἵνα ἴδῃ, ... uenit, ut spectaret.
units.tr: Hina is construed with the subjunctive, as in "hina didaxō", "that I may teach". It is also construed with the optative when the talk is of past events: "he came in order that he might see" [ἀφίκετο, ἵνα ἴδοι].

units.la: Et Indicatiuis in praeterito imperfecto, perfecto & indefinito, ubi aliquid de re praeterita uolumus subesse, aut non subesse, ἐχρῆν αὐτὸν λαβεῖν συγγραφὴν, ἵν᾿ εἶχεν κατὰ νόμους ἀπαιτεῖν, Oportebat eum accipere syngraphām, ut posset iure exigere.
units.tr: It is also construed with the indicative in the imperfect, perfect and aorist tenses, when we want to imply that something in past time was or was not the case: "He ought to have taken the bond, so that he could demand it by law" [ἐχρῆν αὐτὸν λαβεῖν συγγραφὴν, ἵν᾿ εἶχεν κατὰ νόμους ἀπαιτεῖν].

units.la: ΓΑΡ.
units.tr: GAR.

units.la: Γαρ his coniungi potest, γάρ τοι, γὰρ, γάρ. ἀλλ᾿ δὲ αὖ, γάρ, ἔπου, δὲ ἀλλ᾿ πον, δὲ τ᾿ αὖ, pro γὰρ τοι αὖ.
units.tr: Gar can be joined with these: "gar toi", "gar", "gar" [γάρ τοι, γὰρ, γάρ]; "all' de au", "gar", "epou", "de all' pou", "de t' au", which stands for "gar toi au".

units.la: ΟΤΙ.
units.tr: HOTI.

units.la: ὅτι gaudet Indicatiuis, λέγει ὅτι ἥξει, dicit quod ueniet.
units.tr: Hoti takes the indicative: "he says that he will come" [λέγει ὅτι ἥξει].

units.la: In locutione narratiua additur Optatiuo, ἠγγέλλετο ὅτι γένοιτο. καὶ ἦν, καὶ ἔσοιτο, Nunciabat quod fieret, & esset, & erit.
units.tr: In narrative speech it takes the optative: "he reported that it might happen" [ἠγγέλλετο ὅτι γένοιτο]. "And it was, and it would be" [καὶ ἦν, καὶ ἔσοιτο]. He reported that it would happen, and that it was and will be.

units.la: Iungitur quandoque superlatiuis, ὅτι πλεῖστον, ὅτι μάλιστα, quàm plurimum, quàm maxime.
units.tr: It is sometimes joined with superlatives: "as much as possible" [ὅτι πλεῖστον]; "as much as possible, as far as possible" [ὅτι μάλιστα].

units.la: APA.
units.tr: APA.

units.la: {ἀρα} ἀρα alijs dictionibus conftructa fignifi- cat dubitationem, ἐκ οἶδα ὅτι λέγεις ἀρα. Non noui quid diceret. ἐγένετο ἀρα, fuiffet. Διετέθηκε ἄρα, conftituiffet, ἕτως ἀρα φαίνῃς, fic fugias. ὡς ἐδόκει ὅπου ἄρα ὅτι βαίνοις, quam timeo, quorfum euadas.
units.tr: ἄρα, when construed with other words, signifies doubt: οὐκ οἶδα ὅτι λέγεις ἄρα [I do not know what you are saying]. I did not know what he was saying. ἐγένετο ἄρα [it had happened], it would have been. Διετέθηκε ἄρα [he had disposed], he would have arranged. ἕτως ἄρα φαίνῃς [so you seem], so flee. ὡς ἐδόκει ὅπου ἄρα ὅτι βαίνοις [as it seemed, where indeed you were going], what I fear, whither you will escape.

units.la: APA.
units.tr: APA.

units.la: ἄρα uero hoc modo conftruitur, ἄρ' ἐν. ἀρά γε, utrum. ἄρα οὖν, itaque: & ponitur in initio orationis, ἄρ' ἐν, utrum, an non. ἀρά ποτε, utrum tandē. ἄρα μὴ, nunquid, utrum, idem ualet quod ἀλλὰ μὴ, in con sequentia orationis.
units.tr: ἄρα is construed in this way: ἄρ' ἐν [ἄρ' ἐν], whether. ἀρά γε [ἀρά γε], whether. ἄρα οὖν [ἄρα οὖν], therefore, and it is placed at the beginning of a sentence: ἄρ' ἐν, whether or not. ἀρά ποτε [ἀρά ποτε], whether at last. ἄρα μή [ἄρα μή], surely not? whether; it has the same force as ἀλλὰ μή, in the sequence of the sentence.

units.la: OYN.
units.tr: OYN.

units.la: Οὖν postponitur nominibus infinitis ὁποιοσιοῦν, qualiscunque. ὁποσιοῦν quā tuscunque, ὁποσοσῦν, quotuslibet. ὁπηλίκοσοῦν, quantuscunque. ὁποδαπποῦν; cuiascunque. ὁποσοπλασιῶν, quamlibet multiplex. ὁπότεροσῦν, uterlibet. ὁπωσοῦν, ὁπωσιοῦν, ὁπηοῦν, quouis modo, quomodocunque.
units.tr: Οὖν is placed after indefinite words: ὁποιοσιοῦν [ὁποιοσοῦν], of whatever kind. ὁποσιοῦν, however much. ὁποσοσῦν, however many. ὁπηλίκοσοῦν, however great. ὁποδαπποῦν [ὁποδαποῦν], of whatever country. ὁποσοπλασιῶν, however many times over. ὁπότεροσῦν, whichever of the two. ὁπωσοῦν, ὁπωσιοῦν, ὁπηοῦν, in any way whatever.

units.la: ATTA.
units.tr: ATTA.

units.la: ἄττα, multis adiectiuis iungitur, ut ποίης ποίοις ἄτλα, πόσ' ἄτλα, πόλλ' ἄτλα, ὀλίγ' ἄτλα, ἕτερ ἄτλα, τοιαῦτ' ἄτλα.
units.tr: ἄττα is joined to many adjectives: ποίης ἄττα, of some sort; πόσ' ἄττα, some number; πόλλ' ἄττα, many things; ὀλίγ' ἄττα, a few things; ἕτερ' ἄττα, certain other things; τοιαῦτ' ἄττα, things of such a kind.

units.la: Sunt enim additamenta plus ornatus, quàm significationis afferentia orationi, ueluti Latinis, quis tandem, quisnam, qualisnam.
units.tr: For these are additions that bring more ornament than meaning to the sentence, as in Latin quis tandem, quisnam, qualisnam.

units.la: Ponitur etiam per se, pro πνά, ut ἐλεγὼ ἄτλα, dicebam quaedam. Quare subiungitur quandoq; substantiuis nominibus. εἰς δείματ' ἄτλα. In interrogationibus quosdam seruit & interrogationibus; cum est aspiratum, ut ὥσ ἠ ἄτλα ποτὲ διελέχθη; quomodo & quae disseruit? Nam relatiua interdum pro interrogatiuis ponuntur.
units.tr: It is also used by itself for τινά [some], as ἐλεγὼ ἄττα, I was saying certain things. Hence it is sometimes joined to nouns: εἰς δείματ' ἄττα [into certain fears]. In questions it serves also as an interrogative; when aspirated, as ὥσ' ἡ ἄττα ποτὲ διελέχθη [how and what did she ever discourse]? In what way and what things did she discourse? For relatives are sometimes put in place of interrogatives.

units.la: ΗΠΟΥ.
units.tr: ΗΠΟΥ.

units.la: ἦτε utiq;, profecto, nimirum, seruit etiam interrogationi, ut Latinis nempe.
units.tr: ἦ που [ἦτε], surely, certainly, no doubt; it also serves in questions, as nempe does in Latin.

units.la: Significat etiam ἦπε & ἦπέ γε, multo magis, & praeponitur illis ὅπε, ut ὅπε ἐκεῖνοι οἰκῆσαι πόλεις οἷοί τε γεγόνασι, ἦπου ἡμεῖς ἂν διωνῃσείμεθα καταοχεῖν, quandoquidem illi ualent inhabitare ciuitates, multo magis nos possemus.
units.tr: It also signifies ἦπε and ἦπέ γε, much more so, and ὅπε is placed before them, as ὅπε ἐκεῖνοι οἰκῆσαι πόλεις οἷοί τε γεγόνασι, ἦπου ἡμεῖς ἂν δυνηθείημεν καταοικεῖν [ἦπου], since those were able to inhabit cities, much more could we.

units.la: Eadē seruata syntaxi significat etiam nonnunquam, multo minus, ut ὅτῳ αὐτὸς κεάπτωρ οὐ δύνᾶται, ἢπου ἡμεῖς, ἰδιώται δὲ ὑπθεὶμψ ἂν; Quandoquidē imperator nō potest, multo minus nos priuati homines possemus. Sic Athenæus libro undecimo. ἀδύνατον δὲ ἢ ἢ φαιδρὸν κατὰ τὸ κεάτλω εἶ, ἢπου γε καὶ ἐρωμένον αὐτὸ γεγο- νέναι, Fieri non potest ut Phædrus So- cratis ætate fuerit, multo minus ut ama- sius eius fuerit, uel nedum ut amasius ei us fuerit.
units.tr: With the same construction it sometimes also signifies much less: since the emperor himself cannot, much less could we private men. So Athenaeus in book eleven: it is impossible that Phaedrus was of Socrates' age, much less that he was his lover, or, not to say that he was his lover.

units.la: Quandoque illi subiungitur χολὴ γε, quod etiam significat multo minus, & dicitur coniunctim, ἢπου χολὴ γε, pro, multo minus Attice.
units.tr: Sometimes γε is added to it, which also means much less; and they are written together, ἦπου γε [ἢπου χολὴ γε], meaning much less, in Attic.

units.la: ἢ οὐ̃ ποτε, ecquando, autem, ἢ δὲ, nón ne, pro quo quandoque dícunt ἢ οὐ. ἢ δὲ ἂν, alioqui, alioqui si, nam si. ιλιάδ & α. ἢ δὲ ἂν ἀτρεί∂ν νῦν ὕςατα λωβήσαιτο, Nam alioqui nunc ultimum improbo tibi ef- se contigisset. Chrysostomus ꝛ.de Fato, ἢ δὲ ἂν ὑποπλύσαντες αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐχθρὸν, ἔφυγον, Nam si existimassent, uel alioqui si existimassent ipsum esse hostem, fugis sent.
units.tr: ἦ οὐ ποτε [ἢ οὔ ποτε], whether ever? ἦ δὲ [ἢ δὲ], is it not? for which they sometimes say ἦ οὔ. ἦ δὲ ἄν [ἢ δὲ ἄν], otherwise, otherwise if, for if. Iliad, ἦ δὲ ἄν ... νῦν ὕστατα λωβήσαιτο, for otherwise he would now have dishonoured you to the last degree. Chrysostom, in his work on Fate: ἦ δὲ ἄν ... ἔφυγον, for if they had thought him an enemy, or otherwise if they had thought it, they would have fled.

units.la: ἢ μλω̃ ñ μλω, uerè, apponitur feré iurijuran-do, νὴ δία ñ μλω ἐγὼ ἐπαῤῥόν τι τοιᾶτον, Ve-rè per Iouem tale quippiam ego passus sum.
units.tr: ἦ μὴν [ἤ μὴν], truly, is put almost always with an oath: νὴ Δία ἦ μὴν ἐγὼ ἐπαθόν τι τοιοῦτον, truly, by Jove, I suffered something of the kind.

units.la: Conuenít etiam post interrogationẽ & exclamationem, ὦ Ζεῦ, ñ μλω καλὸς φαίνη οὗτος, ô Iupiter, uere formosus hic apparuit.
units.tr: It also fits after a question and an exclamation: ὦ Ζεῦ, ἦ μὴν καλὸς φαίνῃ οὗτος, O Jupiter, truly this man appears handsome.

units.la: Addítur etiam sponsionibus & promissionibus, ñ μλω ποιήσω, certè faciam.
units.tr: It is also added to promises and pledges: ἦ μὴν ποιήσω, I will certainly do it.

units.la: ΓΕ.
units.tr: ΓΕ.

units.la: Γε omnibus fermè iungitur coniunc-tionibus, ἀλλὰ μλω γε, νὴ μλω γε, & sic de aliís.
units.tr: γε is joined to almost all conjunctions: ἀλλὰ μὴν γε, νὴ μὴν γε, and so on with others.

units.la: ΔΗ.
units.tr: ΔΗ.

units.la: Δὴ etiam aliís subiungitur, καὶ δὴ, continuo, protinus, hoc est ideo. ἀλλὰ δὴ, at enim. οὐδὲ δὴ, nec uero. φέρε δὴ, age uero, ἔστω ἐν δὴ, esto uero. ἰδὴ δὴ, id est, ἰδὴ ὃς δὴ, pro ὅς. οἵῳ δὴ, pro οἵῳ. τί δὴ, Quid tandem? Pro quo etiam dicunt τί μλω, ποῖον δὴ, quale tandem. δὲ δὴ, porrò. δὴ που, utique, nimirum, profecto, οὐδὲ-που, nunquid? ἦπου ἂν, utique, nimi-rum, ὅπου δὴ, id est, ubi cunque. ὁ ἁλήποτε, ὅτι ἁλήποτε, ἃ ἁλήποτε, quíduis. ὁπωσᾶ ήποτε, ὁπωσοῦν, ὁπωσᾶλη- ποτῶν, ὁπηνῆ ήποτε, quouis modo, quomo docunque. ποσοσᾶ ήποτε, quot tandem.
units.tr: δὴ is also added to other words: καὶ δὴ, immediately, straightaway, that is, for this reason. ἀλλὰ δὴ, but indeed. οὐδὲ δὴ, nor indeed. φέρε δὴ, come now. ἔστω ἐν δὴ, let it be so indeed. ἰδὴ δὴ, that is, ἰδὴ ὃς δὴ, for ὅς. οἵῳ δὴ, for οἵῳ. τί δὴ, what then? For which they also say τί μὴν, ποῖον δὴ, of what sort then. δὲ δὴ, moreover. δὴ που, surely, no doubt, certainly; οὐδὲ-που, surely not? ἦπου ἄν, surely, no doubt; ὅπου δὴ, that is, wherever. ὁ ἁλήποτε, ὅτι ἁλήποτε, ἅ ἁλήποτε, whatever. ὁπωσᾶ ποτε, ὁπωσοῦν, ὁπωσαλη ποτῶν, ὁπηνῆ ποτε, in whatever way, howsoever. ποσοσᾶ ποτε, how many ever.

units.la: MHN.
units.tr: MHN.

units.la: Τί μὲν, quid nam. Aliquando etiam concedentis est, pro, quid ni? γε μὲν, uero. ναὶ μὲν, atqui. ὅμως μὲν, tamen.
units.tr: τί μέν, what then? Sometimes it is also of concession, meaning why not? γε μέν, indeed. ναὶ μέν, yes, but. ὅμως μέν, nevertheless.

units.la: ΠΟΥ.
units.tr: ΠΟΥ.

units.la: Πο, interdum conuenit interrogatio- ni, ut ἡ ζῶων ἐστι, τὸ μὴ π λογικὸν τό ἀλλ μὴ; Est animalium aliud quidem homo, aliud uero non?
units.tr: που sometimes goes with a question, as: ἦ ζῴων ἐστι, τὸ μὲν λογικὸν, τὸ δὲ ἄλογον; Is one of the animals man, and another not?

units.la: Est etiam nonnunquam in oratione ociosum, quemadmodū ἀ ἢ δὲ γε, δὲ τοι, et μὲν δὲ αὖ, δὲ postponitur, ut in his, μὴ ου, γέπου, ἢ ἢ του, ἔπω που, τάχα του, ὡς τε, ἀ ἢ πε, ἀ ἢ του, ἀλήπτεθεν, ἢ πε, ἢ τε, ὃ πε, ἀχει πε, μέχει πε.
units.tr: It is also sometimes superfluous in a sentence, as ἀ ἢ δὲ γε, δὲ τοι, and μὲν δὲ αὖ; δὲ is placed after, as in these: μὴ ου, γέ που, ἢ ἢ του, ἔπω που, τάχα του, ὡς τε, ἀ ἢ πε, ἀ ἢ του, ἀλήπτεθεν, ἢ πε, ἢ τε, ὃ πε, ἀχει πε, μέχει πε.

units.la: TOI.
units.tr: TOI.

units.la: Τοι cum multis constuitur dictioni- bus, οὕτω τοι, φαίνυτοι, γέτοι, ἀλέτοι, δὲ ita in aliis, ornatus tantum gratia, & expletamenti orationis. In τιγάρτοι, etiam gemi- natur.
units.tr: Τοι is joined to many words, as in οὕτω τοι, φαίνυτοι, γέτοι, ἀλέτοι, and similarly in others, merely for ornament and to fill out the sentence. In τιγάρτοι it is also doubled. [οὕτω τοι, φαίνυτοι, γέτοι, ἀλέτοι, τιγάρτοι]

units.la: Interponitur etiam sine compositio=ne, διὰ τοι τῶ͂ς, eam ob rem.
units.tr: It is also inserted without composition, as in διὰ τοι τῶ͂ς, that is, for that reason. [διὰ τοι τῶ͂ς]

units.la: Τοίνυν, quando præponitur coniun-ctioni ἀν̓, ualet at, atqui, ut ὑμῖν τοίνυν ἀλλ' ἀν̓ ἔις, Atqui nullus est omnino ue-strum.
units.tr: Τοίνυν, when placed before the conjunction ἀλλ' ἀν̓, has the force of "at," "but indeed": ὑμῖν τοίνυν ἀλλ' ἀν̓ ἔις, "But certainly none of you is at all..." [Τοίνυν, ὑμῖν τοίνυν ἀλλ' ἀν̓ ἔις]

units.la: In assumptionibus etiam, ut ἀλλὰ μὴν, ponitur, ἐ τοίνυν παρὰ ληφθὲν ἀδεῖς, At ne-mo tum prodit.
units.tr: It is also placed in minor premises, as in ἀλλὰ μὴν: ἐ τοίνυν παρὰ ληφθὲν ἀδεῖς, "But then no one comes forward." [ἀλλὰ μὴν, ἐ τοίνυν παρὰ ληφθὲν ἀδεῖς]

units.la: Significat etiā proinde συλλογιστικῶς. ἐὰν μὲν τοίνυν τῶν ἄρτι ως ἐποεισάμεθα, ὥ-στε δοκεῖν τι λέγειν, Proinde unum hoc inuenimus, ut aliquid dicere uideamur.
units.tr: It also signifies "accordingly," in the manner of a syllogism: ἐὰν μὲν τοίνυν τῶν ἄρτι ως ἐποεισάμεθα, ὥστε δοκεῖν τι λέγειν, "Accordingly we find only this one thing, that we seem to be saying something." [ἐὰν μὲν τοίνυν τῶν ἄρτι ως ἐποεισάμεθα, ὥστε δοκεῖν τι λέγειν]

units.la: Aliquando significat igitur, ἄκουε τοίνυν, ὡς ἔχει τάμα, Audi igitur, ut sese habent res meæ.
units.tr: Sometimes it means "therefore": ἄκουε τοίνυν, ὡς ἔχει τάμα, "Hear then, as my affairs stand." [ἄκουε τοίνυν, ὡς ἔχει τάμα]

units.la: Ponitur etiam pro μήτοι. ἐντεῦθα τοίνυν πάντες προσεβλέψαν αὐτῷ, Hic quidem omnes intuebantur eum.
units.tr: It is also used for μήτοι: ἐντεῦθα τοίνυν πάντες προσεβλέψαν αὐτῷ, "Here indeed all looked at him." [ἐντεῦθα τοίνυν πάντες προσεβλέψαν αὐτῷ]

units.la: Est etiam nonnunquam expletiuum. μνδαμῶς τοίνυν εἴπης, Tu uero ne dicas, ἐπὶ τοίνυν, iam uero, atque etiam, ἠτοίνυν, neque uero.
units.tr: Sometimes it is expletive: μνδαμῶς τοίνυν εἴπης, "Do not say so by any means." Also ἐπὶ τοίνυν, "indeed now, and furthermore"; ἠτοίνυν, "nor indeed." [μνδαμῶς τοίνυν εἴπης, ἐπὶ τοίνυν, ἠτοίνυν]

units.la: Et ponitur pro ἀλλὰ μλὼ, ὅτι τοίνυν, quod uero, quod autem, itaque quod.
units.tr: It is also put for ἀλλὰ μλὼ, and ὅτι τοίνυν: "but indeed," "but in fact," "and therefore since." [ἀλλὰ μλὼ, ὅτι τοίνυν]

units.la: AN.
units.tr: AN.

units.la: ἂν construitur Græcis & Δυωντικῶς hoc est, ut denotet potentiam, & ἀορίστως λογικῶς, hoc est, infinite. Δυωντικῶς quidem, ut εἰ καὶ μὴ ἐποίησε, ἀλλ' ἐποίησεν ἄν, Et si non fecit, fecisse tamen credi posset.
units.tr: ἂν is construed by the Greeks both Δυωντικῶς, that is, so as to denote potentiality, and ἀορίστως λογικῶς, that is, indefinitely. Δυωντικῶς, for example: εἰ καὶ μὴ ἐποίησε, ἀλλ' ἐποίησεν ἄν, "Even if he did not do it, yet it could be believed that he had done it." [εἰ καὶ μὴ ἐποίησε, ἀλλ' ἐποίησεν ἄν]

units.la: Et habet quandoque uim uerbi taciti ac subaudiendi. Τοσαύτην ἐποίησαν τῶ ἄλλω, ὅσῳ ἂν τῆς ἑαυτῶν χώρας τοπον μέγης, Tam enixe contenderunt, quàm facere potuissent, si suum agrum populantes uidissent.
units.tr: It also sometimes has the force of a tacit and understood verb: Τοσαύτην ἐποίησαν τῶ ἄλλω, ὅσῳ ἂν τῆς ἑαυτῶν χώρας τοπον μέγης, "They strove as eagerly as they could have done, had they seen their own land being laid waste." [Τοσαύτην ἐποίησαν τῶ ἄλλω, ὅσῳ ἂν τῆς ἑαυτῶν χώρας τοπον μέγης]

units.la: Adfert enim particula hæc compendium in oratione, ut δόξαν μὲν ἐγὼ γ' ἂν συγχωρήσω, τάδ' ἕτερα τῶν τε ἂν: ibi ἂν ponitur, pro non etiam, uel non itidem concederem. Iungitur Δυωντικῶς omnibus temporibus.
units.tr: For this particle brings brevity into speech, as in δόξαν μὲν ἐγὼ γ' ἂν συγχωρήσω, τάδ' ἕτερα τῶν τε ἂν: there ἂν is put for "not even," or "I would not likewise concede." It is joined in the Δυωντικῶς sense with all tenses. [δόξαν μὲν ἐγὼ γ' ἂν συγχωρήσω, τάδ' ἕτερα τῶν τε ἂν]

units.la: ἂν cum præsenti.
units.tr: ἂν with the present. [ἂν cum præsenti]

units.la: Præsenti quidem in Optatiuo, ἂν ἂν λέγοις, ἂν ἂν φαίης, Non diceres. σὺ δ' ἂν ἐκεῖνον θεωρῶνς, Tu finieres illum.
units.tr: With the present in the optative: ἂν ἂν λέγοις, ἂν ἂν φαίης, "you would not say." σὺ δ' ἂν ἐκεῖνον θεωρῶνς, "You would finish him off." [ἂν ἂν λέγοις, ἂν ἂν φαίης, σὺ δ' ἂν ἐκεῖνον θεωρῶνς]

units.la: Et in Coniunctiuo. Plato in Phædro, καλὸν γε ἂν εἴδ' ἡ καταγνῶ νοῦ ... βῶν. βών, Atqui bellam speciem is intellectu perciperet, qui hoc assequi posset, uel intellectu perceperit, qui hoc assequutus fuerit.
units.tr: And in the subjunctive. Plato in the Phaedrus: καλὸν γε ἂν εἴδ' ἡ καταγνῶ νοῦ ... βῶν. βών, "Indeed, one who could attain this would perceive a fine beauty by the intellect, or one who had attained it would have perceived it by the intellect." [καλὸν γε ἂν εἴδ' ἡ καταγνῶ νοῦ ... βῶν. βών]

units.la: Et Infinitiuo, τί ποιεῖν ἄν, ἢ τί οἴκοι λέγειν. Quid dicturos fuisse existimatis, aut quid facturos.
units.tr: And with the infinitive: τί ποιεῖν ἄν, ἢ τί οἴκοι λέγειν. "What do you think they would have said or done?" [τί ποιεῖν ἄν, ἢ τί οἴκοι λέγειν]

units.la: ἄν cum praeterito.
units.tr: ἄν with the past tense.

units.la: Praeterito uero in Indicatiuo, quum de re praeterita loquuntur, τίς ἕτως ἄγριος, ὅστις ἂν ἐδύνατο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν; Quis tam inmitis, qui posset hoc facere?
units.tr: With the past tense in the indicative, when they speak of a past matter: τίς ἕτως ἄγριος, ὅστις ἂν ἐδύνατο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν; "Who is so savage as to have been able to do this?" [τίς ἕτως ἄγριος, ὅστις ἂν ἐδύνατο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν]

units.la: Potest hoc & per Optatiuum enuntiari, sed ita ut loqui uideamur in re praesenti, ὅστις ἂν δύναιτο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν, Qui tamen posset hoc facere.
units.tr: This may also be expressed by the optative, but in such a way that we seem to speak of a present matter: ὅστις ἂν δύναιτο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν, "who yet could do this." [ὅστις ἂν δύναιτο ἄν τοῦτο ποιεῖν]

units.la: Et inuenitur hoc pacto iunctum praeteritis omnibus, etiam perfectis, & pluSquamperfectis. Perfecto, ut Demosth. πειράσομαι τὸν ξόπον εἰπεῖν, ὃν ἂν μοι δοκεῖ τε μάλιστα παρεσκευάσθαι, Conabor eo modo dicere, quo mihi uidemini, &c. Plusquamperfecto, ὅτι μὲν δεῖ τὰ γράμματα ἐπίστασθαι ἀκηκοέναι, ἄν, Quod quidem oportet scire literas, &c.
units.tr: It is found joined in this way to all past tenses, even the perfect and pluperfect. With the perfect, as in Demosthenes: πειράσομαι τὸν ξόπον εἰπεῖν, ὃν ἂν μοι δοκεῖ τε μάλιστα παρεσκευάσθαι, "I shall try to speak in the manner in which you seem to me to have been most prepared," etc. With the pluperfect: ὅτι μὲν δεῖ τὰ γράμματα ἐπίστασθαι ἀκηκοέναι, ἄν, "That indeed one ought to have known letters, etc." [πειράσομαι τὸν ξόπον εἰπεῖν, ὃν ἂν μοι δοκεῖ τε μάλιστα παρεσκευάσθαι, ὅτι μὲν δεῖ τὰ γράμματα ἐπίστασθαι ἀκηκοέναι, ἄν]

units.la: Per præteritum item sæpe loquuntur de futuro, addita particula ἂν, tam in uerbis quàm in participijs, ut ποιήσειαν ἂν, pro ποιήσεσθαι. λεχθέντων ἂν, pro λεχθὲν ... ἂν ὑποσχὰς, pro ὑποσχησόμενος. ἡγοῦ ... μὲν ἄν, pro ἡγησόμενον.
units.tr: Likewise, by the past tense they often speak of the future, with the particle ἂν added, both in verbs and in participles: ποιήσειαν ἂν, for ποιήσεσθαι; λεχθέντων ἂν, for λεχθὲν ... ἂν ὑποσχὰς, for ὑποσχησόμενος; ἡγοῦ ... μὲν ἄν, for ἡγησόμενον. [ποιήσειαν ἂν, ποιήσεσθαι, λεχθέντων ἂν, λεχθὲν ... ἂν ὑποσχὰς, ὑποσχησόμενος, ἡγοῦ ... μὲν ἄν, ἡγησόμενον]

units.la: ἂν cum futuro.
units.tr: ἂν with the future. [ἂν cum futuro]

units.la: Futuris item additur in Optatiuo, ἂν ἀν λέξοις.
units.tr: It is also added to futures in the optative: ἂν ἀν λέξοις. [ἂν ἀν λέξοις]

units.la: Insuper indicatiuo & infinitiuo, licet id sit rarius, ἐλπίζω ὅπως ἂν ἀεισα τυχεῖν puto me hoc pacto optime facturum.
units.tr: Moreover with the indicative and infinitive, although this is rarer: ἐλπίζω ὅπως ἂν ἀεισα τυχεῖν, "I think I shall do best in this way." [ἐλπίζω ὅπως ἂν ἀεισα τυχεῖν]

units.la: Id fit plerunque in uerbis quæ futu-rum poscunt, ut νομίζω, οἶμαι, ἐλπίζω, ἡγοῦμαι, φημί, ὑπόσχομαι, & similibus: licet etiā sine his uerbis inueniatur additū futuro apud authores, ut est illud Isocra-tis in Areop. ἡμεῖς γὰρ, ἢν μὲν ὅπως οἰκῶμεν τὴν πόλιν, ὥσπερ νῦν οἰκοῦμεν, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἂν βουλευσόμεθα, καὶ πολεμήσομεν, &c. nos si inhabitaremus ciuitatem, quem-admodum nunc inhabitamus, quouis modo consulturi essemus & bellaturi. Itaque quod Latini per Coniunctiuum per se positum, hoc Græci etiam per a-lios lios modos efferunt, addita Coniunctio ne αἲ, ut ἀπολαξαίμεν αἲ, uel εἰ λίδ αξα αἲ, εἰ ἐβουλήθης, Docuissem si discere uoluisses.
units.tr: This happens for the most part with verbs that require a future, such as νομίζω, οἶμαι, ἐλπίζω, ἡγοῦμαι, φημί, ὑπόσχομαι, and similar ones; although it is also found in authors with a future added without these verbs, as in that passage of Isocrates in the Areopagiticus: ἡμεῖς γὰρ, ἢν μὲν ὅπως οἰκῶμεν τὴν πόλιν, ὥσπερ νῦν οἰκοῦμεν, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἂν βουλευσόμεθα, καὶ πολεμήσομεν, etc. "For if we were to inhabit the city as we now inhabit it, there is no way in which we would not be about to deliberate and to make war," etc. Therefore, as the Latins express by the subjunctive alone, so the Greeks also express by other moods, with the conjunction εἰ added, as in ἀπολαξαίμεν αἲ, or εἰ λίδ αξα αἲ, εἰ ἐβουλήθης, "I would have taught you, if you had wished to learn." [ἡμεῖς γὰρ, ἢν μὲν ὅπως οἰκῶμεν τὴν πόλιν, ὥσπερ νῦν οἰκοῦμεν, ἀπολαξαίμεν αἲ, εἰ λίδ αξα αἲ, εἰ ἐβουλήθης]

units.la: Item quod Latini exprimunt per im perfectum coniunctiuum, dum de rebus transacto tempore promissis, uel cogitatis loquuntur, hoc Graeci per praesens, uel futurū loquuntur· τί φθέξοι αἲ ἐννοεῖν ἤρξατο, Quid ageret cogitare coepit. ἐλέξε μέλλοντας, οἱ ποιήσοιεν αἲ ὀρθῶς dixit futuros, qui recte facerent. τί αἲ λέγοι τὸ ἂν οἶδεν, Non nouit, quid diceret.
units.tr: Likewise, what the Latins express by the imperfect subjunctive, when they speak of things promised or thought of in past time, the Greeks express by the present or future: τί φθέξοι αἲ ἐννοεῖν ἤρξατο, "He began to think what he would say." ἐλέξε μέλλοντας, οἱ ποιήσοιεν αἲ ὀρθῶς, "He said that those who would act rightly were about to be..." τί αἲ λέγοι τὸ ἂν οἶδεν, "He did not know what he would say." [τί φθέξοι αἲ ἐννοεῖν ἤρξατο, ἐλέξε μέλλοντας, οἱ ποιήσοιεν αἲ ὀρθῶς, τί αἲ λέγοι τὸ ἂν οἶδεν]

units.la: Et modo praecedit, modo sequitur uerbum ad quod refertur. ὅστις αἲ ταῦτα ἔχοι λέγειν, uel ὅστις ταῦτ' ἔχοι αἲ λέγδν, Quicunque haec possit dicere.
units.tr: And it sometimes precedes, sometimes follows, the verb to which it refers: ὅστις αἲ ταῦτα ἔχοι λέγειν, or ὅστις ταῦτ' ἔχοι αἲ λέγδν, "whoever could say these things." [ὅστις αἲ ταῦτα ἔχοι λέγειν, ὅστις ταῦτ' ἔχοι αἲ λέγδν]

units.la: Construitur etiam cum particula ὁ interrogatiue, σὺ ὁ αἲ ἐκεῖνον φθεροφῆς; Sineres tu illum?
units.tr: It is also construed with the interrogative particle ὁ: σὺ ὁ αἲ ἐκεῖνον φθεροφῆς; "Would you have let him?" [σὺ ὁ αἲ ἐκεῖνον φθεροφῆς]

units.la: Cum autem sine ὁ ponitur non habet eandem uehementiam, ut τί ποιεῖν αἲ οἴεσθε; Quid facturos fuisse existimatis? ὅπως & ὡς.
units.tr: But when it is put without ὁ it does not have the same force, as in τί ποιεῖν αἲ οἴεσθε; "What do you think they would have done?" ὅπως & ὡς. [τί ποιεῖν αἲ οἴεσθε]

units.la: Construitur etiam cum ὅπως, & cum ὅταν ὡς, & tum Optatiuo, Subiunctiuoque convenit. ἀγωνίζομεν, ὅπως ἂν τῶ νίκῃ ἀποβάλωμεν, Certamus, ut victoria præripia mus. μόνον ἀπεδιδάζω, ὅπως ἂν χαρισθῶμέν σοι, Solum studeo quonam pacto gratifi carer tibi. διδάξω, ὡς ἂν τῆς σοφίας βάθος μὴ ἀγνοῇς, Docebo, ut sapientiæ profun ditatem non ignores. διηγήσομαι, ὡς ἂν τὸ ἁλῶς ἡγοῖτο, Narrabo quonam pacto hoc bene fieret.
units.tr: It is also construed with ὅπως, and with ὅταν, ὡς, and then agrees with the optative and subjunctive. ἀγωνίζομεν, ὅπως ἂν τῶ νίκῃ ἀποβάλωμεν, "We strive that we may snatch away victory." μόνον ἀπεδιδάζω, ὅπως ἂν χαρισθῶμέν σοι, "I study only how we might be pleasing to you." διδάξω, ὡς ἂν τῆς σοφίας βάθος μὴ ἀγνοῇς, "I shall teach you, so that you may not be ignorant of the depth of wisdom." διηγήσομαι, ὡς ἂν τὸ ἁλῶς ἡγοῖτο, "I shall narrate how this might well be done." [ἀγωνίζομεν, ὅπως ἂν τῶ νίκῃ ἀποβάλωμεν, μόνον ἀπεδιδάζω, ὅπως ἂν χαρισθῶμέν σοι, διδάξω, ὡς ἂν τῆς σοφίας βάθος μὴ ἀγνοῇς, διηγήσομαι, ὡς ἂν τὸ ἁλῶς ἡγοῖτο]

units.la: AN ΑΟΡΙΣΤΟΛΟΓΙΚΩΣ.
units.tr: On ἂν used indefinitely [ἀοριστολογικῶς]

units.la: ἂν indefinite acceptum plerunque Subiunctiuo construitur, ὅ, τὶ ἂν λέγῃς, quodcunque dicas. ὅσῳ ἂν διαφέρῃς, quan tocunque differas. ὁποδαπός ἂν ἢ, cuiafcunq; sit. ὁπότερος ἂν ἢ, uterlibet sit. ὅπῃ ἂν ἔλθῃ, quacunq; eat.
units.tr: ἂν, used indefinitely, is for the most part construed with the Subjunctive: whatever you say [ὅ, τι ἂν λέγῃς]; however much you differ [ὅσῳ ἂν διαφέρῃς]; of whatever sort he may be [ὁποδαπός ἂν ἢ]; whichever he may be [ὁπότερος ἂν ἢ]; whichever way he goes [ὅπῃ ἂν ἔλθῃ].

units.la: Interdum cum Optatiuo, sed tum demum cum res præterita narratur, νῦν ἂν εἴπεῖν τι κατὰ τούτων δέοι, cum oportet, uel cum oportebat dicere quippiam aduerfus hæc, ἀν & ἴαν, pro ἐὰν acceptæ, inueniuntur etiam cum Optatiuo, ὡς ἂν, siue ὡς ἂν ἀφέτεος τις εἴποι, Quasi uero si quis prior dixisset.
units.tr: Sometimes it is also construed with the Optative, but only when a past event is being narrated: when it was necessary, or when it was necessary to say something against these things [νῦν ἂν εἴπεῖν τι κατὰ τούτων δέοι]. Also ἀν and ἴαν, taken for ἐάν, are found with the Optative, as in ὡς ἂν, or ὡς ἂν ἀφέτεος τις εἴποι: as if someone had said earlier.

units.la: Appendix.
units.tr: Appendix.

units.la: Av potentialiter acceptum, siue indefinite saepe deest in oratione. Demosth. οὐδείς ποτε ἀνθρώπων εὕρεγι τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ ἁδλυ ἀλλειφθεὶν, pro εὕρεγι ἂν, Nemo unquam hominum inuenire posset delictum aliquod in me.
units.tr: ἂν, used potentially or indefinitely, is often left out in speech. Demosthenes: No one of men could ever find any fault in me [οὐδείς ποτε ἀνθρώπων εὕρεγι τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ ἁδλυ ἀλλειφθεὶν], for εὕρεγι ἂν.

units.la: Saepe item abundat. Aristophanes in Pluto, ἡ τοι γ᾽ ἂν ἔχοι τις ἂν ἀλίκμον ἀντεῖ-πεῖν ἐπ, Quod iustum posset quispiam adhuc contradicere. In quo loco abundat alterum ἂν.
units.tr: It is also often superfluous. Aristophanes in the Plutus: "Which just anyone could still contradict" [ἡ τοι γ᾽ ἂν ἔχοι τις ἂν ἀλίκμον ἀντεῖ-πεῖν ἐπ]. In this passage the second ἂν is superfluous.

units.la: Ponuntur enim Graecis tum caeterae orationis partes, ut dictum est, tum praecipue coniunctiones, sic ut orationi adferant nonnunquam ornamenti aliquid, sed nihil sententiae, quod potissimum fit in coniunctionibus expletiuis, & in ijs quae hic sequuntur.
units.tr: For, as has been said, the Greeks use other parts of speech, but especially conjunctions, in such a way that they sometimes add some ornament to the sentence but nothing to its meaning. This happens chiefly with the expletive conjunctions, and with those that follow here.

units.la: ΟΥΝ.
units.tr: Oun [οὖν]

units.la: Οὖν, ut ὅπερ ἂν ἐποίησεν, pro ὅπερ ἐποίη-σεν, quod fecit. ὥσπερ ἂν ᾔ ἔχει, pro ὥσπερ καὶ ἔχει, Quemadmodum se habet, ὡς ἄν, pro ὡς.
units.tr: οὖν, as in ὅπερ ἂν ἐποίησεν for ὅπερ ἐποίησεν: what he did. ὥσπερ ἂν ᾗ ἔχει for ὥσπερ καὶ ἔχει: just as it stands. ὡς ἄν for ὡς: as.

units.la: Ὢν ἰωνικῶς.
units.tr: ὢν in the Ionic manner.

units.la: ὤν non modo abundat, sed etiam inter praepositionem & uerbum compositum interponitur, ἀπ' ὧν ἔδοντο, pro ἀπέ ἔδοντο, reddebant. ἐξ ὧν εἶλον, pro ἐξεῖλον. ἀπ' ὧν ἐβαλεν. pro ἀπέβαλεν. κατ' ὧν ἐκάλυ ψε, pro κατεκάλυψε.
units.tr: ὤν is not only superfluous but is also inserted between a preposition and a compound verb: ἀπ' ὧν ἔδοντο for ἀπέδοντο: they gave back. ἐξ ὧν εἶλον for ἐξεῖλον: they took out. ἀπ' ὧν ἐβαλεν for ἀπέβαλεν: he threw away. κατ' ὧν ἐκάλυψε for κατεκάλυψε: he covered over.

units.la: TE.
units.tr: Te [τε]

units.la: Τε, ut ἐφ' ὣτι, pro ἐφ' ὧ.
units.tr: τε, as in ἐφ' ὣτι for ἐφ' ᾧ: wherefore.

units.la: KAI.
units.tr: Kai [καί]

units.la: Καὶ, ut καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς ὁ λόγος & ἀληθής ἐστιν, Etenim sermo ipse uerus est.
units.tr: καί, as in For the saying itself is true [καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς ὁ λόγος ἀληθής ἐστιν].

units.la: ATTA.
units.tr: Atta [ἄττα]

units.la: ἄτλα, ut ποῖ ἄτλα, ἕτερ ἄτλα, ut supra dictum est.
units.tr: ἄττα, as in ποῖ ἄττα, ἕτερ' ἄττα, as said above.

units.la: OTI.
units.tr: Oti [ὅτι]

units.la: ὅτι, ut Ioan. 1. ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ χριστός, Confessus est, non sum ego Christus. Nam nisi abundaret ὅτι, sensus esset Baptistam esse confessum, Euangelistā nō esse Christū. Et cap. 4. καλῶς εἶπας ὅτι ἀνδρα οὐκ ἔχω, Bene dixisti, uirū nō habeo. Quo etiam in loco si ὅτι non abundaret, nihil significaret aliud, quàm recte dixisse Samaritanam, quod Christus uirum
units.tr: ὅτι, as in John 1: "He confessed, I am not the Christ" [ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ χριστός]. For unless ὅτι were superfluous, the sense would be that the Baptist confessed that the Evangelist was not Christ. And in chapter 4: "Well have you said, I have no husband" [καλῶς εἶπας ὅτι ἀνδρα οὐκ ἔχω]. In this place too, if ὅτι were not superfluous, it would mean nothing other than that the Samaritan woman spoke rightly in saying that Christ, that is, that she, had no husband at that time.

units.la: rum tum non haberet. Item Marci 13. λέγον∙ τες ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμί, dicentes ego sum. Quo in loco si nō abundaret ὅτι, sensus esset, Ve turos qui dicerent Christum esse Chri- stum. Rursus Apocal. 3. λέγεις ὅτι πλουσι ὸς εἰμί, Ego sum dives: cum alioqui esset sensus, Tu dicis me esse diuitem.
units.tr: Likewise in Mark 13: "saying, I am he" [λέγοντες ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμί]. In this place, if ὅτι were not superfluous, the sense would be that those who were to come would say that Christ is Christ. Again, in Revelation 3: "You say, I am rich" [λέγεις ὅτι πλούσιος εἰμί]; whereas otherwise the sense would be, "You say that I am rich."

units.la: Ω Σ.
units.tr: Hos [ὡς]

units.la: ὡς pro ὅτι, ut λέγεις ὡς καλὸς εἰμί, Dicis ego sum formosus.
units.tr: ὡς for ὅτι, as in "You say that I am handsome" [λέγεις ὡς καλὸς εἰμί].

units.la: Neque solum abundant Græcis oratio ni partes, sed nonnunquam totæ oratio nes, veluti εὖ οἶδ' ὅτι, ut ἀπαῦλ✓, ὡς πᾶσι, εὖ οἶδ' ὅτι, ἐν γραφαῖς ἀπλόν δεῖ, τὸν ἕτερον ἐπετίμησε, Paulus (ut omnibus per scri- pturas manifestum est) Petrum increpauit.
units.tr: Not only are parts of a sentence superfluous in Greek, but sometimes whole clauses are, as in "I know well that" [εὖ οἶδ' ὅτι], "as to all" [ὡς πᾶσι], "I know well that" [εὖ οἶδ' ὅτι], "in the Scriptures" [ἐν γραφαῖς], "one rebuked the other" [τὸν ἕτερον ἐπετίμησε]. Paul (as is clear to everyone from the Scriptures) rebuked Peter.

units.la: ΕΤ ΙΣΘΙ.
units.tr: Eu isthi [εὖ ἴσθι]

units.la: Abundat etiam interdum εὖ ἴσθι, quod Græcis usui est eo loco, quo Latinis, mi hi crede, ut ἀδελφὲ, εὖ ἴσθι, τῶν ἀνόμων σωθήσεται, Nemo, mihi crede, iniquorum serua- bitur.
units.tr: εὖ ἴσθι is also sometimes superfluous, and in Greek it serves in the place where Latin uses "believe me." For example: "Brother, believe me, none of the lawless will be saved" [ἀδελφὲ, εὖ ἴσθι, τῶν ἀνόμων σωθήσεται].

units.la: FINIS CONSTRV- CTIONIS.
units.tr: End of the Construction.

units.la: DE ACCENTIBVS ET OBITER DE QVANTITATE uocalium, a, i, v. CAPVT IX.
units.tr: On accents, and incidentally on the quantity of the vowels a, i, u. Chapter 9.

units.la: Rectus declinationis primæ.
units.tr: Of the nominative of the first declension.

units.la: NOMINATIVVS primæ declinationis accentum habet in penultima, & a semper producitur, αἰνείας, χεύσης. Exceptis in της uerbalibus a uerbis cōtractis, quæ ultimam acuunt, ποιητής, μιμητής. Item quibusdam a uerbis incontractis, κριτής, δικαστής. In ας autem circunflexa Dorica sunt, κοσμᾶς.
units.tr: The nominative of the first declension has the accent on the penult, and the a is always long: aineias, cheusēs [αἰνείας, χεύσης]. Excepted are the verbal nouns in -της from contracted verbs, which accent the last syllable: poiētēs, mimētēs [ποιητής, μιμητής]. Likewise some from uncontracted verbs: kritēs, dikastēs [κριτής, δικαστής]. Nouns in -ας with a circumflex are Doric: kosmās [κοσμᾶς].

units.la: Secundæ.
units.tr: Of the second declension.

units.la: In secunda declinatione a finalis recti nominum adiectiuorum, eius quantitatis est, cuius ultima syllaba genitiui sui masculini, ὁ θεῖος τῆς θείας, ἡ θεία. ὁ ἡμέρος τῆς ἡμέρας, ἡ ἡμέρα. ὁ ἡδὺς τῆς ἡδέος, ἡ ἡδεῖα. Præter ἡ δῖα ab ὁ δῖος τῆς δῖος. Item a nominum a uerbis in δέω producitur, προσβεία a προσβάλλω.
units.tr: In the second declension, the final a of the nominative of adjectives has the same quantity as the last syllable of the genitive of the masculine: ho theios, tēs theias, hē theia [ὁ θεῖος τῆς θείας, ἡ θεία]; ho hēmeros, tēs hēmeras, hē hēmera [ὁ ἡμέρος τῆς ἡμέρας, ἡ ἡμέρα]; ho hēdys, tēs hēdeos, hē hēdeia [ὁ ἡδὺς τῆς ἡδέος, ἡ ἡδεῖα]. Except hē dia, from ho dios, tēs dios [ἡ δῖα, ὁ δῖος τῆς δῖος]. Also the a is long in nouns from verbs in -δέω: prosbeia, from prosballō [προσβεία, προσβάλλω].

units.la: Similiter in ες præcedente sola uoca lí, πήες, etiam σαίες αἵες. In ααα polisyl= laborum σελλωαία.
units.tr: Similarly in -ες, when only the vowel ι precedes: pēies, also saies, haies [πήες, σαίες, αἵες]. In polysyllables in -αια [σελλωαία] the same holds.

units.la: In ια, δια, θια, φιλοσοφία, λήσα, χιοσαίθα.
units.tr: In -ια, -δια, -θια: philosophia, lēsa, chiosaitha [φιλοσοφία, λήσα, χιοσαίθα].

units.la: In alijs semper corripitur, πεῖες γαῖα, ὁμόνοια, εὐγήνεια, θάλασσα, &c.
units.tr: In other cases it is always short: pheies, gaia, homonoia, eugēneia, thalassa, and so on [πεῖες, γαῖα, ὁμόνοια, εὐγήνεια, θάλασσα].

units.la: Nomina in ια, ιων, ον, frequentius pe nacuuntur, ποιλία, εὐφεγσιων, αρσιvón.
units.tr: Nouns in -ια, -ιων, -ον are more often found, as in poilia, eupheginōn, arsiphon [ποιλία, εὐφεγσιων, αρσιvón].

units.la: Penultimam longam nominatiui in α bissyllabi accentus plerunq; occupat, χώρα, μέσσα.
units.tr: The long penult of a disyllabic nominative in -α usually takes the accent: chōra, messa [χώρα, μέσσα].

units.la: In α correptam nomina plurifyllaba antepenultimam acuūt, ἀγγύλα, ὁμόνοια, ἐλέσσοιvα.
units.tr: Polysyllables with a short -α in the nominative accent the antepenult: angyla, homonoia, elessoina [ἀγγύλα, ὁμόνοια, ἐλέσσοιvα].

units.la: Tertiæ.
units.tr: Of the third declension.

units.la: Tertię declinationis possessiua in ος ultimam acuunt, λογικός, κήκόν. In ιος uel γ᾽ antepenacuuntur, ἑαυτός, ἑαυτίας, ἀ= ραύιον, λίθινος, λίθινη, λίθινον.
units.tr: Possessive adjectives of the third declension in -ος accent the last syllable: logikos, kēkon [λογικός, κήκόν]. Those in -ιος or -ινος accent the antepenult: heautos, heautias, araiion, lithinos, lithinē, lithinon [ἑαυτός, ἑαυτίας, ἀραύιον, λίθινος, λίθινη, λίθινον].

units.la: Antepenacuuntur properispomena Trochaica in compositione, ἀλλά, εὐ= ἁγλος. Etiam alia quædam ὥρα, ὥρα, μέγον ἐμμέζω.
units.tr: Trochaic properispomena are accented on the antepenult in compounds: alla, euhaglos [ἀλλά, εὐάγλος]. Certain others likewise: hōra, mégon, emmezō [ὥρα, μέγον, ἐμμέζω].

units.la: A mediis præteritis uerbi χτείνω uel ξέφω compositia, significationis quidem
units.tr: Of compounds of the middle past tenses of the verbs ktenō and xephō, with respect to meaning:

units.la: Passiuae sí passiuae antepenacuuntur, ξιφόντον·, gnificatio ense occisus, λαότεσφ· à populo nutri-tus. Actiuae uero penacuuntur, ξιφοντό v· gladio interficiens, λαοξόφ· nutri-tor populi.
units.tr: When passive, they accent the antepenult: xiphontos, killed by the sword; laotesphos, nourished by the people [ξιφόντος, λαότεσφος]. When active, they accent the penult: xiphonto, killing with the sword; laoxoos, nourisher of the people [ξιφοντό, λαοξόφ].

units.la: A πολῶ cum praepositione compositae antepenacuuntur, ᾱσεζπολ·, ἀμφίπο-λ·, cum alia parte orationis penacuun-tur, ὀνειεζπόλ· ξυνπόλ· Similiter reli-qua fere à praeteritis medijs composita, ἀσεζλόγ·, ἄλογ·, ἀνομ·, παμφάγος, δο-ρυφόρ·, δημοβόρ·.
units.tr: Compounds of pōlō with a preposition accent the antepenult: aselpolos, amphipolos [ᾱσεζπολ, ἀμφίπολ]. With another part of speech they accent the penult: oneipolos, xynpolos [ὀνειεζπόλ, ξυνπόλ]. Likewise most other compounds of middle past tenses: aselgos, alogos, anomos, pamphagos, dorypheros, demoboros [ἀσεζλόγ, ἄλογ, ἀνομ, παμφάγος, δορυφόρ, δημοβόρ].

units.la: Substantia neutra in ιον.
units.tr: Neuter substantives in -ιον.

units.la: Antepenacuuntur in ιον substantiua neutra, μυςήειον, ἱπωάειον, ὀπισόλιον, μό-ειον, ὀπινίκιον. In ειον uero penultimam circunflectunt, ἰχθυοφοφεῖον, μνημεῖον, βα-λανεῖον, κουρεῖον. Substantiua bissyllaba frequenter accentum habent in prima, λόγ·, ὦμ·, humerus. Adiectiua in ul-tima, ὠμός, crudus.
units.tr: Neuter substantives in -ιον accent the antepenult: mysēion, hippōaeion, opisolion, moeion, opinikion [μυςήειον, ἱπωάειον, ὀπισόλιον, μόειον, ὀπινίκιον]. In -ειον, however, they put a circumflex on the penult: ichthyophopheion, mnēmeion, balaneion, koureion [ἰχθυοφοφεῖον, μνημεῖον, βαλανεῖον, κουρεῖον]. Disyllabic substantives often have the accent on the first syllable: logos, ōmos, humerus [λόγ, ὦμ]. Adjectives have it on the last: ōmos, crudus, raw [ὠμός].

units.la: Bissyllaba interrogatiua primam ac-centuant, ποῖ·; qualis? πόσ·; quātus? Facto uero infinita, ultimam, ποιός, qua-lisçunq;, ποσός, quantuscunq;.
units.tr: Disyllabic interrogatives accent the first syllable: poi, of what sort? [ποῖ]; pos, how great? [πόσ]. When made indefinite, they accent the last: poios, qualiscunque [ποιός]; posos, quantuscunque [ποσός].

units.la: Verbalia in μῷ & τῷ.
units.tr: Verbals in -μος and -τος.

units.la: Verbalia in μῷ & τῷ acuūt ultima συλλογισμὸς, πλιγτὸς, ἀσφαρτὸς: quesi dictio ni, cui uerbū nō potest, cōponātur, accē tum traducunt, σελλωόπλητος, ἀσφαρτὸς.
units.tr: Verbals in -μός and -τός accent the last syllable: syllogismos, plēktos, asphartos [συλλογισμὸς, πλιγτὸς, ἀσφαρτὸς]. When a compound is made with a word that cannot be compounded with a verb, they move the accent back: selloopletos, asphartos [σελλωόπλητος, ἀσφαρτὸς].

units.la: Vltima uocali in nominibus per apo strophum abiecta, si supra se acutum ha-buerit ad præcedentem syllabā transfer tur, δ' ἐνα, δ' εἰν' ἔπη πέλᾳ. In aliis aūt dictio nibus cū uocali deciditur, κῷ, κατ' ἐμᾶ.
units.tr: A final vowel cut off in nouns by an apostrophe, if it had an acute accent, transfers the accent to the preceding syllable: d' ena, d' ein' epē pelā [δ' ἑνα, δ' εἰν' ἔπη πέλᾳ]. In other words, when a vowel is cut off, as in kō and kat' emā [κῷ, κατ' ἐμᾶ], the accent is not moved.

units.la: Quartæ.
units.tr: Of the fourth declension.

units.la: Quartæ declinationis acuūt rectū. No mina in αν & α producunt, παν, πᾶν. At πᾶν omne, suū masculinū sequitur πᾶς.
units.tr: Nouns of the fourth declension accent the nominative. Nouns in -αν and -α lengthen the vowel: pan, pān [παν, πᾶν]. But pān, "all", has the masculine pās [πᾶς].

units.la: Fœminina in as.
units.tr: Feminines in -as.

units.la: In as fœminina, & α corripiunt, λαμ- πᾶς, δέκας.
units.tr: Feminine nouns in -ας shorten the α: lampas, dekas [λαμπάς, δέκας].

units.la: In ais & aiξ.
units.tr: In -αις and -αιξ.

units.la: In ais & aiξ monosyllaba, ςαῖς, δαῖς αἴξ, sed πᾶῆς contractum est.
units.tr: Monosyllables in -αις and -αιξ: saïs, daïs, aix [ςαῖς, δαῖς, αἴξ]; but pāēs is contracted [πᾶῆς].

units.la: Adiectiua in ης.
units.tr: Adjectives in -ης.

units.la: In ης adiectiua flexa per ε, ἀληθής. Excipe quæ plenitudinem significat πλ-λώδης: etiam quædam composita ἀμή-νης, παμμεγέθης.
units.tr: Adjectives in -ης inflected through ε: alēthēs [ἀληθής]. Except those signifying fullness: pollōdēs [πλλώδης]; also some compounds: amēnēs, pammegethēs [ἀμήνης, παμμεγέθης].

units.la: A In ηρ.
units.tr: In -ηρ.

units.la: In ηρ, σωτήρ. præter μήτηρ, δημήτηρ, Ζυ-
units.tr: In -ηρ: sōtēr [σωτήρ]. Except mētēr, dēmētēr, and Zeu-

units.la: In υς adiectiua. (χάτηρ.
units.tr: In -υς adjectives (chatēr).

units.la: In υς adiectiua & υ corripiunt, ἡδύς. præter Ϡηλυς. In δς.
units.tr: In -υς adjectives, the υ is short: hēdys [ἡδύς]. Except thēlys [Ϡηλυς].

units.la: In δς, ἀχλλδς, πηλδς. Dorice ἀχίλ- λδς, πήλδς. In ων.
units.tr: In -ευς: achilleus, pēleus [ἀχιλλεύς, πηλεύς]. Doric: achillds, pēlds [ἀχίλλδς, πήλδς].

units.la: In ων comprehensiua, κοιτων, ἀγων, πε εισερεων, ἀπατεων. In ω & ως.
units.tr: In -ων.

units.la: In ω & ως fœminina, λιθω, αἰδως. Masculina in ας.
units.tr: Comprehensive nouns in -ων: koitōn, agōn, apatēōn [κοιτων, ἀγων, ἀπατεων].

units.la: In penultima accentu recipiunt masculina in ας, et α producunt, αἴας, ἄτλας; præter μέγας, λάας. In ξ.
units.tr: Feminines in -ω and -ως: lithō, aidōs [λιθω, αἰδως]. Masculines in -ας accept the accent on the penult and lengthen the α: aias, atlas [αἴας, ἄτλας]; except megas, laas [μέγας, λάας].

units.la: In ξ, ἀρπαξ, πέρδιξ; & masculina quidem ancipite ante ξ extendunt, fœminina uero corripiunt, ὁ θώραξ, φοίνιξ, κήρυξ, ἡ αὖλαξ In ης.
units.tr: In -ξ: harpax, perdix [ἀρπαξ, πέρδιξ]. Masculines lengthen the doubtful vowel before ξ, while feminines shorten it: ho thōrax, phoinix, kērykx, hē aulax [ὁ θώραξ, φοίνιξ, κήρυξ, ἡ αὖλαξ]. In -ης:

units.la: In ης propria copofita, ἀεισοτέλης, σω κεράτης. In της.
units.tr: In -ης, proper compounds: aeisotelēs, sōkeratēs [ἀεισοτέλης, σωκεράτης]. In -της:

units.la: In της fœminina abstracta, φιλότης; præpreter Κεφαλυτὴς, ἀσπορὴς, ταχυτὴς, δνιοῖὴς.
units.tr: In -της, feminine abstracts: philotēs [φιλότης]. Except kephalytēs, asporēs, tachytēs, dnioiēs.

units.la: In εις.
units.tr: In -εις.

units.la: In εις adiectiua, χαρίεις.
units.tr: Adjectives in -εις: charieis [χαρίεις].

units.la: In ων.
units.tr: In -ων.

units.la: In ων propria, adiectiua & getilia, πλάων. τῶν, ὁυδαίμων, τεύτων. At ποσειδῶν, ξενοφῶν contracta sunt ex ποσειδάων ξενοφάων.
units.tr: Proper, adjectival and gentile nouns in -ων: plaōn, tōn, daimōn, teutōn [πλάων, τῶν, δαίμων, τεύτων]. But Posidōn and Xenophōn are contracted from Poseidaōn and Xenophaōn [ποσειδῶν, ξενοφῶν, ποσειδάων, ξενοφάων].

units.la: Composita.
units.tr: Compounds.

units.la: Antepenacuūtur huiusmodi compo fita, εὐχαρις, εὔπολις, πολύμητις, ἀναλκις, ξύνυημις. Item ἀδωνις, ἔπηλυς.
units.tr: Compounds of this kind accent the antepenult: eucharis, eupolis, polymētis, analkis, synnoēmis [εὐχαρις, εὔπολις, πολύμητις, ἀναλκις, ξύνυημις]. Likewise adōnis, epēlys [ἀδωνις, ἔπηλυς].

units.la: Neutra.
units.tr: Neuter nouns.

units.la: Neutra primam syllabam accētuant, et αιυ finales semper corripiūt, νόμισμα, σωώπη, ἑλεῦ, πῶυ, γῆρας, σόμα, δῶμα.
units.tr: Neuter nouns accent the first syllable, and final -αι and -υ are always short: money [νόμισμα], silence [σιωπή], ἑλεῦ, flock [πῶυ], old age [γῆρας], mouth [στόμα], house [δῶμα].

units.la: Monosyllaba in υς.
units.tr: Monosyllables in -υς.

units.la: Circunflectuntur monosyllaba in υς, μῦς σῦς, item βῆς, πῦρ, σκαλρ, ἰχθῦς, ὀσφῦς, ὀφρῦς. Et cōtracta τὸ φῶς ἀ φάος (sed ὁ φως uir, incōtractū est) ἐῶξ, ἡρῆς ἀ ἔοαξ, ἡρέας
units.tr: Monosyllables in -υς take the circumflex: mouse [μῦς], pig [σῦς], likewise βῆς, fire [πῦρ], σκαλρ, fish [ἰχθῦς], loin [ὀσφῦς], eyebrow [ὀφρῦς]. Also contracted τὸ φῶς (light) from φάος, but ὁ φώς (man) is not contracted: ἐῶξ, ἡρῆς from ἔοαξ, ἡρέας.

units.la: Quaedam propter uaria significata uarie recipiunt accentus, ut βίος uita, βιός sagitta, πονηρὸς prauus, πόνηρος laboriosus. Nōnulla omnino à communi tramite recedunt, ut χεύσεως χεύσεως, pro χεύσες, ἀργύρεος ἀργυρῆς, ἡ μία, τῆς μιᾶς, τῇ μιᾷ, τὴν μίαν. ὁ ἑαστότης ὢ ἑαστότα, ὁ μητρὸς τῆς ὢ μητρίετα, ἡ θυγάτηρ μήτηρ, τὴ θυγατέρος μητέρ⊙, &c.
units.tr: Some words take different accents according to their various meanings: βίος (life), βιός (arrow), πονηρὸς (wicked), πόνηρος (toilsome). Some depart altogether from the common pattern: χεύσεως for χεύσες; ἀργύρεος, ἀργυρῆς (silver); ἡ μία, τῆς μιᾶς, τῇ μιᾷ, τὴν μίαν (one); ὁ ἑαστότης, ὢ ἑαστότα; ὁ μητρὸς, τῆς μητρίετα; ἡ θυγάτηρ, μήτηρ; τῇ θυγατέρος, μητέρῳ; etc.

units.la: Item secundæ declinationis genitiuus pluralis nominis adiectiui accetum habet genitiui sui masculini tertiæ declinationis existentis, ὁ ἅγιος τῆς ἁγίων, ἡ ἁγία τῆς ἁγίων, non ἁγιαν, apud Pindarum ποντιαῦ pro ποντίων.
units.tr: Likewise the genitive plural of an adjective of the second declension has the accent of the genitive of its masculine, which belongs to the third declension: ὁ ἅγιος, τῆς ἁγίων; ἡ ἁγία, τῆς ἁγίων; not ἁγιῶν. In Pindar, ποντιαῖν stands for ποντίων.

units.la: Masculino tamen existente quarti declinatus, genitiuus fœmininus circumflectit ultimam, ὁ ἡδῦς τῆς ἡδέων, ἡ ἡδεῖα τῆς ἡδειῶν, ὁ μέλας τῆς μελαίνων, ἡ μέλαινα τῆς μελαίνων, ὁ τύπλων τῆς τυπλόντων, ἡ τύπλεσα τῆς τυπλούσῶν. Cæterum substantiua semper genitiuum circumflectunt, ut dictum est in declinatione secunda.
units.tr: But when the masculine belongs to the fourth declension, the feminine genitive circumflexes the last syllable: ὁ ἡδύς, τῆς ἡδέων; ἡ ἡδεῖα, τῆς ἡδειῶν; ὁ μέλας, τῆς μελαίνων; ἡ μέλαινα, τῆς μελαινῶν; ὁ τυφλῶν, τῆς τυφλόντων; ἡ τυφλοῦσα, τῆς τυφλουσῶν. Substantives, however, always circumflex the genitive, as was said in the second declension.

units.la: Insuper nominatiuus pluralis adiectiui fœminini, nominatiuum pluralem masculini sequitur, non suum nominatiuum singularem, ὁ λίθινος, οἱ λίθινοι, ἡ λίθινα, λίθινα αἱ λίθιναι.
units.tr: Moreover, the nominative plural of a feminine adjective follows the nominative plural of the masculine, not its own nominative singular: ὁ λίθινος, οἱ λίθινοι; ἡ λίθινα, αἱ λίθιναι (of stone).

units.la: Quartæ declinationis uocatiuus.
units.tr: Vocative of the fourth declension.

units.la: Quartæ declinationis uocatiuus pro priorum in ης, accentum in antepenulti mam reducit, ὁ ἀεισοτέλνης, ὢ ἀεισοτέλες. ὁ σοφοκλέης, cōtracte ὁ σοφοκλῆς, ὢ σοφόκλε ες, ὢ σοφόκλεις. Sic quorundā in ων uoca-tiuus in ον, ὁ ἀγαμέμνων, ὢ ἀγαμέμνον, ὁ ἡ-κοδαίμων, ὢ κακόδαιμον. Et nominum in ηρ uocatiuus in ερ, ὁ πατὴρ, ὢ πάτερ, ἡ δημή τηρ, Δυγάτηρ, ὢ δλήμητερ, Δύγατερ.
units.tr: The vocative of the fourth declension, in place of the forms in -ης, moves the accent back to the antepenult: ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης, ὦ Ἀριστότελες; ὁ Σοφοκλέης, contracted ὁ Σοφοκλῆς, vocative ὦ Σοφόκλεες or ὦ Σοφόκλεις. So too some nouns in -ων have the vocative in -ον: ὁ Ἀγαμέμνων, ὦ Ἀγάμεμνον; ὁ κακοδαίμων, ὦ κακόδαιμον. And nouns in -ηρ have the vocative in -ερ: ὁ πατήρ, ὦ πάτερ; ἡ Δημήτηρ, θυγάτηρ, ὦ Δημήτερ, θύγατερ.

units.la: Vocatiuus in ὀ.
units.tr: Vocative in -ευ.

units.la: Vocatiuus in ὀ nominū in ὀς circū-flectitur, ὁ βασιλεύς, ὢ βασιλεῦ. Quia ὀ et ῳ diphthongi finales, sī habent accētum, circunflectūtur, φεῦ, παυλαχῷ. præter ἰδῷ.
units.tr: The vocative in -ευ of nouns in -ευς is circumflexed: ὁ βασιλεύς, ὦ βασιλεῦ. Because the final diphthongs -ου and -ῳ, when they carry the accent, are circumflexed: φεῦ, παντᾷ, except ἰδού.

units.la: Ancipites finales.
units.tr: Doubtful final syllables.

units.la: Ancipites finales in obliquis quartædeclinationis corripiūtur. τῷ αὐαντι, τ̔ αὐ-αντα, τοῖς αὐασι, Ῑς αὐανΐας. In obliquis pri mę & secūdę declinationis producūtur, præterɋ in accusatiuo singulari, q semper eiusde tēporis est cū recto τ̔ μῶσαν.
units.tr: Final syllables of doubtful quantity are short in the oblique cases of the fourth declension: τῷ αἰάντι, τ' αἰάντα, τοῖς αἰάσι, τῆς αἰάντιας. In the oblique cases of the first and second declensions they are long, except in the accusative singular, which always has the same quantity as the nominative: τὴν μῶσαν (the Muse).

units.la: Accentus uerborum.
units.tr: Accents of verbs.

units.la: Omne uerbum habens super ultimalonga accentum circunflectitur, τυφθῶ, ἐβη abiecto augmento accentus cadit in ultimam βῇ. præter χεῖ. χεύσεως, αργύρεος αργυρᾶς, ἡ μία, τῆς μιᾶς, τὴ μιᾷ, τὴν μίαν. ὁ ἑαστότης ὦ ἑαστότα, ὁ μητρὶ̈ τῆς ὦ μητρίετα, ἡ θυγάτηρ μήτηρ, ᾗ θυγατέρος μητέρῳ, &c.
units.tr: Every verb with a long final syllable carrying the accent takes the circumflex: τυφθῶ; ἔβην, with the augment dropped, has its accent falling on the last syllable: βῇ, except χεῖ.

units.la: Item secundæ declinationis genitiuus pluralis nominis adiectiui accetum habet genitiui sui masculini tertiæ declinationis existentis, ὁ ἁγιῳ τῆς ἁγίων, ἡ ἁγία τῆς ἁγίων, non ἁγιῶν, apud Pindarum ποντιαῖν pro ποντίων.
units.tr: Likewise the genitive plural of an adjective of the second declension has the accent of the genitive of its masculine, which belongs to the third declension: ὁ ἅγιος, τῆς ἁγίων; ἡ ἁγία, τῆς ἁγίων; not ἁγιῶν. In Pindar, ποντιαῖν stands for ποντίων.

units.la: Masculino tamē existente quarti declinatus, genitiuus fœmininus circūflectit ultimam, ὁ ἡδὺς τῆς ἡδέων, ἡ ἡδεῖα τῆς ἡδεῖαν, ὁ μέλας τῆς μελαίνων, ἡ μέλαινα τῆς μελαίνων, ὁ τύπλων τῆς τυπλόντων, ἡ τύπλωσα τῆς τυπλούσων. Cæterum substantiua semper genitiuum circunflectunt, ut dictum est in declinatione secunda.
units.tr: But when the masculine belongs to the fourth declension, the feminine genitive circumflexes the last syllable: ὁ ἡδύς, τῆς ἡδέων; ἡ ἡδεῖα, τῆς ἡδειῶν; ὁ μέλας, τῆς μελαίνων; ἡ μέλαινα, τῆς μελαινῶν; ὁ τυφλῶν, τῆς τυφλόντων; ἡ τυφλοῦσα, τῆς τυφλουσῶν. Substantives, however, always circumflex the genitive, as was said in the second declension.

units.la: Insuper nominatiuus pluralis adiectiui fœminini, nominatiuum pluralem masculini sequitur, non suum nominatiuum singularem, ὁ λίθινος, οἱ λίθινοι, ἡ λίθινα, λίθιναι.
units.tr: Moreover, the nominative plural of a feminine adjective follows the nominative plural of the masculine, not its own nominative singular: ὁ λίθινος, οἱ λίθινοι; ἡ λίθινα, αἱ λίθιναι (of stone).

units.la: Quartæ declinationis uocatiuus.
units.tr: Vocative of the fourth declension.

units.la: Quartæ declinationis uocatiuus pro priopriorum in ης, accentum in antepenulti mam reducit, ὁ ἀεισοτέλης, ὦ ἀεισότελες. ὁ σοφοκλέης, contracte ὁ σοφοκλῆς, ὦ σοφόκλε ες, ὦ σοφόκλεις. Sic quorundā in ων uoca-tiuus in ον, ὁ ἀγαμέμνων, ὦ ἀγαμέμνον, ὁ κηκοδαίμων, ὦ κηκόδαιμον. Et nominum in ηρ uocatiuus in ερ, ὁ πατὴρ, ὦ πάτερ, ἡ δημή τηρ, θυγάτηρ, ὦ δημήτερ, θύγατερ.
units.tr: The vocative of the fourth declension, in place of the forms in -ης, moves the accent back to the antepenult: ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης, ὦ Ἀριστότελες; ὁ Σοφοκλέης, contracted ὁ Σοφοκλῆς, vocative ὦ Σοφόκλεες or ὦ Σοφόκλεις. So too some nouns in -ων have the vocative in -ον: ὁ Ἀγαμέμνων, ὦ Ἀγάμεμνον; ὁ κακοδαίμων, ὦ κακόδαιμον. And nouns in -ηρ have the vocative in -ερ: ὁ πατήρ, ὦ πάτερ; ἡ Δημήτηρ, θυγάτηρ, ὦ Δημήτερ, θύγατερ.

units.la: Vocatiuus in ὰ.
units.tr: Vocative in -ευ.

units.la: Vocatiuus in ὰ nominū in ὰς circū-flectitur, ὁ βασιλεὺς, ὦ βασιλεῦ. Quia ὰ et ῃ diphthongi finales, si habent accētum, circunflectūtur, φεῦ, παντὰχῇ. præter ἰδ᾽ ἡ.
units.tr: The vocative in -ευ of nouns in -ευς is circumflexed: ὁ βασιλεύς, ὦ βασιλεῦ. Because the final diphthongs -ου and -ῃ, when they carry the accent, are circumflexed: φεῦ, παντᾷ, except ἰδού.

units.la: Ancipites finales.
units.tr: Doubtful final syllables.

units.la: Ancipites finales in obliquis quartæ declinationis corripiūtur. τῷ αἰαντι, τ᾽ αἰ-αντα, τοῖς αἰασι, ἴδς αἰανῖας. In obliquis pri mę & secūdę declinationis producūtur, præterēᵹ in accusatiuo singulari, q sem= per eiusdē tēporis est cū recto ῥ μᾶσαν.
units.tr: Final syllables of doubtful quantity are short in the oblique cases of the fourth declension: τῷ αἰάντι, τ' αἰάντα, τοῖς αἰάσι, τῆς αἰάντιας. In the oblique cases of the first and second declensions they are long, except in the accusative singular, which always has the same quantity as the nominative: τὴν μῶσαν (the Muse).

units.la: Accentus uerborum.
units.tr: Accents of verbs.

units.la: Omne uerbum habens super ultima longa accentum circunflectitur, τυφθῶ, ἴβη abiecto augmento accentus cadit in ultimam βῆ. præter χεῖ.
units.tr: Every verb with a long final syllable carrying the accent takes the circumflex: τυφθῶ; ἔβη, with the augment dropped, has its accent falling on the last syllable: βῇ, except χεῖ.

units.la: Imperatiuus.
units.tr: Imperative.

units.la: Imperatiuus accentum habet in prima, exceptis ἐλθέ, εὑρέ, λαβέ, ἰδέ.
units.tr: The imperative has its accent on the first syllable, except in elthe [ἐλθέ], heure [εὑρέ], labe [λαβέ] and ide [ἰδέ].

units.la: Infinitum α.
units.tr: The infinitive in α.

units.la: Infinitum primū infinitiui actiui habet accentum in penultima, ποιῆσαι, secunda persona infiniti primi imperatiui medij in prima, ποίησαι.
units.tr: The first aorist infinitive active has its accent on the penult, poiēsai [ποιῆσαι]. The second person of the first aorist middle imperative has it on the first syllable, poiēsai [ποίησαι].

units.la: Infinitum α. participij.
units.tr: The participle in α.

units.la: Infinitum primum participij actiui α producit ποιήσας. Itē solū tria participia præsentia ultimam acuunt, ἰὼν, κιὼν, ἐὼν.
units.tr: The first aorist active participle lengthens the α, poiēsas [ποιήσας]. Likewise, only three present participles have an acute on the last syllable: ion [ἰὼν], kion [κιὼν] and eon [ἐὼν].

units.la: Verba Trochaica properispomena non transferunt accentum in compositione, εἶχε, κατέχε, præter οἶδα συνοἶδα, οἶδα συνοἶδα, κεῖμαι, περίκειμαι.
units.tr: Trochaic verbs with a properispomenon accent do not shift the accent in composition: eichë [εἶχε], katechë [κατέχε]. The exceptions are oida [οἶδα], synoida [συνοἶδα], oida, synoida [οἶδα συνοἶδα], keimai [κεῖμαι] and perikeimai [περίκειμαι].

units.la: In cæteris accētus uerborū manifesti sunt ex τύπτω, & aliis exēplis pręscriptis.
units.tr: In other cases, the accents of verbs are clear from typtō [τύπτω] and the other examples given above.

units.la: DE INCLINATIVIS.
units.tr: On Enclitics

units.la: Notio de inclinatiuis.
units.tr: The notion of enclitics

units.la: DICTIONES Græcæ aut nullum habent accentū scriptum, sicut monosyllaba quædam ὁ, εἰ, ὀξ: aut saltem unum αὐτὸς-, duos uero nunquam, nisi alter aduentitius uentitius sit propter dictionem inclina-tiuam sequentem.
units.tr: Greek words either have no written accent, as with certain monosyllables such as ὁ, εἰ and ὀξ, or else they have at least one accent, as αὐτός does, but never two, unless the second accent is added because of a following enclitic word.

units.la: Dictio inclinatiua quid.
units.tr: What an enclitic word is

units.la: Dictio inclinatiua est, quæ proprium accentum transfert in dictionis præce-dentis finalem syllabam, eam scilicet a-cuendo, ut ἥκιστά τινῶ.
units.tr: An enclitic word is one that transfers its own accent onto the final syllable of the preceding word, sharpening it, as in ἥκιστά τινῶ.

units.la: Talis inclinatio fit, quando precedes uocabulū ἀφεσπαρξὺ τόνον, ἀφεσπαρξὺ ἀμμ uov, uel παρεξύτονον troachicū est, ἀρκεσί-λαός τ σωλόν τε, λάμπτε τε. Aristarchus ta-me ut ferūt, ἀνδρα μοι nō ἀνδρά μοι legen-dū censuit, nō commodā ratus inclina-tionem fieri in paroxytono trochaico.
units.tr: This enclisis occurs when the preceding word is barytone, or is a trochaic paroxytone, as in ἀφεσπαρξὺ τόνον, ἀφεσπαρξὺ ἀμμουν, or παρεξύτονον is trochaic, ἀρκεσίλαός τε σωλόν τε, λάμπτε τε. Aristarchus, as they report, thought that ἄνδρα μοι should be read rather than ἀνδρά μοι, judging that enclisis was not appropriate after a trochaic paroxytone.

units.la: Alias inclinatiuū monosyllabum sal- tem propriū accentum amittit, σοφός τις, σοφῶν τε ἀξειδής τε, πάρῳ γε, ὠλένον τε. Si militer bissyllabum præcedente oxyto-no uel perispomeno, καλόν τινα, ξῆν τῷ. alias conseruat, ἀνθρώπου τινός.
units.tr: Otherwise an enclitic monosyllable at least loses its own accent, as in σοφός τις, σοφῶν τε, ἀξειδής τε, πάρῳ γε, ὠλένον τε. After a disyllable that is oxytone or perispomenon, it likewise takes the accent, as in καλόν τινα, ξῆν τῷ. In other cases it keeps its accent, as in ἀνθρώπου τινός.

units.la: Dictiones inclinatiuę sunt ex nomi- nibus τὶς infinitum cum obliquis τινὸς τι νί τινα, &c. ἦλθέ τις καί τινα, sic τοῦ τεῦ pro τινὸς, & τῷ pro τινί, οὔτέ τῳ ἄλλῳ. sed τίς τίνῳ τίνι, &c. cum acuto in prima, interrogatiuũ est, & non inclinat accentū.εἰμὶ & φημί.
units.tr: The enclitic words are the indefinite pronoun τίς with its oblique cases, τινὸς, τι, νί, τινα and so on, as in ἦλθέ τις and καί τινα; likewise τοῦ and τεῦ for τινὸς, and τῷ for τινί, as in οὔτέ τῳ ἄλλῳ. But τίς, τίνος, τίνι and the rest, with an acute on the first syllable, are interrogative and do not take an enclitic accent. The same applies to εἰμί and φημί.

units.la: Ex uerbis εἰμὶ & φημί, cũ reliquis per sonis præsentis, φέρτερός εἰμι, ἀμάρτός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο, μανθάνειόν φησι φησι φασι.
units.tr: Of the verbs εἰμί and φημί, with the other persons of the present tense: φέρτερός εἰμι, ἀμάρτός εἰς ἀγαθοῖο, μανθάνειόν φησι, φησί, φασί.

units.la: Item ἐςι, quando sermonis est initiū, uel aduerbijs ἐν ὡς, uel coniunctionibus ἡ, εἰ, ἀλλὰ, uel pronomini τῶ postponi-tur, tũc nõ inclinat accentū, sed habet in prima, ἐςι πόλις ἐφύρη, ἐν ἐςιν, ὡς ἐςι, ἢ ἐςιν, εἰ ἐςιν, ἀλλ' ἐςι, τῶτο ἐςι. Alias si præcedens dictio apta est, accentū inclinat, οἶκός δςι, κακός ἐςι, ἀκακός ἐςι, ἐρμῆς ἐςι. Si inepta, ac centū, ut par est, habet in ultima, λόγῳ δςι, ἡμέρας δςι, μαντῆς δςι, ἐρῶς δςι. Item φοί-νιξ δςι, non inclinatur, quia spōdeus est, ξ ultimam faciente positione longam.
units.tr: Likewise ἐστί: when it begins a sentence, or follows the adverbs ἐν or ὡς, the conjunctions ἢ, εἰ or ἀλλά, or the pronoun τοῦτο, it does not take an enclitic accent but keeps it on the first syllable, as in ἔστι πόλις, ἐν ἔστιν, ὡς ἔστι, ἢ ἔστιν, εἰ ἔστιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἔστι, τοῦτό ἐστι. Otherwise, if the preceding word is suitable, it takes the accent, as in οἶκός ἐστι, κακός ἐστι, ἀκακός ἐστι, ἑρμῆς ἐστι. If the preceding word is unsuitable, it keeps its accent on the last syllable, as is proper: λόγῳ ἐστί, ἡμέρας ἐστί, μαντις ἐστί, ἔρως ἐστί. Likewise φοῖνιξ ἐστί is not enclitic, because it is a spondee, the ξ making the final syllable long by position.

units.la: Pronomina inclinatiua.
units.tr: Enclitic pronouns

units.la: Pronomina quæ semper inclinantur, sunt μὲ, μοῦ, μοι, τοι, με, μιν, σφιν, σφε, σφωε, κλυθί μοῦ, ἢ γὰρ μοι, καί τοι, καί με. Quæ mo do absolute sumuntur, & proprium accentum inclinant, modo Emphatice & non inclinât, sunt hæc, σε, τοῦ, σέο, σοι, σὲ, σὲ, εὖ, οἱ, ἑ, ἑθεν, σφί, σφων, σφισι, σφεας, ἡκου-σά σε. σάσυ, audiui te simpliciter: σῦ ἤκουσα, te audiuí non alium.
units.tr: These pronouns are always enclitic: μὲ, μοῦ, μοι, τοι, με, μιν, σφιν, σφε, σφωε, as in κλυθί μοῦ, ἢ γάρ μοι, καί τοι, καί με. Those which are sometimes used absolutely and take their own accent, and sometimes are emphatic and not enclitic, are these: σε, τοῦ, σέο, σοι, σέ, σέ, εὖ, οἱ, ἑ, ἕθεν, σφί, σφῶν, σφισι, σφέας. Thus ἤκουσά σε means "I heard you" simply, whereas σὲ ἤκουσα means "I heard you", not someone else.

units.la: Aduerbia interrogādi bissyllaba accen tum habent in penultima, & non inclínant, facta uero infinita in ultima, & in-clinant, πόθεν; unde? ποθὲν alicunde. πόθεν ἥλθες; ἦλθόν ποτε.
units.tr: Interrogative disyllabic adverbs have the accent on the penult and are not enclitic; when made indefinite, with the accent on the final syllable, they become enclitic: πόθεν; whence? ποθέν, from somewhere. πόθεν ἦλθες; ἦλθόν ποτε.

units.la: Similiter monosyllaba interrogati-ua proprium accentum seruant, infinita inclinant, πῶς οἴδλας; οἰδάπως, sic πῇ που πῶ, & si sunt alia.
units.tr: Similarly, monosyllabic interrogatives keep their own accent, while the indefinite forms are enclitic: πῶς οἶδας; οἶδά πως; so too πῇ, που, πώ, and others of this kind.

units.la: Ex coniunctionibus inclinatiuę sunt τε κεν κε γε γαρ νυ νυν pro δή, περ θεῶ ρα. Particula δὲ.
units.tr: Among the conjunctions the enclitics are τε, κεν, κε, γε, γαρ, νυ, νυν (for δή), περ, θεν and ρα.

units.la: Etiam δ᾽ε quando cum articulis diui-siuum patitur apostrophū, ὁ μὴν, ὁ δ᾽ε, uel οδ᾽, οἱ δ᾽ε οἱ δ᾽τῶ δ᾽ετῶ δ᾽, &c.
units.tr: The particle δέ too: when it is separated from the articles by an apostrophe, as in ὁ μὲν, ὁ δέ, or ὁδ᾽, οἱ δέ, οἱ δ᾽τῶ, δ᾽ετῶ, and so on.

units.tr: CONCERNING THE ANOMALOUS VERBS, LETTER 23.

units.la: Γαμαι μέλλων ἀγάσομαι, ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀ= Miror. γάζω. ἀόεις ἀ. ἠγάθλω. μέσος ἀόρ. α. ἠγασάμην.
units.tr: Agamai, I wonder at (Latin Miror): future agasomai, from agazō; aorist ēgasamēn, middle aorist.

units.la: Ἀγω. μ. ἄξω. ἀδρεῖμυος ἦχα. Ago. ηκὴ ἀτλικῶς ἀγήοχα. ἀόρ. β. ἤγον, ἀτ. ἤαγον.
units.tr: Ago, I lead: future axō; perfect ēcha, and in the Attic form ēgēoxa; second aorist ēgon, Attic ēagon.

units.la: Αζω. ἀόρ. α. ἄαθλων ηκὴ ἀάθλων.
units.tr: Azō: first aorist āathlōn, also ēathlōn.

units.la: Αγνυμι. μέλ. ἄξω. παρ. ἦχα. ἀτ. ἀγήοχα. ἀόρ. α. ἔαξα, ὅθεν τὸ κατέαξα. μέσω ἔαγα. ἦγα ἄχρηςα. ὅθεν ἔαγα ἀτ. ἐξ ἔ τὸ κατέαγα.
units.tr: Agnymi. Future [ἄξω]. Perfect [ἦχα]; Attic perfect [ἀγήοχα]. First aorist [ἔαξα], whence [κατέαξα]. Middle perfect [ἔαγα]. [ἦγα] is not in use, whence the Attic [ἔαγα] and [κατέαγα], formed from [ἔ].

units.la: Αγορεύω. μέλ. ἀγορεύσω. ἀόρ. α. ἠγόρευσα. ἔαγα. εἴρηκα, ἀπὸ τὸ εἶπον.
units.tr: Agoreuō, I speak in the assembly: future agoreusō; first aorist ēgoreusa; eaga, eirēka, from eipon.

units.la: Ἀδω. μέλ. ἄσω. ἀόρ. α. ἤσα.
units.tr: Adō, I sing: future asō; first aorist ēsa.

units.la: Αἱρῶ. μέλ. αἱρήσω. ἀόρ. β. εἶλον, ἀπὸ τὸ ἕλω ἀχρῆσα.
units.tr: Hairō, I take: future hairēsō; second aorist eilon, from helō, which is unused.

units.la: Αἱρέομαι. μέλ. αἱρήσομαι. παρ. ἥρημαι. ἀόρ. α. ἡρέθην. μέσω ἀόρ. β. εἰλόμην, ἀπὸ τὸ ἕλομαι ἀχρῆσα.
units.tr: Haireomai, I choose: future hairēsomai; perfect hērēmai; first aorist hairethēn; middle second aorist eilomēn, from helomai, which is unused.

units.la: Αἰσθάνομαι. μέλ. αἰσθήσομαι. παρ. ἤσθημαι. μέσω ἀόρ. β. ἠσθόμην, ἀπὸ τὸ αἰσθέομαι αἰσθῆμαι ἀχρῆσα. (ἀχρῆσα.
units.tr: Aisthanomai, I perceive: future aisthēsomai; perfect ēsthēmai; middle second aorist ēsthomēn, from aistheomai; aisthēmai is unused.

units.la: Ἀλέξω. μ. ἀλεξήσω, ἀπὸ τ' ἀλεξέω ἀλεξῶ
units.tr: Alexō, I defend: future alexēsō, from alexeō, alexō.

units.la: Ἀλίσκομαι. μέλ. ἁλώσομαι. ἀόρ. ϛ. ἥλων, ἥλως. ἥλω. ηκὴ ἑάλων ἀτ. παρὰ τὸ ἁλόω ἁλῶ. ἁλῶμι, ὅθεν ἡ μεζχὴ, ὁ ἁλὲς τὲ ἁλόντω.
units.tr: Haliskomai, I am taken: future halōsomai; first aorist ēlōn, ēlōs, ēlō; Attic ealōn, from halaō, halō, halōmi, whence the participle hals, halontōi.

units.la: Ἁμαρτάνω. μέλ. ἁμαρτήσω. παρ. ἡμάρτη κα. ἀόρ. β. ἥμαρτον, ἀπὸ τὸ ἁμαρτέω ἁμαρτῶ ἀ- χρῆσα.
units.tr: Hamartanō, I sin: future hamartēsō; perfect hēmartēka; second aorist hēmarton, from hamarteō, hamartō, which is unused.

units.la: Ἀμφιςἰννυμι. μέλ. ἀμφιέσω. παρ. πεθη- πικὸς ἡμφίεσμαι.
units.tr: Amphiennymi, I clothe: future amphiesō; perfect passive ēmphiesmai.

units.la: Ἀνοίγω
units.tr: Anoigō.

units.la: Ανοίγω. μέλ. ἀνοίξω. ἀόρ. α. ἀνέῳξα. μέσος. Ϙᾱαι. ἀνέῳγα. παθητικὸς Ϙᾱαι. ἀνεῳγμαι. ἀόρ. α. ἀνεῴχθην.
units.tr: Anoigō, I open: future anoixō; first aorist aneōxa; middle ōai, aneōga; passive ōai, aneōgmai; first aorist passive aneōchthēn.

units.la: Ἀναγινώσκω, παθητικὸς ἀνεγίνωσκον. μέλ. ἀναγνώσομαι. παρακ. ἀνέγνωκα. ἀόρ. β. ἀνέγνων, ἀπὸ τ ἀναγνόω ῶ, ἀνάγνωσμι ἀχρὴς ϰ.
units.tr: Anaginōskō, I read; imperfect passive anegignōskon. Future anagnōsomai; perfect anegnōka; second aorist anegnōn, from anagnoō, anagnōsmi, which is unused.

units.la: Ἀναῤῥηγνύω ἢ ἀναῤῥήγνυμι. μέλλων ἀναῤ ῥήξω, ἀπὸ τὸ ἀναῤῥήγω.
units.tr: Anarrēgnyō or anarrēgnymi, I break up: future anarrēxō, from anarrēgō.

units.la: Ἀπεχθανόμαι. μέλ. ἀπεχθήσομαι. παρακ. ἀπήχθημαι. μέσος. ἀόρ. β. ἀπηχθόμην, ἀπὸ τ ἀπεχθέομαι, ἔμαγ, ἀχρὴς ϰ.
units.tr: Apechthanomai, I am hated: future apechthēsomai; perfect apēchthēmai; middle second aorist apēchthomēn, from apechtheomai, emag, which is unused.

units.la: Αὐξάνω, ἢ αὔξω, μ. αὐξήσω, ἀόρ. α. ἠὔξησα.
units.tr: Auxanō, or auxō, I increase: future auxēsō; first aorist ēuxēsa.

units.la: Ἀπόχρη. μέλ. ἀποχρήσω, ἀόρ. α. ἀπέχρησα, ἀπὸ τὸ ἀποχρέω παλαιῶ.
units.tr: Apochrē, I suffice: future apochrēsō; first aorist apechrēsa, from apochreō, palaiō.

units.la: Ἀναζυγνύω. μέλ. ἀναζεύξω.
units.tr: Anazygnyō, I unyoke: future anazeuxō.

units.la: Ἀνακράζω. μέλ. ἀνακράξω. μέσος παρακ. ἀνακέκραγα. ἀόρ. β. ἀνέκραγον.
units.tr: Anakrazō, I cry out: future anakrazō; middle perfect anekekraga; second aorist anekragon.

units.la: Ἀναπνέω. μ. ἀναπνεύσω. ἀόρ. ἀνέπνευσα. ἀπὸ τ ἀναπνεύω παλαιῶ.
units.tr: Anapneō, I breathe: future anapneusō; aorist anepneusa, from anapneuō, palaiō.

units.la: Ἀναμιμνήσκω. ἀναμνήσω. ἀόρ. α. ἐμνήσθην.
units.tr: Anamimnēskō, I remind: future anamnēsō; first aorist emnēsthēn.

units.la: Ἀπαναίνομαι. ἀόρ. ἀπηρνησάμην.
units.tr: Apanainomai, I deny: aorist apērnēsamēn.

units.la: Αλίσκομαι. μ. α. ληφθήσομαι. ἀπὸ τ λήβομαι ληψομαι ἑλήφθην. ἀόρ. β. ἑάλων ἀπὸ τ ἁλόω. ῶ
units.tr: Haliskomai, I am taken: future passive lēphthēsomai, from lēbomai, lēpsomai, elēphthēn; second aorist ealōn, from halaō.

units.la: Αντιτρέφω. μέλ. ἀντιτρέψω. μέσος. παρακ. ἀντέτροφα. Explico. | Ἀναπετάννυω καὶ ἀναπετάννυμι. μέλλων ἀναπετάσω. Perdo. | Ἀπολέω. λῶ. ἡ ἀπολλύω, ἡ ἀπόλλυμι. μέλ. ἀπολῶ, ἀπὸ τῆς ἀπόλλω, καὶ ἀπολέσω, ῥαρ. ἀπώλεσα, ἡ ἀπ' ἀπωλώλεκα. ἡ μέσῳ ῥαρ. ἀπώλεσα, ἀπλικῶς ἀπόλωλα. Recipio. | Ἀπέχω. μέλλων ἀφέξω. ῥαρ. ἀπέσχηκα. ἀόρ. β. ἀπέσχον. Aufugio. | Ἀποδιδράσκω. μέλ. ἀποδράσω. ἀόρ. α. ἀπέδρα. τὸ α. τῆς πληθυντικῶν ἀπέδραμεν, ἀπέδραν, ἡ μετοχὴ ὁ ἀποδράς. Ostendo. | Ἀποδεικνύω ἡ ἀποδείκνυμι. μέλ. ἀποδείξω, ἀπὸ τὸ ἀποδείκω. Extinguo | Ἀποσβεννύω καὶ ἀποσβέννυμι. μέλ. ἀποσβέσω. ἀόρ. β. ἀπέσβλω. Abscindo | Ἀποτέμνω, μ. ἀποτεμῶ ἡ ἀποτμήσω. ἀόρ. β. ἀπέτεμον. Priuo. | Ἀπαυράω. ῶ, ἀόεις ἀπῆνεγα. Extendo. | Ἀποτανύω. μέλλων ἀποτάσω. Deploro. | Ἀποκλαίω. μέλ. ἀποκλαύσω, ἀπὸ τ' κλαύω παλαιῶ. Placeo. | Ἀρέσκω. μέλ. ἀρέσω, ἡ τὸ ἀφεσόσωπον ἀρέσει, ῥαρ. ταπικὸς ἤρεσκε, ab ἀρέω. Inhonoro | Ἀτίζω. μ. ἀτίξω. Peruenio | Ἀφικνοῦμαι. μ. ἀφίξωμαι. ῥαρ. ἀφῖμαι.
units.tr: Antitrephō, I turn back: future antitrepsō; middle perfect antetropha. Explico, I unfold: Anapetannyō and anapetannymi, future anapetasō. Perdo, I destroy: Apoleō, apolō, Apollyō, Apollymi; future apolō, from apollō, and apolesō; perfect apōlesa, and apōlōleka; middle perfect apōlesa, and in the simple form apōlōla. Recipio, I receive: Apechō, future apexō; perfect apeschēka; second aorist apeschon. Aufugio, I flee away: Apodidraskō, future apodrasō; first aorist apedra; the plural first aorist apedramen, apedran; participle apodras. Ostendo, I show: Apodeiknyō or apodeiknymi, future apodeixō, from apodeikō. Extinguo, I quench: Aposbennyō and aposbennymi, future aposbesō; second aorist aepesbon. Abscindo, I cut off: Apotemnō, future apotemō or apotmēsō; second aorist apetemon. Privo, I deprive: Apauraō, aōs, apēnenga. Extendo, I stretch out: Apotanyō, future apotasō. Deploro, I lament: Apoklaiō, future apoklausō, from klauō, palaiō. Placeo, I please: Areskō, future aresō; the impersonal aphesoson aresei; imperfect ēresken, from areō. Inhonoro, I dishonour: Atizō, future atixō. Perveniō, I arrive: Aphiknoumai, future aphixomai; perfect aphimai.

units.la: μέσῳ ἀόρ. ἀφικόμιλν.
units.tr: Middle second aorist aphikomēn.

units.la: Αφίπαμαι. μ. ἀποπήσομαι. ἀόεισος β. ἀ- πέπλιν. μέσῳ ἀπεπάμιλν.
units.tr: Aphipamai, future apopēsomai; second aorist apepēn; middle apepamēn.

units.la: Αχθομαι. μέλλων ἀχθήσομαι, ἢ ἀχθέσομαι ἀόρ. α. ἠχθέσθην.
units.tr: Achthomai, I am vexed: future achthēsomai or achthesomai; first aorist ēchthesthēn.

units.la: Αχω. ϖδακ. ἤαχεν.
units.tr: Achō, I grieve: imperfect ēachen.

units.la: Βάλλω. μέλ. βαλῶ. ϖδακ. βέβληκα. ἀόρ. ἔβαλον. ἀπὸ βλῶ ἐλήσω.
units.tr: Ballō, I throw: future balō; perfect beblēka; aorist ebalon, from blō, elēsō.

units.la: Βαίνω. μέλλων βήσομαι. ἀόρ. β. ἔβην, ἀπὸ τῆ βῆμι ἀχρήσω.
units.tr: Bainō, I go: future bēsomai; second aorist ebēn, from bēmi, which is unused.

units.la: Βλαστάνω, μέλ. βλαστήσω. ἀόρ. β. ἔβλαστον.
units.tr: Blastanō, I sprout: future blastēsō; second aorist eblaston.

units.la: Βούλομαι. μέλ. βουλήσομαι. ϖδακ. βεβού- λημαι ἐβεβουλήμην, ἐβουλήθην.
units.tr: Boulomai, I wish: future boulēsomai; perfect bebouleumai, ebebouleumēn, ebouleuthēn.
